# Multi-source SI network — Plan S3-A: stage-3 P0 hazards and guards, code layer Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Close the hazards stage 3 must not build on, with no consensus change: HouseGate refuses every peer-trusted mention of a protocol database (including the four stage-3 member databases); an owner SNode audits its `hg_safe` against the acknowledged inventory before every promotion and after every ClickHouse restart, and in repair mode drops resurrected twins and holds unclean tables Pending; the arbiter serves three leader-barriered reads that later phases need (partition states, promotion outcomes, block verification), lets `arbiter-admin` take an issuance hold or a drain before signing a consensus update, exposes the consensus-state size and snapshot timings as gauges, and opens ClickHouse with credentials; and a ClickHouse mechanics suite pins every measured behaviour stage 3 relies on.

**Architecture:** housegate reserves the member databases, lets a Pending table keep its schema, and adds a peer rule to `sireserved` with a regression corpus of every legitimate peer leg (Tasks 1–2). arbiter-proto adds the three `SafeState` reads and three `ConsensusAdmin` hold RPCs, none Raft-reachable (Task 3). arbiter-core adds wire types, client methods and a credentialed test opener (Task 4), the owner audit with ClickHouse restart detection (Task 5), and the mechanics suite (Task 6). arbiter adds FSM read views and the read handlers (Task 7), the issuance hold, drain mode and their `arbiter-admin` flow (Task 8), the state-size and snapshot gauges (Task 9), ClickHouse credentials in its startup path (Task 10), and an integration proof (Task 11). Plan S3-B (`2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3b-p0-hosts-rollout.md`) puts it to work on sentio-node, production and devnet2 and carries the ClickHouse lockdown and the enrolment of indexer-c.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.26; protobuf + buf (arbiter-proto); Bazel 9.1.0 + Bzlmod + gazelle (housegate, arbiter-core, arbiter); hashicorp/raft + raft-boltdb; ClickHouse 26.3 (`clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` for CI and the release gate, `26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16` for the manual deployed-image run); Prometheus client_golang.

**Spec:** housegate `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` (branch `urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-spec`, commit `54c01a3`, PR housegate#236) — binding, as clarified by *Plan clarifications* below. This plan implements the P0 row of §16 for the code repositories: §13.1 (state-growth guards), §14 bullets 1–2 (peer-trusted guard, owner `hg_safe` audit), the credentials half of §14 bullet 3, the read RPCs and the issuance hold of §15, and §10.1–§10.2's issuance hold and leader drain mode. The umbrella spec `2026-10-10-multi-source-si-network-design.md` and Plans S1-A, S1-B, S2-A and S2-B stay in force wherever this plan does not replace them.

**Base revisions.** Line anchors in the tasks refer to housegate `66d4df7` (v0.19.0), arbiter-proto `1c6ae67` (v0.11.0), arbiter-core `8f0bc43` (v0.14.1), arbiter `fb42260` (v0.12.0), sentio-node `5d2f169`, production `eba93300a`. devnet2 (read 2026-10-14): epoch 5, tracks enabled with cutover 60/52, `si_indexers` {0: `snode-1`, 1: `snode-2`}, verifiers `verifier-1..3`, `max_writers` 2, snapshot v20, voters at 2Gi memory and 2Gi PVC.

## Global Constraints

- **No consensus change.** Appendix A §0 is binding: no Raft command, Raft tag, Raft-reachable field, snapshot version, header byte or feature string changes. A replay of the devnet2 voters' logs under arbiter `v0.12.0` and `ARBITER_TAG` yields identical state digests, and the new binary writes v20 snapshots that `v0.12.0` restores. Every component can be rolled back to its previous image.
- **Stages 1 and 2 stay in force.** Every Global Constraint of Plans S1-A and S2-A applies unless a line below replaces it (strict decoder, request-only signatures, signed-claims and tracks rules, golden files, worktrees, commits, remote actions).
- **arbiter-proto numbers and names:** Appendix A §1, verbatim. The P0 `PROTO_TAG` carries only these additions: no v21 field (a new `VerifierEntry` or parameter field would break arbiter-core's `assertMirror` checks).
- **Reserved databases** (housegate): `[hg_safe hg_unsafe hg_promote hg_member_unsafe hg_replica hg_rstage hg_xfer]`, in that order; nothing creates the last four in this plan.
- **Peer rule** (housegate): on peer-trusted, non-forwarded sessions every mention of a reserved database or of `_hg_row_id`, string literals included, and every `{x:Identifier}` placeholder is refused with 392; operator sessions keep today's rules; ordinary and forwarded sessions are unchanged.
- **Owner audit:** report mode is the default and never drops a part or gates a table; repair mode drops resurrected equal-hash twins without an acknowledged name with `DROP PART` and holds an unclean table not-ready (sentio-node answers Pending, 733). The reference is the newer of the SNode's own acknowledged inventory and the FSM's `SafeParts`.
- **Reads** are `SafeState` methods on the data-plane listener, one leader read barrier each, with every shape refusal before the barrier (Appendix A §4).
- **Holds** are leader-local: an issuance hold freezes `PromotionSeq` by refusing every `RecordPromotionIssued`; a drain finishes every block at or below each track's recorded frontier and starts no later one. Both are authorised by a draft `UpdateConsensusParamsCmd` checked exactly like `UpdateConsensusParams`, carry a bearer hold id, and clear on commit, refusal, release, timeout or leadership loss. `arbiter-admin consensus update` defaults to `--hold drain`.
- **State size** is exported only as gauges (Appendix A §4); the 1 GiB read cap is unchanged; the writer never refuses a snapshot.
- **ClickHouse credentials:** YAML carries only a username; a password comes only from the environment variable named in Appendix A §4–§5; an empty username keeps today's passwordless connection byte for byte.
- **Never edit existing golden or vector files:** everything Plans S1-A and S2-A list. New frozen fixtures: the conformance ledgers of Task 3.
- **Repository commands, worktrees, commits, releases:** Appendix A §6. Remote and live actions require explicit user confirmation in chat; commands handed to the user are fish.
- **Hunks are anchored on the base revisions.** Tasks were drafted in parallel; when a later task's hunk overlaps an earlier task's edit, apply the later intent on top of the earlier change. The contract and the named tests are binding; line anchors are guidance.
- **References.** `contract §N` points to Appendix A of this plan (binding for Plan S3-B too); `S2 contract §N` points to Plan S2-A's Appendix A; a task group's "Facts" point to Appendix B; Appendix C records the release ledger values and the run records as they are made.

## Plan clarifications (binding)

The spec leaves these P0 details open; each is resolved here and binding for Plans S3-A and S3-B.

- **K1 — Owner-audit modes (spec §14).** The spec says the audit "ships report-only first" and that "while it is unclean the host answers the owner's SI tables Pending". Resolution: two modes. `report` (the default) audits, logs at error level and counts, but never drops a part and never gates; `repair` drops resurrected twins and gates an unclean table. The Pending answer applies in repair mode only, so a false positive in the first soak cannot take a table offline.
- **K2 — Repair drops with `DROP PART` (spec §14, §2).** Measured on upstream 26.3: after a restart resurrects the parts a `REPLACE PARTITION` retired, `ALTER TABLE ... DROP PART` of each resurrected twin leaves exactly the replacement parts active, leaves no active zero-row part, and the dropped parts stay dropped across a second restart (`DETACH PART` followed by `DROP DETACHED PART` behaves the same). M11 pins this on the deployed image.
- **K3 — An unreachable FSM does not gate (spec §14).** If `GetPartitionStates` fails, the audit uses the SNode's own acknowledged inventory and counts `fsm_unavailable`; only a partition with no reference at all is unclean (`no_acknowledged_inventory`). The owner's read availability is therefore not coupled to the arbiter's.
- **K4 — An unresolved promotion intent is reported, not repaired (spec §14).** A partition whose promotion intent has not converged is skipped and reported `unresolved_intent`; its repair is a runbook step (Plan S3-B) until a later design.
- **K5 — Hold authorisation (spec §10.1).** A hold is authorised by a draft `UpdateConsensusParamsCmd` that the leader checks with the same validator as `UpdateConsensusParams` and never proposes; in issuance mode the draft is the update to submit, so one signature suffices. No new signing purpose exists. The hold id is a random 128-bit bearer capability returned only to the caller; `GetConsensusHold` and `ReleaseConsensusHold` need only the id. It travels as gRPC metadata `arbiter-consensus-hold`, never inside the Raft command.
- **K6 — Drain is the default (spec §10.2).** An issuance hold alone can wait forever on a half-promoted multi-partition frontier block, because its cleanup waits for publication; `arbiter-admin consensus update` therefore defaults to `--hold drain` until the narrowed drain gate exists.
- **K7 — Exact `expected_promotion_seq` (spec §10.1).** `PromotionSeq` advances only through `RecordPromotionIssued`, which has one producer (`arbiter:orchestrator/promotion.go:152`). The orchestrator holds a shared issuance lease from its `PromotionSeq` read through the proposal; a hold takes the lease exclusively before reading the sequence it returns.
- **K8 — State size has no RPC (spec §13.1).** The spec asks for gauges; an `arbiter-admin state size` RPC is not added. Operators read the gauges.
- **K9 — The deployed image runs the mechanics by hand (spec §16 P0).** The spec asks for the mechanics "pinned in CI on the deployed image". The deployed image (`us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16`) is private and arbiter-core's CI is public, so CI and the release gate run the suite on the exact upstream patch `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` (not the floating `26.3` tag), and the deployed image runs it by hand before Plan S3-B rolls anything (Task 6). Making it a CI job needs a read-only registry secret that an administrator provides; that is a follow-up.
- **K10 — Hold readiness (spec §10.1–§10.2).** A hold of either mode is `ready` only once the stage-2 drain gate passes; an ISSUANCE hold issues no promotion meanwhile, so it can expire on a half-promoted multi-partition block (K6).

## Review Focus

1. **A ClickHouse restart inside the outdated-part window on an owner.** The parts a `REPLACE PARTITION` retired come back active. Expected: in report mode the audit logs and counts the finding, drops nothing and keeps the table served; in repair mode it drops exactly the resurrected twins, holds the table not-ready (Pending on the host) until the audit is clean, and the next promotion of the partition succeeds; a partition whose promotion intent has not converged is reported `unresolved_intent` and left alone. Tests: Task 5 `TestOwnerAuditRepairsResurrectedPartsAcrossAClickHouseRestart`, `TestOwnerAuditReportModeNeverDropsOrHoldsBack`, `TestOwnerAuditRepairDropsResurrectedTwinsBeforeTheShadow`, `TestOwnerAuditSkipsAPartitionWithAnUnresolvedIntent`; Task 6 M3 and M11.
2. **The audit cannot reach the arbiter, or the arbiter does not serve the reads yet.** Expected: the audit falls back to the SNode's own acknowledged inventory, counts `fsm_unavailable` once per pass, and never holds a table for that reason alone (K3); when the arbiter's inventory is newer it wins; when the FSM is ahead of the local journal nothing is dropped and the partition is unclean. Tests: Task 5 `TestOwnerAuditPassAsksAFailingArbiterOnce`, `TestOwnerAuditTakesTheArbitersInventoryWhenItIsNewer`, `TestOwnerAuditFSMAheadIsUncleanAndDropsNothing`.
3. **A consensus update under continuous writes on two tracks, with a multi-partition block half promoted.** Expected: a drain hold keeps issuing promotions for blocks at or below each track's recorded frontier, refuses only later blocks, becomes ready, and the update signed with the reported `promotion_seq` commits on its first attempt; the hold then ends `committed` and promotion resumes; a hold expires on its timeout and clears on a leadership change. Tests: Task 11 `TestDrainModeUpdateCommitsUnderContinuousWrites`; Task 8 `TestDrainModeAdmitsEveryPromotionAtOrBelowTheFrontier` (two partitions of the frontier block and a re-issue of one), `TestDrainModeReadyOnlyWhenEveryTrackPassedItsFrontier`, `TestHoldExpiresAfterItsTimeout`, `TestHoldClearsOnLeadershipLoss`, `TestIssuanceLeaseSpansThePromotionSeqReadAndTheProposal`.
4. **A legitimate cross-indexer read after `HG_TAG`.** The rewriter's `remote()` loopback legs reach the peer as peer-trusted, non-forwarded sessions. Expected: every leg form the rewriter emits passes; a leg that names a reserved database, `_hg_row_id` or an `{x:Identifier}` placeholder is refused with 392 and counted; operator sessions keep today's rules; forwarded sessions are not peer-checked. Tests: Task 2 `TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsPass`, `TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsWithAReservedNameAreRefused`, `TestPeerReservedGuard_MeasuredRemoteSecondaryQueriesPass`, `TestPeerReservedGuard_RemoteLeftJoinOfALocalSITableIsRefused`, `TestOnQuery_PeerSessionWithAnOperatorFlagKeepsTheOperatorRules`, `TestOnQuery_ForwardedFromPeerSessionsAreNotPeerChecked`.
5. **A ClickHouse login is misconfigured.** Expected: a password key in YAML is refused at load, a password without a username is refused, an empty username sends exactly today's passwordless hello, the schema-retry reconnect keeps the login, and the password never appears in printed configuration or logs. Tests: Task 10 `TestLoadConfig_RefusesAClickHousePasswordKey`, `TestLoadConfig_RefusesAClickHousePasswordWithoutAUsername`, `TestOpenClickHouse_WithoutAUserSendsTodaysHello`, `TestResetForSchemaRetryKeepsTheLogin`, `TestPrintedConfigCarriesNoClickHousePassword`, `TestClickHouseAuthRedactsThePassword`.

## Follow-ups (not in this plan)

- rewriter-go renders an `ActionRemote` IN operand as a bare `x IN remote(...)`, which ClickHouse 25.8 and 26.3 refuse at the initiator (code 46); an IN against a remote-mapped logical database is broken today and needs a rewriter-go issue (Appendix B, G1).
- The peer guards' warn logs carry the refused statement, which can include a nested `remote()`'s peer-hello envelope and peer-relay JWS; redact carrier credentials in `sireserved` and `sipeerguard` in a later change.
- A reserved name computed by a carrier argument (`merge(concat('hg_', 'replica'), …)`) is not refused on peer sessions; Plan S3-B's ClickHouse lockdown grants close it, and stage 3 P3 (members serving reads) must revisit it.
- A CI job for the mechanics suite on the deployed image needs a read-only registry secret from an administrator (K9).
- An unresolved promotion intent found by the audit has no automatic repair (K4); Plan S3-B's runbook carries the operator step.
- `consensus_admin.max_issuance_hold` is not validated against `max_token_age`; a GetConsensusHold poll crosses one read barrier per second for the life of a drain hold.
- The narrowed drain gate, checkpoints, groups and everything else of stage 3 beyond P0: Plans S3-C to S3-F.

## Task 1: housegate — reserved member databases and a Pending table that keeps its schema (S3-A)

Spec §14 bullet 1 and contract §2 bullets 1–2. Stage 3 gives every SI indexer host three new protocol databases owned by the `si-member` process — `hg_member_unsafe` (its ReplicatedMergeTree replicas of an owner's unsafe tables), `hg_replica` (its verified copies) and `hg_rstage` (install and replay scratch, spec §8.1) — and reserves `hg_xfer`. Today `sitable.ReservedDatabases()` returns only `hg_safe`, `hg_unsafe` and `hg_promote` (`pkg/sitable/sitable.go:145-147`), so a tenant statement could name the member databases and the engines would not protect them. Every consumer reads the one function — the engines' `reserved_databases` (`pkg/rewriter/storage_integrity.go:175`) and `protected_databases` (`pkg/rewriter/args.go:67-79`), `tablerefguard` G1 (`build.go:736-741`), `sireserved` (`build.go:709-715`), the exception scrubber (`pkg/rewriter/storage_integrity.go:297-314`), the ingress `DROP TABLE` check (`pkg/plugins/storageintegrity/plugin.go:849`) and the operator warnings (`build.go:1907-1911`) — so appending the four names to that function is the whole code change; only the tests that pin the list by literal move.

Spec §14 bullet 2 (the owner audit, Tasks 5 and S3-B): in repair mode the host answers an unclean owner's SI tables Pending (733, retryable). sentio-node already maps "Active but not ready" to a schema-less Pending (`sentio-node:storageintegrityadapter/tablestate/snapshot.go:186-188`), which produces the spec's client refusal with no HouseGate change. What it loses is the schema: `tableStateSchemaResolver` (`storage_integrity_runtime.go:241-249`) resolves journal recovery and cleanup through `Snapshot.Schema`, which misses a Pending table, so a non-terminal legacy record (no journaled `TouchedPartitionIDs`) of a table that a restart finds held fails recovery with `ErrStorageIntegrityRecoverySchemaPurged`. The contract therefore lets a Pending table carry its schema, exactly like the stage-2 quarantined Refused table (clarification C13): `Snapshot.Schema` answers it when `Schema.TableID != ""`, `NewSnapshot` / `Fake` support it, and the client message and every status decision stay byte-identical.

Notes:
- **Order is part of the contract.** The four names are appended, so `ReservedDatabases()[0]` stays `hg_safe`, every operator message built by `reservedDatabaseNames()` (`build.go:1910`) still starts with `hg_safe / hg_unsafe / hg_promote`, and `protectedDatabases` (`pkg/rewriter/args.go:67-79`) stays "physical first, then every reserved database except a duplicate of physical".
- **The leaf-package rule stays.** `pkg/sitable` must not import `pkg/config` (which imports `pkg/rewriter`). `pkg/config` keeps its three Spec C D2 constants; the member databases exist only in `pkg/sitable`, and `TestSitablePhysicalNamesMatchConfig` pins them by literal (contract §2).
- **Engines need no change.** Both engines accept any simple-identifier entry in `reserved_databases` and `protected_databases` (rewriter-go `internal/nameresolve/resolve.go:511-516`, `protected.go:15-30`; rewriter `src/handlers/storage_integrity.cc:927-931`); the startup probes (`pkg/rewriter/probe.go:83-103`) now send seven names, and the probe answers do not depend on the list. The PR's `Integration (ClickHouse)` job runs the native engine (FFI `v0.17.0`) and proves it.
- **Blast radius beyond SI.** `tablerefguard` (enforce by default, wired on every ClickHouse-forwarding server) and `protected_databases` (sent on every request, SI or not) read the same list, so after this release any ordinary tenant statement that mentions `hg_member_unsafe`, `hg_replica`, `hg_rstage` or `hg_xfer` — as a database, table, column or inside a string literal — is refused, as `hg_safe` already is. Plan S3-B's rollout runs the read-only preflight (`system.databases`, `system.tables`, `system.columns` and the registry's logical databases for these four names on every SI ClickHouse) before any host takes `HG_TAG`.
- **Pending with a schema changes no decision.** `sitablestate` switches on the status (`pkg/plugins/sitablestate/plugin.go:104-113`: Pending reads and writes get 733 `storage_integrity: table <id> is pending activation (retryable)`, pinned in `pkg/chproto/client_error_test.go:55`, `pkg/plugins/sitablestate/plugin_test.go:86`, `pkg/proxy/relay_reject_test.go:525` and `pkg/integration/storage_integrity_table_state_test.go:169-171`); `snapshotSchema` (`pkg/plugins/storageintegrity/plugin.go:1078-1095`) switches on `Lookup`'s status first, so the signed lane still refuses a held table; `buildStorageIntegrityArgs`, the scrubber and `requireActiveAccessedIDs` read only `Active()`; the agent's `sistatement` claims only `status == "active"` (`pkg/plugins/sistatement/plugin.go:519-522`). The only new answer is `Schema(id)`, read by `tableStateSchemaResolver` and `Static.Schemas()` (Static lists only Active tables).
- **No release here.** Task 2 continues on the same branch and cuts `HG_TAG` for both tasks, the first release of the plan (`HG_TAG` (Task 2) → `PROTO_TAG` (Task 3) → `CORE_TAG` (Task 6)).

```go
// TestStorageIntegrityScrubber_RedactsStage3Databases is spec 2026-10-14 §14:
// the stage-3 member databases are reserved, so an upstream message naming one
// reaches no client, even with no Active table. hg_member_unsafe is redacted
// whole, and with an Active table the qualified hg_unsafe name of that table
// still maps back to its logical id while its member-database name does not.
func TestStorageIntegrityScrubber_RedactsStage3Databases(t *testing.T) {
	s := NewStorageIntegrityScrubber(sitable.NewFake(sitable.Pending).Current())
	for _, tc := range []struct{ in, want string }{
		{"Table hg_replica.db1__t__i3 does not exist in hg_rstage", "Table <storage-integrity>.db1__t__i3 does not exist in <storage-integrity>"},
		{"Table hg_member_unsafe.db1__t does not exist", "Table <storage-integrity>.db1__t does not exist"},
		{"Database hg_xfer does not exist", "Database <storage-integrity> does not exist"},
	} {
		if got := s.Scrub(tc.in); got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("Scrub(%q) = %q, want %q", tc.in, got, tc.want)
		}
	}
	active := NewStorageIntegrityScrubber(siSnap())
	if got := active.Scrub("hg_unsafe.db1__t and hg_member_unsafe.db1__t"); got != "db1.t and <storage-integrity>.db1__t" {
		t.Fatalf("Scrub with an Active table = %q, want the unsafe name mapped back and the member name redacted", got)
	}
}
```

```go
// TestCheck_RefusesEveryReservedDatabase is spec 2026-10-14 §14: G1 built from
// sitable.ReservedDatabases(), as build.go wires it, refuses the stage-3 member
// databases on ordinary sessions in every surface but comments, as it refuses
// hg_safe. A longer word that merely contains a reserved name is not a mention.
func TestCheck_RefusesEveryReservedDatabase(t *testing.T) {
	reservedNow := sitable.ReservedDatabases()
	for _, db := range []string{"hg_member_unsafe", "hg_replica", "hg_rstage", "hg_xfer"} {
		if !slices.Contains(reservedNow, db) {
			t.Fatalf("sitable.ReservedDatabases() = %v lacks %s", reservedNow, db)
		}
	}
	for _, db := range reservedNow {
		for _, sql := range []string{
			"SELECT * FROM " + db + ".x",
			"SELECT * FROM `" + db + "`.`x`",
			"SELECT * FROM " + strings.ToUpper(db) + ".x",
			"SELECT * FROM db1.o WHERE s = '" + db + "'",
			"SELECT * FROM merge('" + db + "', 'x')",
			"SELECT $$" + db + "$$",
		} {
			rule, detail := Check(sql, "phys", reservedNow)
			if rule != RuleReservedName || detail != "reserved database "+db+" is not addressable" {
				t.Errorf("Check(%q) = %q, %q; want %q naming %s", sql, rule, detail, RuleReservedName, db)
			}
		}
		for _, sql := range []string{"SELECT 1 /* " + db + " */", "SELECT " + db + "_count FROM db1.o"} {
			if rule, detail := Check(sql, "phys", reservedNow); rule != "" {
				t.Errorf("Check(%q) = %q, %q; want a pass", sql, rule, detail)
			}
		}
	}
}
```

In `pkg/sitable/sitable.go` replace the constant block and `ReservedDatabases` (`:132-147`) with:

```go
// Protocol-owned storage-integrity databases (Spec C D2 naming freeze). The
// first three are the SNode's and equal config.StorageIntegritySafeDatabase /
// UnsafeDatabase / PromoteDatabase; this leaf package cannot import
// pkg/config (which imports pkg/rewriter), and a pkg/config test pins the
// equality. The last four are the stage-3 member databases (spec 2026-10-14
// §8.1, §14), owned by the si-member process rather than the SNode: a
// member's ReplicatedMergeTree replicas of an owner's unsafe tables, its
// verified copies, its install and replay scratch tables, and a name reserved
// for a later transfer phase. HouseGate never creates any of them; it only
// keeps every session from addressing them.
const (
	SafeDatabase         = "hg_safe"
	UnsafeDatabase       = "hg_unsafe"
	PromoteDatabase      = "hg_promote"
	MemberUnsafeDatabase = "hg_member_unsafe"
	ReplicaDatabase      = "hg_replica"
	ReplicaStageDatabase = "hg_rstage"
	TransferDatabase     = "hg_xfer"
)

// ReservedDatabases returns the protocol-owned databases in this fixed order,
// the SNode's three first: HouseGate sends them as
// StorageIntegrityArgs.reserved_databases on every enabled request (so the
// engines protect them even while no table is Active) and inside
// protected_databases on every request, and tablerefguard, sireserved, the
// exception scrubber and the ingress DROP TABLE check refuse or redact them.
// Every call returns a fresh slice.
func ReservedDatabases() []string {
	return []string{
		SafeDatabase, UnsafeDatabase, PromoteDatabase,
		MemberUnsafeDatabase, ReplicaDatabase, ReplicaStageDatabase, TransferDatabase,
	}
}
```

In `pkg/sitable/sitable_test.go`, in `TestSnapshotSchemaAnswersARefusedTableOnlyWhenItCarriesOne`, replace the row `Table{ID: "db1.pending", Status: Pending, Schema: testSchema("db1.pending")},` (`:165`) with

(the test keeps asserting that `db1.pending` misses), and append after that test (`:200`):

```go
// TestSnapshotSchemaAnswersAHeldPendingTable is spec 2026-10-14 §14: a host
// reports an Active incarnation it holds back (not ready on its SNode, or an
// unclean owner hg_safe audit in repair mode) as Pending and keeps its schema
// and hash, so journal recovery and cleanup still resolve it. A default-deny
// Pending table carries no schema and stays unanswered, and answering Schema
// makes neither table usable.
func TestSnapshotSchemaAnswersAHeldPendingTable(t *testing.T) {
	held := Table{
		ID: "db1.held", Status: Pending,
		Schema: testSchema("db1.held"), SchemaHash: payloadexec.TableSchemaHash("net", testSchema("db1.held")),
	}
	f := NewFake(Pending, held, Table{ID: "db1.denied", Status: Pending})
	snap := f.Current()

	got, ok := snap.Schema("db1.held")
	if !ok || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, held) {
		t.Fatalf("Schema(db1.held) = %+v ok=%v, want the Pending entry with its schema and hash", got, ok)
	}
	for _, id := range []string{"db1.denied", "db1.unlisted"} {
		if table, ok := snap.Schema(id); ok {
			t.Fatalf("Schema(%s) = %+v, want a miss: a default-deny Pending table has no schema", id, table)
		}
	}
	if lookup := snap.Lookup("db1", "held"); lookup.Status != Pending || lookup.SchemaHash != held.SchemaHash {
		t.Fatalf("Lookup(db1, held) = %+v, want it still Pending with its hash", lookup)
	}
	if active := snap.Active(); len(active) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("Active() = %+v, want none: a held table is not Active", active)
	}

	// The answer is a fresh copy, like every other.
	got.Schema.Columns[0].Name = "mutated"
	if again, _ := snap.Schema("db1.held"); again.Schema.Columns[0].Name != "a" {
		t.Fatalf("mutating a Schema()-returned Pending Table's Columns leaked into the snapshot: %+v", again.Schema.Columns)
	}

	// The Fake carries the hold across versions: Active, then held.
	f.Set(Table{ID: "db1.held", Status: Active, Schema: testSchema("db1.held"), SchemaHash: held.SchemaHash})
	f.Set(held)
	if table, ok := f.Current().Schema("db1.held"); !ok || table.Status != Pending || table.SchemaHash != held.SchemaHash {
		t.Fatalf("after the hold Schema(db1.held) = %+v ok=%v, want the held Pending entry", table, ok)
	}
	if len(f.Current().Active()) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("a held table must leave the Active set")
	}
}
```

```go
// heldPendingState reports net1.events the way a host reports an Active
// incarnation it holds back (spec 2026-10-14 §14: not ready on its SNode, or
// an unclean owner hg_safe audit in repair mode): Pending, its schema and
// hash kept.
func heldPendingState() sitable.TableState {
	schema := bpSchemas()[0]
	return sitable.NewFake(sitable.Pending, sitable.Table{
		ID: "net1.events", Status: sitable.Pending,
		Schema: schema, SchemaHash: payloadexec.TableSchemaHash("testnet-v2", schema),
```

and after `TestTableStateSchemaResolverAnswersAQuarantinedTable` (`:158`):

```go
// TestTableStateSchemaResolverResolvesAHeldPendingTable pins the resolver that
// journal recovery and cleanup share (contract §2, spec 2026-10-14 §14): it
// answers a Pending table that carries a schema, an Active incarnation its
// host holds back, and still misses a default-deny Pending table, listed or
// not, which carries none.
func TestTableStateSchemaResolverResolvesAHeldPendingTable(t *testing.T) {
	want := bpSchemas()[0]
	got, ok := tableStateSchemaResolver(heldPendingState()).StorageIntegrityTableSchema("net1.events")
	if !ok || got.TableID != want.TableID || got.PartitionBy != want.PartitionBy || !slices.Equal(got.Columns, want.Columns) {
		t.Fatalf("resolver = %+v ok=%v, want the held table's schema", got, ok)
	}
	denied := sitable.NewFake(sitable.Pending, sitable.Table{ID: "net1.events", Status: sitable.Pending})
	if _, ok := tableStateSchemaResolver(denied).StorageIntegrityTableSchema("net1.events"); ok {
		t.Fatal("a listed default-deny Pending table has no schema to resolve")
	}
	if _, ok := tableStateSchemaResolver(purgedState()).StorageIntegrityTableSchema("net1.events"); ok {
		t.Fatal("an unrecorded (Pending by default) table has no schema to resolve")
	}
}

// TestRecoveryOfAHeldPendingTableResolvesItsSchema closes the legacy-record
// gap the owner audit's hold would open (spec 2026-10-14 §14): a record
// without journaled partitions, admitted while the table was Active, still
// recovers after a restart that finds the table held Pending by its host.
// Without the schema recovery would call the table purged and fail closed.
func TestRecoveryOfAHeldPendingTableResolvesItsSchema(t *testing.T) {
	journal := leavePendingRecord(t, nil)
	pressure, err := recoverWith(t, journal, heldPendingState())
	if errors.Is(err, ErrStorageIntegrityRecoverySchemaPurged) {
		t.Fatalf("a held Pending table keeps its schema in the table state: %v", err)
	}
	pressure.mu.Lock()
	defer pressure.mu.Unlock()
	if pressure.restored != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("restored = %d, want 1", pressure.restored)
	}
}
```

```go
// Snapshot is immutable; every method is in-memory and performs no I/O.
//
// Schema is how journal recovery and cleanup resolve a table's schema. It
// answers an Active or Gone table, a Refused table that carries a schema (a
// quarantined indexer's, code "indexer_quarantined") and a Pending table that
// carries one (an Active incarnation its host holds back, spec 2026-10-14
// §14); NewSnapshot, Static and Fake do. It misses for every other table,
// including a Refused or Pending one without a schema (an admission refusal,
// default deny) and an Ordinary one.
type Snapshot interface {
	Version() uint64
	Lookup(database, table string) Table // answers for any table
	Active() []Table                     // sorted by ID
	Schema(id string) (Table, bool)      // Active or Gone, or Refused or Pending with a schema
}
```

and replace `snapshot.Schema` with its comment (`:217-238`) with:

```go
// Schema answers an Active or Gone table, and a Refused or Pending table that
// carries a schema: a host keeps the schema of each table it reports Refused
// because its SI indexer is quarantined (code "indexer_quarantined", spec
// 2026-10-10 §10) and of each Active incarnation it reports Pending while it
// holds it back (not ready on its SNode, or an unclean owner hg_safe audit in
// repair mode, spec 2026-10-14 §14), so journal recovery and cleanup still
// resolve it. A Refused table without a schema (the arbiter's admission
// refusal), a Pending one without a schema (default deny), an Ordinary one and
// an unlisted one all miss.
func (s *snapshot) Schema(id string) (Table, bool) {
	t, ok := s.byID[id]
	if !ok {
		return Table{}, false
	}
	switch t.Status {
	case Active, Gone:
	case Refused, Pending:
		if t.Schema.TableID == "" {
			return Table{}, false
		}
	default:
		return Table{}, false
	}
	return cloneTable(t), true
}
```

## Task 2: housegate — the peer-trusted reserved-name guard, the peer-leg corpus, release HG_TAG (S3-A)

Spec §14 bullet 1, §2 "Peer-trusted bypass", contract §2 bullets 3–6. Today a peer-trusted, non-forwarded session — a rewriter `remote()` loopback — reaches ClickHouse with no reserved-name check at all: `sireserved` acts only on maintenance and platform-operator sessions (`pkg/plugins/sireserved/plugin.go:29-32`), `tablerefguard` returns early for it (`pkg/plugins/tablerefguard/plugin.go:80`), rewrite and `sitablestate` opt out of peer trust, and `sipeerguard` refuses only the ordinary physical table of a governed table (`pkg/plugins/sipeerguard/plugin.go:70-99`). Stage 3 puts every member's `hg_member_unsafe`, `hg_replica` and `hg_rstage` on the SI hosts, so a peer that can open such a session could read or (through a write carrier) address them. This task adds the peer rules to `sireserved` — the plugin already wired whenever `storage_integrity.enabled` (`build.go:709-715`), already opted into both chain filters and already ordered before `sipeerguard`, `tablerefguard` and `forward` — and pins every legitimate peer-leg form as admitted, then releases housegate with Tasks 1–2 as `HG_TAG`.

The rules (contract §2, verbatim): on a peer-trusted session that was not forwarded from a peer, every mention of a reserved database (Task 1's seven) or of `_hg_row_id` outside comments, string literals included, and every `{x:Identifier}` placeholder is refused with ClickHouse 392; a statement the peer scan cannot model is refused too. Maintenance and platform-operator sessions keep today's operator rules byte for byte (checked first, so a peer session that also carries an operator flag gets the stricter rules); ordinary and forwarded-from-peer sessions are unchanged (`tablerefguard` and the engines own their client SQL).

  - Added names (Appendix B): unexported `(*Plugin).operatorRefusal(sql string) error`, `(*Plugin).peerRefusal(ctx context.Context, peerAddress, sql string) error`, `refusePeer`, `identifierPlaceholderToken`, `peerRefusals`, `peerReasonReservedName` / `peerReasonIdentifierPlaceholder` / `peerReasonStatementUnscannable`, `maxLoggedStatementBytes`, `truncatedMarker`, `truncateStatement` (in `sireserved`); unit tests `TestOnQuery_PeerSessionsRefuseReservedNamespace`, `TestOnQuery_PeerSessionsRefuseIdentifierPlaceholders`, `TestOnQuery_PeerUnscannableStatementIsRefused`, `TestOnQuery_ForwardedFromPeerSessionsAreNotPeerChecked`, `TestOnQuery_PeerSessionWithAnOperatorFlagKeepsTheOperatorRules`, `TestOnQuery_PeerRefusalCountsAndLogs`, `TestPeerReservedNamespaceViolation_DecodesEscapes`, `TestPeerScanOptionsDecodeBothEscapeKinds`; renamed tests `TestOnQuery_IdentifierPlaceholderLeavesOrdinarySessionsAlone` (was `…LeavesOrdinaryPeerBypassAlone`) and `TestOnQuery_LeavesOrdinarySessionsAlone` (was `…LeavesOrdinaryAndNonOperatorSessionsAlone`); integration helpers `seedPeerReserved`, `startPeerReservedInternal`, `peerLegQueryID`, `captureSecondaryQueries(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, queryID, sql string) ([]string, error)`, `peerReservedRemote`, constants `peerReservedPhys = "phys_pr"`, `peerReservedDB = "prdb"`.
  - Release `HG_TAG` (Tasks 1–2), recorded by content: the first release of the plan (release order `HG_TAG` (this task) → `PROTO_TAG` (Task 3) → `CORE_TAG` (Task 6)). housegate keeps arbiter-proto `v0.11.0`, because nothing in Tasks 1–2 needs `PROTO_TAG`, which does not exist yet. Consumed by Plan S3-B (sentio-node pins it, because the guard reaches the SI hosts only through sentio-node's embedded HouseGate). arbiter-core (Task 4) and arbiter (Task 7) call nothing it changes but pin it with `bash scripts/update-housegate.sh $HG_TAG` (contract §6), so every repository builds against one housegate.

Notes:
- **Why `sireserved`.** It is wired whenever SI is enabled; `sipeerguard` is wired only with `rewriter.physical_database` (`build.go:720-727`) and does nothing without a table state, so it is the wrong host for a rule that must hold on every SI host. `sireserved` cannot import `sipeerguard` (the import goes the other way, `pkg/plugins/sipeerguard/plugin.go:20`), so the 15-line statement truncation is duplicated rather than shared; the scan options, which must not drift, are exported once (`PeerScanOptions`) and used by both.
- **Which sessions are peer-trusted and non-forwarded.** On an SI host only rewriter `remote()` loopbacks signed with `peer.SignPeerHello` (`pkg/rewriter/sentio.go:599-621`, validated in `pkg/plugins/credential/injector.go:76-84,118-143`); the internal listener also pre-flags peer trust (`build.go:1098-1110`), but sentio-node refuses `internal_listen` with storage integrity enabled (`sentio-node:standalone/startup_transaction.go:833-834`). Forward pivots arrive `IsForwardedFromPeer` and stay `tablerefguard`'s. Neither arbiter-core nor the arbiter connects through HouseGate.
- **The peer scan decodes; the operator scan refuses.** ClickHouse emits backslash-bearing literals and escaped quoted identifiers in legitimate secondary queries (projection aliases measured on 26.8.1, `pkg/plugins/sipeerguard/plugin_test.go:157-163`), which the operator rules' strict `sqlsurface.Scan` refuses. The peer rules therefore scan with `PeerScanOptions` — exactly what `sipeerguard` already applies to every peer statement on SI hosts, so no new scan refusal appears in practice — and decoding also catches encoded names (`'hg\x5Fsafe'` is `hg_safe` on `WithLiterals`).
- **Placeholders are read from the token stream.** `sqlsurface.ContainsIdentifierPlaceholder(OutsideLiterals)` (the operator rule) also matches text inside a quoted identifier, and ClickHouse writes an expression's text into the projection alias of a secondary query: a client literal `'{p:Identifier}'`, which the origin's `tablerefguard` G4 admits, becomes the alias `` `concat(s, '{p:Identifier}')` `` on the leg. The peer rule matches the five tokens `{` name `:` `Identifier` `}` instead (case-insensitive, comments and whitespace between them allowed), which is exactly what ClickHouse parses as a substitution. ClickHouse substitutes query parameters on the initiator, so no legitimate leg carries one; the old row "ordinary peer" of the identifier-placeholder test flips to refused.
- **Carriers are not refused on peer sessions.** A legitimate leg carries a nested `remote(…)` whenever ClickHouse pushes a `remote()`-left JOIN of another `remote()`, or an IN subquery over another `remote()`, into the leg (measured on 25.8.28.1: `… FROM \`phys_pr\`.\`prdb.o\` AS \`__table1\` ALL INNER JOIN remote('<host>', 'phys_pr', 'prdb.o') AS \`__table2\` …` and `… IN (SELECT … FROM remote('<host>', …) AS \`__table1\`)`), so the operator rules' carrier refusal would break cross-indexer reads. rewriter-go's IN-operand rendering, a bare `x IN remote(…)` (`internal/engine/nodes.go:3207-3222`), is refused by ClickHouse 25.8.28.1 and 26.3.37.3 at the initiator with code 46 and never reaches a peer; the corpus keeps it admitted anyway. The residual gap — a name computed by a carrier argument, `merge(concat('hg_', 'replica'), …)` or `INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote('localhost', concat(…), …)` — is closed by the ClickHouse lockdown of Plan S3-B (HouseGate's upstream user holds no grants on the member databases), recorded in Appendix B. The build warning says so.
- **Order with `sipeerguard`.** `sireserved` runs first, so an unscannable peer statement is now refused with `sireserved`'s message and counted in `storage_integrity_peer_reserved_name_refusals_total{reason="statement_unscannable"}`; on a host where both are wired `sipeerguard`'s `statement_unscannable` branch and its counter no longer see such a statement. `sipeerguard`'s own tests call it directly and stay green unchanged.
- **The 392 carries no session or seq marker.** The refusals set neither `KeepSession` nor `SeqUnspent`, and `isSessionPreservingIngressException` (`pkg/proxy/relay.go:2314-2331`) recognises only the exact table-no-longer-accepts-writes and indexer-quarantined messages under 392, so on the agent's deferred lane these stay fail-closed like every other 392 (`sipeerguard`'s and `sitablestate`'s included).
- **Known non-legitimate leg.** A JOIN whose left operand is `remote()` cannot be made GLOBAL (rewriter-go `internal/engine/global.go:8-35`), so when ClickHouse pushes such a JOIN into the leg the peer receives the origin's `hg_safe` read of its local SI table; it never worked (the peer read its own table of that name, or failed). `TestPeerReservedGuard_RemoteLeftJoinOfALocalSITableIsRefused` measures whether the CI ClickHouse pushes it (25.8.28.1 does: `… ALL INNER JOIN \`hg_safe\`.\`prdb__l\` AS \`__table2\` …`) and pins the 392 either way.
- **Member byte sources stay off HouseGate.** The pulls of spec §8.6 target ClickHouse 9000 directly with named collections; through a HouseGate port this guard would refuse them.
- **ClickHouse version.** The integration job uses `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.8` (`pkg/integration/testenv/clickhouse.go:22`); the deployed image is `26.3-lts-decimal512`. The rule matches mentions, so formatting differences do not matter, and Plan S3-B's devnet2 acceptance checks a real cross-indexer read with the counter at 0.
- **Rollback.** No state, no wire change: the previous image restores today's behaviour.

```go
		if errors.As(err, &ce) {
			t.Errorf("%s: the operator refusal must stay a plain error (403), got %+v", sql, ce)

		err = runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false))
		if !errors.As(err, &ce) || ce.Code != chproto.CodeQueryIsProhibited || ce.Message != peerReservedMessage(db) {
			t.Errorf("%s on a peer loopback: err = %v, want the 392 naming %s", sql, err, db)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
// peerGuard is the guard as build.go wires it.
func peerGuard() *Plugin {
	return &Plugin{ReservedDatabases: sitable.ReservedDatabases(), ReservedRowIDColumn: "_hg_row_id"}
}

// peerQuery returns a query context on a peer-trusted session: a rewriter
// remote() loopback when forwarded is false, a forward pivot otherwise.
func peerQuery(t *testing.T, sql string, forwarded bool) *plugin.QueryContext {
	t.Helper()
	sess := newSessionForTest(t, 40)
	sess.State().SetPeerTrustForwarded("10.0.0.7:9000", forwarded)
	return &plugin.QueryContext{Session: sess, OriginalSQL: sql, Query: &chproto.Query{Body: sql}}
}

// runChain runs p through a one-plugin chain so its marker methods decide.
func runChain(ctx context.Context, p *Plugin, qctx *plugin.QueryContext) error {
	return (&plugin.PluginChain{QueryPlugins: []plugin.QueryPlugin{p}}).OnQuery(ctx, qctx)
}

func peerReservedMessage(name string) string {
	return "storage_integrity: reserved name " + name + " is not addressable on a peer connection; the peer guard refuses any mention, string literals included"
}

func requirePeerRefusal(t *testing.T, err error, message string) {
	t.Helper()
	var ce *chproto.ClientError
	if !errors.As(err, &ce) || ce.Code != chproto.CodeQueryIsProhibited || ce.Message != message {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want 392 %q", err, message)
	}
}

func captureLogs(t *testing.T) (context.Context, *bytes.Buffer) {
	t.Helper()
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	return log.WithContext(context.Background(), log.New(slog.NewTextHandler(&buf, nil))), &buf
}

// peerLegForms is the regression corpus of the SQL a storage-integrity host
// receives on a legitimate rewriter remote() loopback (peer-trusted, not
// forwarded): ClickHouse's secondary queries for the legs the origin's
// rewriter emits — rewriter-go nodes.go ActionRemote in FROM/JOIN and
// IN-operand position, dblevel.go SHOW TABLES of a remote logical database,
// and the structure probe ClickHouse sends because rewriter-go never passes a
// structure argument. Rows marked (measured) are ClickHouse 26.8.1 output
// pinned in sipeerguard's tests, rows marked (measured 25.8) are ClickHouse
// 25.8.28.1 output, and the others follow the same formatting.
// TestPeerReservedGuard_MeasuredRemoteSecondaryQueriesPass captures from
// ClickHouse itself every class one server emits; it cannot see the
// structure probe (ClickHouse reads a local shard's structure without
// sending it) or the bare IN-operand form (ClickHouse refuses it at the
// initiator). Every row except the system.tables probe names the physical
// database phys, and no other word contains "phys", so
// TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsWithAReservedNameAreRefused can put a reserved
// database in its place.
var peerLegForms = map[string]string{
	// (a) The remote() structure probe; 25.8.28.1 writes the database bare
	// (measured against a second server).
	"structure probe":                 "DESC TABLE `phys`.`db1.t`",
	"structure probe (measured 25.8)": "DESC TABLE phys.`db1.t`",
	// (b) A table read pushed down to the leg.
	"pushed-down count (measured)":        "SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"bare physical database (measured)":   "SELECT `__table1`.`value` AS `value` FROM phys.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"pushed-down filter":                  "SELECT `__table1`.`id` AS `id`, `__table1`.`s` AS `s` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` WHERE `__table1`.`id` IN (1, 2)",
	"aggregation with GROUP BY and LIMIT": "SELECT `__table1`.`s` AS `s`, sum(`__table1`.`x`) AS `sum(x)` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` GROUP BY `__table1`.`s` ORDER BY `__table1`.`s` ASC LIMIT 10",
	"uniq intermediate state":             "SELECT uniq(`__table1`.`s`) AS `uniq(s)` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"FINAL and PREWHERE":                  "SELECT `__table1`.`id` AS `id` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` FINAL PREWHERE `__table1`.`x` > 0.5",
	"pre-analyzer formatting":             "SELECT count() FROM phys.`db1.t`",
	"backslash alias (measured)":          "SELECT extract(`__table1`.`s`, '\\\\d+') AS `extract(s, '\\\\\\\\d+')` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"newline alias (measured)":            "SELECT concat(`__table1`.`s`, '\\n') AS `concat(s, '\\\\n')` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"quote alias (measured)":              "SELECT concat(`__table1`.`s`, 'it\\'s') AS `concat(s, 'it\\\\'s')` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"decimal alias (measured)":            "SELECT avg(`__table1`.`x` * 1.5) AS `avg(multiply(x, 1.5))` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"countIf alias (measured)":            "SELECT countIf(`__table1`.`x` > 0.5) AS `countIf(greater(x, 0.5))` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"Nested column (measured)":            "SELECT `__table1`.`n.a` AS `n.a` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	"dotted alias (measured)":             "SELECT `__table1`.`s` AS `db1.alias` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	// A client literal the origin's tablerefguard G4 admits becomes alias text.
	"Identifier-shaped literal in an alias": "SELECT concat(`__table1`.`s`, '{p:Identifier}') AS `concat(s, '{p:Identifier}')` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
	// (c) SHOW TABLES of a remote logical database.
	"SHOW TABLES structure probe": "DESC TABLE `system`.`tables`",
	"SHOW TABLES filtered read":   "SELECT `__table1`.`name` AS `name` FROM `system`.`tables` AS `__table1` WHERE (`__table1`.`database` = 'phys') AND startsWith(`__table1`.`name`, 'db1.')",
	// (d) GLOBAL IN / GLOBAL JOIN: the origin computes the local side, hg_safe
	// reads included, and ships it as an external table.
	"GLOBAL IN external table (analyzer)":     "SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` WHERE `__table1`.`id` GLOBAL IN (`_data_7020342823616227185_10950398713282440232`)",
	"GLOBAL IN external table (pre-analyzer)": "SELECT count() FROM phys.`db1.t` WHERE id GLOBAL IN _data1",
	"GLOBAL JOIN external table":              "SELECT `__table1`.`id` AS `id`, `__table2`.`v` AS `v` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` GLOBAL ALL INNER JOIN `_data_7020342823616227185_10950398713282440232` AS `__table2` USING (`id`)",
	// The 25.8.28.1 analyzer aliases the external table and writes LIMIT as a
	// typed cast.
	"GLOBAL IN external table with an alias (measured 25.8)": "SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` WHERE `__table1`.`id` GLOBAL IN (`_data_12979155211854796489_16094174518441047580` AS `__table2`)",
	"LIMIT as a typed cast (measured 25.8)":                  "SELECT `__table1`.`s` AS `s`, sum(`__table1`.`x`) AS `sum(x)` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` GROUP BY `__table1`.`s` ORDER BY `__table1`.`s` ASC LIMIT _CAST(10, 'UInt64')",
	// (e) A nested remote() carrier, whose literals name another host, the
	// physical database and the peer envelope: ClickHouse pushes a
	// remote()-left JOIN of another remote() and an IN subquery over another
	// remote() into the leg (measured on 25.8.28.1, arguments as the
	// rewriter renders them). rewriter-go's bare IN-operand form is refused by
	// ClickHouse 25.8 and 26.3 at the initiator; it stays admitted here so the
	// rule never depends on that refusal.
	"remote JOIN pushed into the leg (measured 25.8)":        "SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` ALL INNER JOIN remote('10.0.0.5:9000', 'phys', 'db1.u', '__route__|10.0.0.5:9000|__peer__|0x5a1f0e07c3e5d2b6a7f8e9d0c1b2a3f4e5d6c7b8', 'eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NksiLCJ0eXAiOiJKV1QifQ.eyJzdWIiOiJwZWVyLWhlbGxvIn0.c2lnbmF0dXJlX2J5dGVz') AS `__table2` ON `__table1`.`id` = `__table2`.`id`",
	"remote IN subquery pushed into the leg (measured 25.8)": "SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` WHERE `__table1`.`id` IN (SELECT `__table1`.`id` AS `id` FROM remote('10.0.0.5:9000', 'phys', 'db1.u', '__route__|10.0.0.5:9000|__peer__|0x5a1f0e07c3e5d2b6a7f8e9d0c1b2a3f4e5d6c7b8', 'eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NksiLCJ0eXAiOiJKV1QifQ.eyJzdWIiOiJwZWVyLWhlbGxvIn0.c2lnbmF0dXJlX2J5dGVz') AS `__table1`)",
	"remote IN operand inside a remote outer":                "SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` WHERE `__table1`.`id` IN remote('127.0.0.1:19001', 'phys', 'db1.l', '__route__|10.0.0.5:9000|__peer__|0x5a1f0e07c3e5d2b6a7f8e9d0c1b2a3f4e5d6c7b8', 'eyJhbGciOiJFUzI1NksiLCJ0eXAiOiJKV1QifQ.eyJzdWIiOiJwZWVyLWhlbGxvIn0.c2lnbmF0dXJlX2J5dGVz')",
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsPass is spec 2026-10-14 §14's regression rule: every
// legitimate peer leg passes the peer rules, through the chain and through
// PeerReservedNamespaceViolation.
func TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsPass(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	for name, sql := range peerLegForms {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if err := runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false)); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("legitimate peer leg %q refused: %v", sql, err)
			}
			if got, err := PeerReservedNamespaceViolation(sql, sitable.ReservedDatabases(), "_hg_row_id"); err != nil || got != "" {
				t.Fatalf("PeerReservedNamespaceViolation(%q) = %q, %v; want no violation", sql, got, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsWithAReservedNameAreRefused: the same shapes with a
// reserved database in the physical database's place, as identifier or as
// literal, and with the reserved row-id column, are refused with the 392 that
// names it.
func TestOnQuery_PeerLegFormsWithAReservedNameAreRefused(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	var withoutPhysical []string
	for name, sql := range peerLegForms {
		if !strings.Contains(sql, "phys") {
			withoutPhysical = append(withoutPhysical, name)
			continue
		}
		for _, db := range sitable.ReservedDatabases() {
			reserved := strings.ReplaceAll(sql, "phys", db)
			t.Run(name+"/"+db, func(t *testing.T) {
				requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, reserved, false)), peerReservedMessage(db))
			})
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(withoutPhysical)
	if strings.Join(withoutPhysical, ",") != "SHOW TABLES structure probe" {
		t.Fatalf("corpus rows without the physical database = %v; every other row must name phys", withoutPhysical)
	}
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"SELECT `__table1`.`_hg_row_id` AS `_hg_row_id` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
		"SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1` WHERE `__table1`.`_hg_row_id` > 0",
	} {
		t.Run(sql, func(t *testing.T) {
			requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false)), peerReservedMessage("_hg_row_id"))
		})
	}
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerSessionsRefuseReservedNamespace is the mention rule on a peer
// loopback for every reserved database, in every surface but comments: plain,
// quoted and upper-case identifiers, table-function literals, heredocs, an IN
// subquery, metadata literals, and escapes ClickHouse decodes.
func TestOnQuery_PeerSessionsRefuseReservedNamespace(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	for _, db := range sitable.ReservedDatabases() {
		escaped := strings.ReplaceAll(db, "_", `\x5F`)
		escapedLower := strings.ReplaceAll(db, "_", `\x5f`)
		for _, tc := range []struct{ name, sql string }{
			{"qualifier", "SELECT * FROM " + db + ".db1__t"},
			{"pushed-down leg", "SELECT count() AS `count()` FROM `" + db + "`.`db1__t` AS `__table1`"},
			{"double-quoted qualifier", `SELECT * FROM "` + db + `"."db1__t"`},
			{"upper case", "SELECT * FROM " + strings.ToUpper(db) + ".db1__t"},
			{"remote database literal", "SELECT count() FROM remote('127.0.0.1:9000', '" + db + "', 'db1__t')"},
			{"merge database literal", "SELECT * FROM merge('" + db + "', '^db1__t$')"},
			{"heredoc", "SELECT * FROM merge($$" + db + "$$, '^db1__t$')"},
			{"IN subquery", "SELECT count() FROM `phys`.`db1.t` WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM " + db + ".db1__t)"},
			{"metadata literal", "SELECT name FROM system.tables WHERE database = '" + db + "'"},
			{"escaped literal", "SELECT * FROM merge('" + escaped + "', '^db1__t$')"},
			{"escaped quoted identifier", "SELECT * FROM `" + escapedLower + "`.db1__t"},
			{"USE", "USE " + db},
			{"INSERT", "INSERT INTO " + db + ".db1__t VALUES (1)"},
		} {
			t.Run(db+"/"+tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
				requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, tc.sql, false)), peerReservedMessage(db))
			})
		}
	}
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"SELECT `__table1`.`_hg_row_id` FROM `phys`.`db1.t` AS `__table1`",
		"SELECT '_hg_row_id'",
		`SELECT '\x5Fhg\x5Frow\x5Fid'`,
	} {
		requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false)), peerReservedMessage("_hg_row_id"))
	}
	// ClickHouse reads \N as nothing, so 'hg_\Nsafe' is hg_safe.
	requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, `SELECT * FROM t WHERE s = 'hg_\Nsafe'`, false)), peerReservedMessage("hg_safe"))
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerSessionsRefuseIdentifierPlaceholders: every {name:Identifier}
// placeholder ClickHouse would parse is refused on a peer loopback, and text
// that only looks like one — a value placeholder, a literal, a heredoc, a
// quoted identifier (where ClickHouse writes projection aliases) or a
// comment — is not.
func TestOnQuery_PeerSessionsRefuseIdentifierPlaceholders(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	const want = "storage_integrity: a peer statement may not carry ClickHouse Identifier placeholders"
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"SELECT * FROM {db:Identifier}.db1__t",
		"SELECT * FROM { db : identifier }",
		"SELECT {c:Identifier} FROM `phys`.`db1.t`",
		"SELECT * FROM {db/* c */:Identifier}.t",
		"SELECT * FROM `phys`.{t:Identifier}",
	} {
		t.Run(sql, func(t *testing.T) {
			requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false)), want)
		})
	}
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"SELECT count() FROM `phys`.`db1.t` WHERE id = {v:UInt64}",
		"SELECT '{p:Identifier}'",
		"SELECT $${p:Identifier}$$",
		"SELECT 1 AS `{p:Identifier}`",
		"SELECT 1 /* {p:Identifier} */",
	} {
		t.Run(sql, func(t *testing.T) {
			if err := runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false)); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%q is no placeholder: %v", sql, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerUnscannableStatementIsRefused: a statement the peer scan
// cannot model fails closed with the scan error in the message.
func TestOnQuery_PeerUnscannableStatementIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"SELECT 'x",
		"SELECT $ FROM `phys`.`db1.t`",
		`SELECT '\x4g'`,
		"SELECT * FROM `phys`.`db1\\x4gt`",
		"SELECT 1 #x\n",
		"SELECT 1 AS physé",
	} {
		t.Run(sql, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, scanErr := sqlsurface.ScanWith(sql, PeerScanOptions)
			if scanErr == nil {
				t.Fatalf("fixture %q must not scan", sql)
			}
			requirePeerRefusal(t, runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, false)),
				"storage_integrity: a peer statement that cannot be checked for reserved names is refused: "+scanErr.Error())
		})
	}
}

// TestOnQuery_ForwardedFromPeerSessionsAreNotPeerChecked: a forward pivot
// carries the client's own SQL, which the receiving host's tablerefguard and
// engines check; the peer rules do not apply to it.
func TestOnQuery_ForwardedFromPeerSessionsAreNotPeerChecked(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	for _, sql := range []string{
		"SELECT * FROM hg_safe.db1__t",
		"SELECT * FROM hg_replica.db1__t__i3",
		"SELECT * FROM {db:Identifier}.t",
		"SELECT 'x",
	} {
		if err := runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, sql, true)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("forwarded-from-peer %q: %v, want nil", sql, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerSessionWithAnOperatorFlagKeepsTheOperatorRules: the operator
// branch is checked first, so a peer session that also carries an operator
// flag gets the stricter operator rules and their plain (403) errors, which
// also refuse what the peer rules admit: a backslash-bearing alias and a
// carrier.
func TestOnQuery_PeerSessionWithAnOperatorFlagKeepsTheOperatorRules(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	for _, tc := range []struct{ name, sql, want string }{
		{"reserved name", "SELECT * FROM hg_replica.db1__t", `storage-integrity reserved name "hg_replica" is not addressable through the proxy`},
		{"measured backslash alias", peerLegForms["backslash alias (measured)"], "backslash"},
		{"carrier", "SELECT * FROM remote('h', 'other', 'u')", `object-carrier callable "remote"`},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			sess := newSessionForTest(t, 41)
			sess.State().SetPeerTrust("10.0.0.7:9000")
			sess.State().SetPlatformOperator(true)
			err := runChain(context.Background(), p, &plugin.QueryContext{Session: sess, OriginalSQL: tc.sql, Query: &chproto.Query{Body: tc.sql}})
			var ce *chproto.ClientError
			if err == nil || errors.As(err, &ce) || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.want) {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, want the operator refusal containing %q, not the peer 392", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
	if err := runChain(context.Background(), p, peerQuery(t, "SELECT * FROM remote('h', 'other', 'u')", false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a carrier naming no reserved database must pass the peer rules: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestOnQuery_PeerRefusalCountsAndLogs: each refusal increments its reason
// once and writes exactly one warn line with the contract's fields, the
// statement cut to 512 bytes; an admitted leg counts and logs nothing.
func TestOnQuery_PeerRefusalCountsAndLogs(t *testing.T) {
	p := peerGuard()
	long := "SELECT 'x" + strings.Repeat("数据", 400) + "' FROM hg_replica.db1__t"
	for _, tc := range []struct{ reason, sql, reservedField string }{
		{"reserved_name", long, "reserved_name=hg_replica"},
		{"identifier_placeholder", "SELECT * FROM {db:Identifier}.t", `reserved_name=""`},
		{"statement_unscannable", "SELECT 'x", `reserved_name=""`},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.reason, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx, buf := captureLogs(t)
			before := testutil.ToFloat64(peerRefusals.WithLabelValues(tc.reason))
			err := runChain(ctx, p, peerQuery(t, tc.sql, false))
			var ce *chproto.ClientError
			if !errors.As(err, &ce) || ce.Code != chproto.CodeQueryIsProhibited {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, want a 392", err)
			}
			if got := testutil.ToFloat64(peerRefusals.WithLabelValues(tc.reason)) - before; got != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("storage_integrity_peer_reserved_name_refusals_total{reason=%q} grew by %v, want 1", tc.reason, got)
			}
			out := buf.String()
			if strings.Count(out, "\n") != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("want exactly one log line, got %q", out)
			}
			for _, want := range []string{
				"level=WARN",
				"peer statement refused by storage-integrity reserved-name guard",
				"plugin=sireserved",
				"code=392",
				"reason=" + tc.reason,
				tc.reservedField,
				"peer_address=10.0.0.7:9000",
			} {
				if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
					t.Errorf("log line missing %q: %s", want, out)
				}
			}
			if tc.sql == long && (!strings.Contains(out, "…(truncated)") || strings.Contains(out, "FROM hg_replica")) {
				t.Errorf("the statement must be cut at 512 bytes: %s", out)
			}
		})
	}
	ctx, buf := captureLogs(t)
	before := testutil.ToFloat64(peerRefusals.WithLabelValues("reserved_name"))
	if err := runChain(ctx, p, peerQuery(t, peerLegForms["pushed-down count (measured)"], false)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("admitted leg refused: %v", err)
	}
	if buf.Len() != 0 || testutil.ToFloat64(peerRefusals.WithLabelValues("reserved_name")) != before {
		t.Fatalf("an admitted leg logged %q or counted a refusal", buf.String())
	}
}

// TestPeerReservedNamespaceViolation_DecodesEscapes is the function the
// integration tests share: names are compared after ClickHouse's decoding, an
// escape ClickHouse keeps as written is not a reserved name, heredoc bodies are
// raw, and scan errors are returned as is.
func TestPeerReservedNamespaceViolation_DecodesEscapes(t *testing.T) {
	dbs := sitable.ReservedDatabases()
	for _, tc := range []struct{ sql, want string }{
		{`SELECT * FROM merge('hg\x5Freplica', '^t$')`, "hg_replica"},
		{"SELECT * FROM `hg\\x5frstage`.t", "hg_rstage"},
		{`SELECT 'hg_\Nxfer'`, "hg_xfer"},
		{`SELECT 'HG_MEMBER\x5FUNSAFE'`, "hg_member_unsafe"},
		{peerLegForms["backslash alias (measured)"], ""},
		{`SELECT * FROM t WHERE s LIKE 'hg\_safe'`, ""},
		{`SELECT $$hg\x5Fsafe$$`, ""},
	} {
		got, err := PeerReservedNamespaceViolation(tc.sql, dbs, "_hg_row_id")
		if err != nil || got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("PeerReservedNamespaceViolation(%q) = %q, %v; want %q", tc.sql, got, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if _, err := PeerReservedNamespaceViolation(`SELECT '\x4g'`, dbs, "_hg_row_id"); !errors.Is(err, sqlsurface.ErrUndecodableStringEscape) {
		t.Fatalf("err = %v, want ErrUndecodableStringEscape", err)
	}
	// The strict twin still refuses what the peer variant decodes.
	if _, err := ReservedNamespaceViolation(`SELECT * FROM merge('hg\x5Freplica', '^t$')`, dbs, "_hg_row_id"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("ReservedNamespaceViolation must keep refusing backslash-bearing literals")
	}
}

// TestPeerScanOptionsDecodeBothEscapeKinds pins the options sipeerguard shares
// and why the peer rules never use the strict operator scan: it refuses a
// measured, legitimate leg.
func TestPeerScanOptionsDecodeBothEscapeKinds(t *testing.T) {
	if PeerScanOptions != (sqlsurface.Options{DecodeStringEscapes: true, DecodeIdentifierEscapes: true}) {
		t.Fatalf("PeerScanOptions = %+v", PeerScanOptions)
	}
	if _, err := sqlsurface.Scan(peerLegForms["backslash alias (measured)"]); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("the strict scan must refuse the measured backslash alias; the peer rules would then refuse a legitimate leg")
	}
}
```

In `pkg/plugins/sireserved/plugin.go` replace `:1-66` (the package doc through `RejectUndecodableQuery`) with:

```go
// Package sireserved protects protocol-owned storage-integrity names on the
// sessions that deliberately bypass the full SQL rewriter: maintenance and
// platform-operator sessions (the operator rules) and peer-trusted sessions
// that were not forwarded from a peer, i.e. rewriter remote() loopbacks (the
// peer rules, spec 2026-10-14 §14).
package sireserved

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/chproto"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/log"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/plugin"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/sqlsurface"
)

// PeerScanOptions is the scan of every peer-trusted guard, shared with
// sipeerguard so the two cannot drift. ClickHouse's remote() secondary
// queries carry backslash-bearing literals and escaped quoted identifiers
// (projection aliases such as `extract(s, '\\d+')`), which the operator
// rules' strict Scan refuses; decoding both instead compares names as
// ClickHouse reads them, so 'hg\x5Fsafe' is hg_safe. A \x escape without two
// hex digits stays a scan error.
var PeerScanOptions = sqlsurface.Options{DecodeStringEscapes: true, DecodeIdentifierEscapes: true}

// Reasons of the peer refusal counter.
const (
	peerReasonReservedName          = "reserved_name"
	peerReasonIdentifierPlaceholder = "identifier_placeholder"
	peerReasonStatementUnscannable  = "statement_unscannable"
)

var peerRefusals = prometheus.NewCounterVec(prometheus.CounterOpts{
	Name: "storage_integrity_peer_reserved_name_refusals_total",
	Help: "Peer-trusted, non-forwarded statements refused because they mention a storage-integrity reserved database or the reserved row-id column, carry an Identifier placeholder, or cannot be scanned.",
}, []string{"reason"})

func init() {
	prometheus.MustRegister(peerRefusals)
	// Export every reason at zero, so "no refusal since start" is a series an
	// operator can read rather than an absent one.
	for _, reason := range []string{peerReasonReservedName, peerReasonIdentifierPlaceholder, peerReasonStatementUnscannable} {
		peerRefusals.WithLabelValues(reason)
	}
}

// Plugin rejects reserved SI names on the sessions that bypass rewrite. It
// runs independently of rewrite.Plugin so forward and peer-trust filters
// cannot skip this defense-in-depth boundary.
type Plugin struct {
	ReservedDatabases   []string
	ReservedRowIDColumn string
}

// OnQuery applies the operator rules to a maintenance or platform-operator
// session, checked first so a peer session that also carries an operator flag
// gets the stricter rules; the peer rules to a peer-trusted session that was
// not forwarded from a peer (spec 2026-10-14 §14); and nothing to any other
// session. Ordinary and forwarded-from-peer sessions keep the Spec I D6
// boundary here: tablerefguard and the engines own their client SQL.
func (p *Plugin) OnQuery(ctx context.Context, qctx *plugin.QueryContext) error {
	if qctx == nil || qctx.Session == nil {
		return nil
	}
	snapshot := qctx.Session.State().Snapshot()
	sql := qctx.OriginalSQL
	if qctx.Query != nil && qctx.Query.Body != "" {
		sql = qctx.Query.Body
	}
	switch {
	case snapshot.Maintenance || snapshot.PlatformOperator:
		return p.operatorRefusal(sql)
	case snapshot.IsPeerTrusted && !snapshot.IsForwardedFromPeer:
		return p.peerRefusal(ctx, snapshot.PeerAddress, sql)
	default:
		return nil
	}
}

// operatorRefusal is the privileged-session rule set (Spec N): a strict scan
// that refuses every backslash-bearing literal or quoted identifier, then
// every {name:Identifier} placeholder, every mention of a reserved name and
// every object-carrier callable. Its errors are plain, so the relay answers
// 403.
func (p *Plugin) operatorRefusal(sql string) error {
	surfaces, err := sqlsurface.Scan(sql)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity guard could not scan the statement: %w", err)
	}
	if sqlsurface.ContainsIdentifierPlaceholder(surfaces.OutsideLiterals) {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity guard refuses ClickHouse Identifier placeholders on privileged proxy-bypass sessions; use a direct ClickHouse connection for physical access")
	}
	name := reservedNamespaceViolationOnSurface(surfaces.WithLiterals, p.ReservedDatabases, p.ReservedRowIDColumn)
	if name != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity reserved name %q is not addressable through the proxy (the operator guard rejects any mention, including an ordinary column with that name); use a direct ClickHouse connection for physical access", name)
	}
	if carrier := objectCarrierCallable(surfaces.OutsideLiterals); carrier != "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity object-carrier callable %q is not accepted on privileged proxy-bypass sessions; use a direct ClickHouse connection for physical access", carrier)
	}
	return nil
}

// peerRefusal is the peer rule set (spec 2026-10-14 §14) for a rewriter
// remote() loopback, whose SQL is ClickHouse's secondary query for a leg its
// origin emitted: a statement the peer scan cannot model, every
// {name:Identifier} placeholder, and every mention of a reserved database or
// of the reserved row-id column outside comments, string literals included,
// are refused with ClickHouse 392 (not retryable). Object-carrier callables
// are not refused: a legitimate leg may carry a nested remote() that
// ClickHouse pushed into it with a JOIN or an IN subquery.
func (p *Plugin) peerRefusal(ctx context.Context, peerAddress, sql string) error {
	surfaces, err := sqlsurface.ScanWith(sql, PeerScanOptions)
	if err != nil {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonStatementUnscannable, "", peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: a peer statement that cannot be checked for reserved names is refused: "+err.Error())
	}
	if identifierPlaceholderToken(surfaces.Tokens) {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonIdentifierPlaceholder, "", peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: a peer statement may not carry ClickHouse Identifier placeholders")
	}
	if name := reservedNamespaceViolationOnSurface(surfaces.WithLiterals, p.ReservedDatabases, p.ReservedRowIDColumn); name != "" {
		return refusePeer(ctx, peerReasonReservedName, name, peerAddress, sql,
			"storage_integrity: reserved name "+name+" is not addressable on a peer connection; the peer guard refuses any mention, string literals included")
	}
	return nil
}

// RunOnForward keeps the guard active after a session pivots to a peer.
func (*Plugin) RunOnForward() bool { return true }

// RunOnPeerTrust keeps the guard on peer-trusted sessions: OnQuery applies the
// peer rules to a remote() loopback and the operator rules to a peer session
// that carries an operator flag. A session forwarded from a peer reaches it
// either way and is treated as an ordinary one.
func (*Plugin) RunOnPeerTrust() bool { return true }

// RejectUndecodableQuery fails closed before Relay's raw-splice fallback. An
// undecodable query cannot be scanned for reserved names; the marker methods
// above keep this policy active on the forwarded/peer paths where the rewrite
// plugin's equivalent SI policy is deliberately filtered out.
func (*Plugin) RejectUndecodableQuery() bool { return true }
```

Insert after `ReservedNamespaceViolation` (after `:81`):

```go

// PeerReservedNamespaceViolation is ReservedNamespaceViolation on the peer
// scan (PeerScanOptions): string literals and quoted identifiers are decoded
// as ClickHouse reads them, so backslash-bearing spans are accepted and an
// encoded name such as 'hg\x5Fsafe' is found. It reports the first reserved
// name mentioned outside comments, string literals included, and returns a
// scan error as is. It does not check Identifier placeholders.
func PeerReservedNamespaceViolation(sql string, databases []string, rowIDColumn string) (string, error) {
	surfaces, err := sqlsurface.ScanWith(sql, PeerScanOptions)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return reservedNamespaceViolationOnSurface(surfaces.WithLiterals, databases, rowIDColumn), nil
}
```

Insert before the interface assertions (before `:159`):

```go
// refusePeer counts and logs one peer refusal and returns its ClientError. The
// warn line names the peer and the statement, cut to maxLoggedStatementBytes;
// it logs no settings, but the statement text can carry a nested remote()'s
// peer-hello token, exactly as sipeerguard's refusal line can.
func refusePeer(ctx context.Context, reason, reservedName, peerAddress, sql, message string) error {
	peerRefusals.WithLabelValues(reason).Inc()
	_, logger := log.FromContext(ctx, "plugin", "sireserved")
	logger.Warnw("peer statement refused by storage-integrity reserved-name guard",
		"code", int(chproto.CodeQueryIsProhibited),
		"reason", reason,
		"reserved_name", reservedName,
		"peer_address", peerAddress,
		"statement", truncateStatement(sql))
	return &chproto.ClientError{Code: chproto.CodeQueryIsProhibited, Message: message}
}

// identifierPlaceholderToken reports whether tokens hold a ClickHouse
// {name:Identifier} query-parameter placeholder: the five tokens {, a name, :,
// Identifier (any case) and }, with any whitespace or comments between them,
// which is what ClickHouse parses as a substitution. It reads the token stream
// rather than OutsideLiterals, which keeps quoted identifiers: ClickHouse
// writes an expression's text into the projection alias of a secondary query,
// so `concat(s, '{p:Identifier}')` is an alias there, not a placeholder.
func identifierPlaceholderToken(tokens []sqlsurface.Token) bool {
	isPunct := func(i int, text string) bool {
		return i < len(tokens) && tokens[i].Kind == sqlsurface.TokenPunct && tokens[i].Text == text
	}
	isName := func(i int) bool {
		return i < len(tokens) && (tokens[i].Kind == sqlsurface.TokenWord || tokens[i].Kind == sqlsurface.TokenQuoted)
	}
	for i := range tokens {
		if isPunct(i, "{") && isName(i+1) && isPunct(i+2, ":") && isName(i+3) &&
			strings.EqualFold(tokens[i+3].Text, "Identifier") && isPunct(i+4, "}") {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// maxLoggedStatementBytes bounds the statement text a peer refusal log carries,
// as in sipeerguard (which imports this package, so it cannot be shared).
const maxLoggedStatementBytes = 512

// truncatedMarker is appended to a statement cut by truncateStatement.
const truncatedMarker = "…(truncated)"

// truncateStatement returns sql cut to at most maxLoggedStatementBytes bytes on
// a UTF-8 rune boundary, followed by truncatedMarker when anything was cut.
func truncateStatement(sql string) string {
	if len(sql) <= maxLoggedStatementBytes {
		return sql
	}
	cut := maxLoggedStatementBytes
	for cut > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(sql[cut]) {
		cut--
	}
	return sql[:cut] + truncatedMarker
}
```
