Create `wire/stage3_reads.go`:

```go
package wire

import (
	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
)

// The stage-3 SafeState reads (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14, §15; plan S3-A
// contract §1, §3): GetPartitionStates and GetPromotionOutcomes. The arbiter
// answers each behind one leader read barrier on its data-plane listener.
// Neither read is a Raft command or reaches one, so these types have no
// canonical signing form and no JSON tags. The converters copy every field;
// an empty list becomes nil (mapSlice), an absent track or ack a nil pointer,
// and an absent watermark or command the zero value.

// PartitionStatesQuery selects GetPartitionStates' answer: every partition of
// TableID the FSM holds promotion state for, or only PartitionID. A partition
// has state once an applied acknowledgement reached it; one whose promotions
// are all unacknowledged or acknowledged with Applied:false is not listed,
// even when PartitionID names it.
type PartitionStatesQuery struct {
	TableID     string
	PartitionID string
}

// PartitionState is the FSM's promotion state of one partition: its
// fsm.PartitionState (the promotion base, PublishSeq = the newest applied
// acknowledgement, the diagnostic InventoryUnrefreshed), the cumulative
// SafeParts inventory in FSM order, the row LtHashes of its promoted unsafe
// parts still awaiting cleanup (ascending), its newest issued but
// unacknowledged promotion (0 = none) and its newest acknowledged one,
// applied or not (0 = none).
type PartitionState struct {
	TableID                       string
	PartitionID                   string
	BaseSafeSnapshotID            string
	BasePartitionRoot             string
	PublishSeq                    uint64
	SafeParts                     []replay.PartManifestEntry
	PromotedUnsafePartRowLtHashes []string
	UnackedPromotionSeq           uint64
	LastAckedPromotionSeq         uint64
	InventoryUnrefreshed          bool
}

// PartitionStates is GetPartitionStates' answer: the FSM's PromotionSeq and
// safe watermark at the read, and the selected partitions.
type PartitionStates struct {
	PromotionSeq  uint64
	SafeWatermark arbiter.SafeWatermark
	Partitions    []PartitionState
}

// PromotionOutcomesQuery selects GetPromotionOutcomes' answer: the promotions
// after AfterPromotionSeq (an exclusive cursor), of TableID (and PartitionID,
// which needs TableID) when set, at most Limit of them (0 = the arbiter's
// default).
type PromotionOutcomesQuery struct {
	TableID           string
	PartitionID       string
	AfterPromotionSeq uint64
	Limit             uint32
}

// PromotionOutcome is one issued promotion as the FSM keeps it: the command,
// its statements, the block that finishes it (the max block of StatementSeqs),
// its track (nil before the tracks activation; indexer 0 is a value), its
// source SNode, the authority token and epoch it was issued under, whether it
// is acknowledged and, for an acknowledgement recorded after the tracks
// activation (applied or not), the stored source acknowledgement with its
// signature and epoch, and whether a scheduled cleanup still awaits its
// acknowledgement (false also before the cleanup is scheduled, so false is
// not "cleaned up").
type PromotionOutcome struct {
	PromotionSeq   uint64
	Promote        arbiter.PromoteSafePartition
	StatementSeqs  []uint64
	BlockSeq       uint64
	TrackIndexerID *uint64
	SourceNode     string
	AuthorityJWS   string
	AuthorityEpoch uint64
	Acked          bool
	Ack            *arbiter.PromotionAck
	AckJWS         string
	AckEpoch       uint64
	CleanupPending bool
}

// PromotionOutcomes is GetPromotionOutcomes' answer: the FSM's PromotionSeq at
// the read, the outcomes ascending by promotion seq, and the cursor of the
// next page.
type PromotionOutcomes struct {
	PromotionSeq          uint64
	Outcomes              []PromotionOutcome
	NextAfterPromotionSeq uint64
}

func PartitionStatesQueryToPB(q PartitionStatesQuery) *pb.GetPartitionStatesRequest {
	return &pb.GetPartitionStatesRequest{TableId: q.TableID, PartitionId: q.PartitionID}
}

func PartitionStatesQueryFromPB(m *pb.GetPartitionStatesRequest) PartitionStatesQuery {
	return PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: m.GetTableId(), PartitionID: m.GetPartitionId()}
}

func safeWatermarkFromPB(m *pb.SafeWatermark) arbiter.SafeWatermark {
	return arbiter.SafeWatermark{SnapshotID: m.GetSnapshotId(), SafeBlockSeq: m.GetSafeBlockSeq(), ManifestRoot: m.GetManifestRoot()}
}

func safeWatermarkToPB(v arbiter.SafeWatermark) *pb.SafeWatermark {
	return &pb.SafeWatermark{SnapshotId: v.SnapshotID, SafeBlockSeq: v.SafeBlockSeq, ManifestRoot: v.ManifestRoot}
}

func partitionStateFromPB(m *pb.PartitionStateEntry) PartitionState {
	return PartitionState{
		TableID:                       m.GetTableId(),
		PartitionID:                   m.GetPartitionId(),
		BaseSafeSnapshotID:            m.GetBaseSafeSnapshotId(),
		BasePartitionRoot:             m.GetBasePartitionRoot(),
		PublishSeq:                    m.GetPublishSeq(),
		SafeParts:                     mapSlice(m.GetSafeParts(), partManifestEntryFromPB),
		PromotedUnsafePartRowLtHashes: mapSlice(m.GetPromotedUnsafePartRowLthashes(), func(h string) string { return h }),
		UnackedPromotionSeq:           m.GetUnackedPromotionSeq(),
		LastAckedPromotionSeq:         m.GetLastAckedPromotionSeq(),
		InventoryUnrefreshed:          m.GetInventoryUnrefreshed(),
	}
}

func partitionStateToPB(v PartitionState) *pb.PartitionStateEntry {
	return &pb.PartitionStateEntry{
		TableId:                       v.TableID,
		PartitionId:                   v.PartitionID,
		BaseSafeSnapshotId:            v.BaseSafeSnapshotID,
		BasePartitionRoot:             v.BasePartitionRoot,
		PublishSeq:                    v.PublishSeq,
		SafeParts:                     mapSlice(v.SafeParts, partManifestEntryToPB),
		PromotedUnsafePartRowLthashes: mapSlice(v.PromotedUnsafePartRowLtHashes, func(h string) string { return h }),
		UnackedPromotionSeq:           v.UnackedPromotionSeq,
		LastAckedPromotionSeq:         v.LastAckedPromotionSeq,
		InventoryUnrefreshed:          v.InventoryUnrefreshed,
	}
}

func PartitionStatesFromPB(m *pb.PartitionStates) PartitionStates {
	return PartitionStates{
		PromotionSeq:  m.GetPromotionSeq(),
		SafeWatermark: safeWatermarkFromPB(m.GetSafeWatermark()),
		Partitions:    mapSlice(m.GetPartitions(), partitionStateFromPB),
	}
}

func PartitionStatesToPB(v PartitionStates) *pb.PartitionStates {
	return &pb.PartitionStates{
		PromotionSeq:  v.PromotionSeq,
		SafeWatermark: safeWatermarkToPB(v.SafeWatermark),
		Partitions:    mapSlice(v.Partitions, partitionStateToPB),
	}
}

func PromotionOutcomesQueryToPB(q PromotionOutcomesQuery) *pb.GetPromotionOutcomesRequest {
	return &pb.GetPromotionOutcomesRequest{TableId: q.TableID, PartitionId: q.PartitionID, AfterPromotionSeq: q.AfterPromotionSeq, Limit: q.Limit}
}

func PromotionOutcomesQueryFromPB(m *pb.GetPromotionOutcomesRequest) PromotionOutcomesQuery {
	return PromotionOutcomesQuery{TableID: m.GetTableId(), PartitionID: m.GetPartitionId(), AfterPromotionSeq: m.GetAfterPromotionSeq(), Limit: m.GetLimit()}
}

func promotionOutcomeFromPB(m *pb.PromotionOutcome) PromotionOutcome {
	out := PromotionOutcome{
		PromotionSeq:   m.GetPromotionSeq(),
		Promote:        PromoteFromPB(m.GetPromote()),
		StatementSeqs:  mapSlice(m.GetStatementSeqs(), func(seq uint64) uint64 { return seq }),
		BlockSeq:       m.GetBlockSeq(),
		SourceNode:     m.GetSourceNode(),
		AuthorityJWS:   m.GetAuthorityJws(),
		AuthorityEpoch: m.GetAuthorityEpoch(),
		Acked:          m.GetAcked(),
		AckJWS:         m.GetAckJws(),
		AckEpoch:       m.GetAckEpoch(),
		CleanupPending: m.GetCleanupPending(),
	}
	if track := m.GetTrack(); track != nil {
		id := track.GetIndexerId()
		out.TrackIndexerID = &id
	}
	if ack := m.GetAck(); ack != nil {
		stored := PromotionAckFromPB(ack)
		out.Ack = &stored
	}
	return out
}

func promotionOutcomeToPB(v PromotionOutcome) *pb.PromotionOutcome {
	m := &pb.PromotionOutcome{
		PromotionSeq:   v.PromotionSeq,
		Promote:        PromoteToPB(v.Promote),
		StatementSeqs:  mapSlice(v.StatementSeqs, func(seq uint64) uint64 { return seq }),
		BlockSeq:       v.BlockSeq,
		SourceNode:     v.SourceNode,
		AuthorityJws:   v.AuthorityJWS,
		AuthorityEpoch: v.AuthorityEpoch,
		Acked:          v.Acked,
		AckJws:         v.AckJWS,
		AckEpoch:       v.AckEpoch,
		CleanupPending: v.CleanupPending,
	}
	if v.TrackIndexerID != nil {
		m.Track = &pb.L3BlockTrack{IndexerId: *v.TrackIndexerID}
	}
	if v.Ack != nil {
		m.Ack = PromotionAckToPB(*v.Ack)
	}
	return m
}

func PromotionOutcomesFromPB(m *pb.PromotionOutcomes) PromotionOutcomes {
	return PromotionOutcomes{
		PromotionSeq:          m.GetPromotionSeq(),
		Outcomes:              mapSlice(m.GetOutcomes(), promotionOutcomeFromPB),
		NextAfterPromotionSeq: m.GetNextAfterPromotionSeq(),
	}
}

func PromotionOutcomesToPB(v PromotionOutcomes) *pb.PromotionOutcomes {
	return &pb.PromotionOutcomes{
		PromotionSeq:          v.PromotionSeq,
		Outcomes:              mapSlice(v.Outcomes, promotionOutcomeToPB),
		NextAfterPromotionSeq: v.NextAfterPromotionSeq,
	}
}
```

```go
package dataplane

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"reflect"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// stage3SafeState serves the stage-3 reads and records every request. A peer
// with hint answers NotLeader naming it, one with err refuses with it, and
// otherwise it answers states and outcomes.
type stage3SafeState struct {
	pb.UnimplementedSafeStateServer

	mu          sync.Mutex
	hint        string
	err         error
	states      *pb.PartitionStates
	outcomes    *pb.PromotionOutcomes
	stateReqs   []*pb.GetPartitionStatesRequest
	outcomeReqs []*pb.GetPromotionOutcomesRequest
}

func (s *stage3SafeState) refusal() error {
	if s.hint != "" {
		st, err := status.New(codes.FailedPrecondition, "not leader").WithDetails(&pb.NotLeader{LeaderAddr: s.hint})
		if err != nil {
			return status.Error(codes.Internal, err.Error())
		}
		return st.Err()
	}
	return s.err
}

func (s *stage3SafeState) GetPartitionStates(_ context.Context, req *pb.GetPartitionStatesRequest) (*pb.PartitionStates, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.stateReqs = append(s.stateReqs, req)
	if err := s.refusal(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return s.states, nil
}

func (s *stage3SafeState) GetPromotionOutcomes(_ context.Context, req *pb.GetPromotionOutcomesRequest) (*pb.PromotionOutcomes, error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.outcomeReqs = append(s.outcomeReqs, req)
	if err := s.refusal(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return s.outcomes, nil
}

func (s *stage3SafeState) setErr(err error) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.err = err
}

func (s *stage3SafeState) requests() ([]*pb.GetPartitionStatesRequest, []*pb.GetPromotionOutcomesRequest) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]*pb.GetPartitionStatesRequest(nil), s.stateReqs...), append([]*pb.GetPromotionOutcomesRequest(nil), s.outcomeReqs...)
}

func startStage3Peer(t *testing.T, s *stage3SafeState) string {
	t.Helper()
	srv := grpc.NewServer()
	pb.RegisterSafeStateServer(srv, s)
	return serveGRPCForDataplaneTest(t, srv)
}

// TestGetPartitionStatesFollowsTheLeaderHint: the read is leader-barriered, so
// a follower answers NotLeader and the client asks the leader it names; the
// query reaches the leader as given, and the leader is asked first next time
// (plan S3-A contract §3).
func TestGetPartitionStatesFollowsTheLeaderHint(t *testing.T) {
	want := stage3StatesFixture()
	follower := &stage3SafeState{hint: "n2"}
	leader := &stage3SafeState{states: wire.PartitionStatesToPB(want)}
	c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startStage3Peer(t, follower)}, Peer{ID: "n2", GRPCAddr: startStage3Peer(t, leader)})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	got, err := c.GetPartitionStates(ctx, wire.PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: "db.t"})

	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("GetPartitionStates: %v", err)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("states\n got %+v\nwant %+v", got, want)
	}
	followerReqs, _ := follower.requests()
	leaderReqs, _ := leader.requests()
	if len(followerReqs) != 1 || len(leaderReqs) != 1 || leaderReqs[0].GetTableId() != "db.t" || leaderReqs[0].GetPartitionId() != "" {
		t.Fatalf("requests: follower %v, leader %v", followerReqs, leaderReqs)
	}
	if _, err := c.GetPartitionStates(ctx, wire.PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: "db.t"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("second read: %v", err)
	}
	if followerReqs, _ = follower.requests(); len(followerReqs) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("the second read asked the follower again: %d requests", len(followerReqs))
	}
}

	want := wire.PromotionOutcomes{PromotionSeq: 12, Outcomes: []wire.PromotionOutcome{stage3OutcomeFixture(5, "db.t", "p_a"), stage3OutcomeFixture(7, "db.t", "p_a")}, NextAfterPromotionSeq: 7}
	follower := &stage3SafeState{hint: "n2"}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)

// TestStage3ReadsAnswerUnavailableOnAnArbiterWithoutThem: an arbiter v0.12.0
// serves SafeState without the stage-3 methods, and a listener without SafeState
// answers Unimplemented as well; both reads return ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable at
// once instead of retrying (clarification K3: the owner audit then falls back).
func TestStage3ReadsAnswerUnavailableOnAnArbiterWithoutThem(t *testing.T) {
	for name, start := range map[string]func(t *testing.T) string{
		"SafeState without the stage-3 methods": func(t *testing.T) string {
			return startSafeStatePeer(t, &fakeSafeState{code: codes.OK, snapshot: "safe"})
		},
		"no SafeState service": func(t *testing.T) string { return startRegistryPeer(t, newFakeRegistry()) },
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: start(t)})
			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
			defer cancel()
			began := time.Now()
			if _, err := c.GetPartitionStates(ctx, wire.PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: "db.t"}); !errors.Is(err, ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable) {
				t.Fatalf("GetPartitionStates = %v, want ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable", err)
			}
			if _, err := c.GetPromotionOutcomes(ctx, wire.PromotionOutcomesQuery{TableID: "db.t"}); !errors.Is(err, ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable) {
				t.Fatalf("GetPromotionOutcomes = %v, want ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable", err)
			}
			if elapsed := time.Since(began); elapsed > 2*time.Second {
				t.Fatalf("Unimplemented must not be retried: both reads took %v", elapsed)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestStage3ReadsPassOtherRefusalsThrough: the server's shape refusals reach
// the caller unchanged and are not "unavailable".
func TestStage3ReadsPassOtherRefusalsThrough(t *testing.T) {
	peer := &stage3SafeState{}
	c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startStage3Peer(t, peer)})
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		refusal error
		read    func() error
	}{
		{"partition states", status.Error(codes.InvalidArgument, "partition states table_id is required"), func() error {
			_, err := c.GetPartitionStates(ctx, wire.PartitionStatesQuery{})
			return err
		}},
		{"promotion outcomes", status.Error(codes.InvalidArgument, "promotion outcomes limit must be at most 1024"), func() error {
			_, err := c.GetPromotionOutcomes(ctx, wire.PromotionOutcomesQuery{TableID: "db.t", Limit: 1025})
			return err
		}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			peer.setErr(tc.refusal)
			err := tc.read()
			if errors.Is(err, ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable) || status.Code(err) != status.Code(tc.refusal) || status.Convert(err).Message() != status.Convert(tc.refusal).Message() {
				t.Fatalf("read = %v, want %v unchanged", err, tc.refusal)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestGetPartitionStatesRefusesAnAnswerOutsideTheQuery: the reads are
// unauthenticated, so an answer naming a partition the query did not ask for,
// or one partition twice, is refused rather than trusted.
func TestGetPartitionStatesRefusesAnAnswerOutsideTheQuery(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		query  wire.PartitionStatesQuery
		answer []wire.PartitionState
		want   string
	}{
		{"another table", wire.PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: "db.t"}, []wire.PartitionState{{TableID: "db.other", PartitionID: "all"}},
			"dataplane: GetPartitionStates for db.t answered partition db.other/all"},
		{"another partition", wire.PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p_a"}, []wire.PartitionState{{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p_b"}},
			"dataplane: GetPartitionStates for db.t/p_a answered partition db.t/p_b"},
		{"a partition twice", wire.PartitionStatesQuery{TableID: "db.t"}, []wire.PartitionState{{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p_a"}, {TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p_a"}},
			"dataplane: GetPartitionStates answered partition db.t/p_a twice"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			peer := &stage3SafeState{states: wire.PartitionStatesToPB(wire.PartitionStates{Partitions: tc.answer})}
			c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startStage3Peer(t, peer)})
			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
			defer cancel()
			if _, err := c.GetPartitionStates(ctx, tc.query); err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("GetPartitionStates = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestGetPromotionOutcomesRefusesAnAnswerOutsideTheQuery(t *testing.T) {
	otherCommand := stage3OutcomeFixture(3, "db.t", "p_a")

		{"the acknowledgement of another promotion", wire.PromotionOutcomesQuery{TableID: "db.t"}, []wire.PromotionOutcome{otherAck},

			c := newTestClient(t, Peer{ID: "n1", GRPCAddr: startStage3Peer(t, peer)})

			if _, err := c.GetPromotionOutcomes(ctx, tc.query); err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("GetPromotionOutcomes = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Implement the client methods**

Create `dataplane/stage3_reads.go`:

```go
package dataplane

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"

	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
)

// ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable is the answer of an arbiter that predates the
// stage-3 SafeState reads (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §15): it answers
// Unimplemented, which WithLeaderRetry returns at once. A caller falls back
// rather than retries; the owner audit, for one, then audits against the
// SNode's own inventory (plan S3-A clarification K3).
var ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable = errors.New("dataplane: the arbiter does not serve the stage-3 reads")

// GetPartitionStates reads the FSM's promotion state of q's partitions from
// the leader, behind one leader read barrier. It returns an error wrapping
// ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable from an arbiter without the read, any other gRPC
// refusal unchanged, and refuses an answer that names a partition outside q or
// one partition twice (SafeState reads are unauthenticated).
func (c *Client) GetPartitionStates(ctx context.Context, q wire.PartitionStatesQuery) (wire.PartitionStates, error) {
	var out wire.PartitionStates
	err := c.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		m, err := pb.NewSafeStateClient(conn).GetPartitionStates(ctx, wire.PartitionStatesQueryToPB(q))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		out = wire.PartitionStatesFromPB(m)
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return wire.PartitionStates{}, stage3ReadError("GetPartitionStates", err)
	}
	if err := checkPartitionStates(q, out); err != nil {
		return wire.PartitionStates{}, err
	}
	return out, nil
}

// GetPromotionOutcomes reads one page of issued promotions from the leader,
// behind one leader read barrier, with GetPartitionStates' answers. It refuses
// an outcome at or before the cursor or out of ascending order, outside q's
// table or partition, carrying the command or the stored acknowledgement of
// another promotion, and more outcomes than q's limit.
func (c *Client) GetPromotionOutcomes(ctx context.Context, q wire.PromotionOutcomesQuery) (wire.PromotionOutcomes, error) {
	var out wire.PromotionOutcomes
	err := c.WithLeaderRetry(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, conn *grpc.ClientConn) error {
		m, err := pb.NewSafeStateClient(conn).GetPromotionOutcomes(ctx, wire.PromotionOutcomesQueryToPB(q))
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		out = wire.PromotionOutcomesFromPB(m)
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		return wire.PromotionOutcomes{}, stage3ReadError("GetPromotionOutcomes", err)
	}
	if err := checkPromotionOutcomes(q, out); err != nil {
		return wire.PromotionOutcomes{}, err
	}
	return out, nil
}

func stage3ReadError(method string, err error) error {
	if status.Code(err) == codes.Unimplemented {
		return fmt.Errorf("%w (%s: %s)", ErrStage3ReadsUnavailable, method, status.Convert(err).Message())
	}
	return err
}

// readScope names a query's scope in a refusal.
func readScope(table, partition string) string {
	switch {
	case table == "":
		return "every table"
	case partition == "":
		return table
	}
	return table + "/" + partition
}

func checkPartitionStates(q wire.PartitionStatesQuery, s wire.PartitionStates) error {
	seen := make(map[string]bool, len(s.Partitions))
	for _, p := range s.Partitions {
		if p.TableID != q.TableID || (q.PartitionID != "" && p.PartitionID != q.PartitionID) {
			return fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetPartitionStates for %s answered partition %s/%s", readScope(q.TableID, q.PartitionID), p.TableID, p.PartitionID)
		}
		if seen[p.PartitionID] {
			return fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetPartitionStates answered partition %s/%s twice", p.TableID, p.PartitionID)
		}
		seen[p.PartitionID] = true
	}
	return nil
}

func checkPromotionOutcomes(q wire.PromotionOutcomesQuery, o wire.PromotionOutcomes) error {
	if q.Limit != 0 && len(o.Outcomes) > int(q.Limit) {
		return fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetPromotionOutcomes answered %d outcomes for a limit of %d", len(o.Outcomes), q.Limit)
	}
	previous := q.AfterPromotionSeq
	for _, out := range o.Outcomes {
		p := out.Promote
		switch {
		case out.PromotionSeq <= previous:
			return fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetPromotionOutcomes answered promotion %d, which is not after %d", out.PromotionSeq, previous)
		case p.PromotionSeq != out.PromotionSeq:
			return fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetPromotionOutcomes answered promotion %d carrying the command of promotion %d", out.PromotionSeq, p.PromotionSeq)
		case (q.TableID != "" && p.TableID != q.TableID) || (q.PartitionID != "" && p.PartitionID != q.PartitionID):
			return fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetPromotionOutcomes for %s answered promotion %d of %s/%s", readScope(q.TableID, q.PartitionID), out.PromotionSeq, p.TableID, p.PartitionID)
		case out.Ack != nil && (out.Ack.PromotionSeq != out.PromotionSeq || out.Ack.TableID != p.TableID || out.Ack.PartitionID != p.PartitionID):
			return fmt.Errorf("dataplane: GetPromotionOutcomes answered promotion %d with the acknowledgement of %s/%s promotion %d", out.PromotionSeq, out.Ack.TableID, out.Ack.PartitionID, out.Ack.PromotionSeq)
		}
		previous = out.PromotionSeq
	}
	return nil
}
```

## Task 5: arbiter-core — owner hg_safe audit and ClickHouse restart detection (S3-A)

Spec §2 ("Restart resurrection") and §14 bullet 2, as resolved by clarifications K1–K4: `REPLACE PARTITION` on the `hg_safe` MergeTree leaves the replaced parts outdated for `old_parts_lifetime` (480 s), and a ClickHouse restart inside that window reactivates them under their pre-REPLACE names with the `hash_of_all_files` of their replacements, so `hg_safe` serves rows twice and the owner's next promotion of the partition fails its shadow closure gate (`snode/promote_replace.go:349-356`); nothing repairs it today. This task makes the owner SNode audit each `hg_safe` partition against the newer of its own last acknowledged inventory and the FSM's `SafeParts` (Task 4's `GetPartitionStates`) before building each promotion's shadow, at startup, and after every ClickHouse restart (a new `dataplane/chrestart` watcher on `uptime()`). `report` mode (the default) logs at error level and counts; `repair` mode drops resurrected equal-hash twins without an acknowledged name with `DROP PART` and holds an unclean table not-ready, so sentio-node answers it Pending (733) and the SNode builds no shadow for it.

Notes:
- **What is compared.** A part is identified by its name and `hash_of_all_files` (`partInfo.Name`, `PhysHash`; `SafePartMapping.SafePartName`, `PartPhysHash`; `PartManifestEntry.PartName`, `PartPhysHash`): `safeMappings` records exactly those for every active part after REPLACE (`snode/promote_match.go:22-87`), and the FSM stores the same inventory (`arbiter:fsm/apply.go:871-898`). REPLACE copies the shadow's parts, which `prepareShadow` ATTACHed from `hg_safe` (`hash_of_all_files` kept, spec §2), so a resurrected part has an active twin with the same hash under the acknowledged name.
- **The local reference survives a not-applied acknowledgement.** `RecordAck` (a base CAS refusal, `snode/promote.go:70-81`) overwrites `LastAcks[k]`, so the last applied inventory would be lost there. `acked_safe_inventories` keeps it: written by `RecordAppliedPromotion` and by a `RecordRefreshedAck` that completes a legacy acknowledgement, kept by `RecordAck`, forgotten by `ForgetTable`. A v0.14.1 state file has none and loads unchanged: the accessor derives the inventory from an applied `LastAcks` entry with a complete `SafePartitionParts`, and `RecordAck` writes that derivation down before it overwrites the entry; a v0.14.1 binary ignores the field (`openStateStore` uses `json.Unmarshal`, `snode/state.go:101`), and the field is omitted while empty, so a state with no inventory keeps v0.14.1's shape.
- **The reference rule (contract §3, K3).** "Newer by publish seq" between the local inventory (its promotion seq) and the FSM's `SafeParts` (its `PublishSeq`, which only an applied acknowledgement advances). "The FSM is ahead" means ahead of this SNode's own promotion watermark (`Watermarks[k]`, which every journaled acknowledgement, applied or not, advances): the arbiter recorded an applied promotion this SNode has no record of, so its local state is behind and nothing is dropped (`fsm_ahead`). Measured against the local inventory instead, every partition whose last pre-upgrade acknowledgement was a not-applied one would be permanently unclean and its promotions refused. Equal seqs with different inventories are `fsm_disagrees`. An FSM that answers without an entry for the partition is an authoritative empty inventory at seq 0: the arbiter lists a partition only once an applied acknowledgement reached it (it has a promotion base, a safe-part inventory or a promoted unsafe part; contract §1, Task 3's field comments, Task 7's `PartitionStates`), so a partition whose promotions are all unacknowledged or acknowledged with `applied=false` has no entry even when the audit names it. The audit never reads `UnackedPromotionSeq` (a first promotion in flight has no entry to carry it): a partition's unresolved promotion intent is the SNode's own journal (K4, "Unresolved intent" below). An FSM read failure of any kind (an arbiter `v0.12.0`'s `Unimplemented`, a timeout of `OwnerAuditFSMTimeout`, a reply refused by the client's checks) counts `FSMUnavailable` and leaves the audit on the local inventory; only a partition with parts and no reference at all is `no_acknowledged_inventory`.
- **The repair rule (K2).** Of each group of active parts with one `hash_of_all_files`, the members whose (name, hash) the reference carries are kept and every other member is a resurrected twin. The plan drops twins only when the drops leave the active set exactly equal to the reference (contract §3, "Repair"): any part without an acknowledged twin — a twin group in which no member carries an acknowledged name, or a single unacknowledged part (a foreign insert or an `OPTIMIZE` rename included) — is `unacknowledged_part`, any acknowledged part missing is `acknowledged_part_missing`, and either makes the partition unclean with nothing dropped, as does the FSM ahead of this SNode (`fsm_ahead`) or disagreeing with it (`fsm_disagrees`), where no reference is chosen at all. Repair mode issues `ALTER TABLE <hg_safe>.<table> DROP PART '<name>'` per twin, lists the partition again and requires the result to match the reference; a zero-row covering part (none on upstream 26.3 per K2; M11 pins the deployed image) would be an unacknowledged part, so it fails safe.
- **Unresolved intent (K4).** A startup or restart pass skips a partition whose promotion intent is journaled and not finalized and records `unresolved_intent`: its redelivery reconciles it (`reconcilePromotionIntent`), and a resurrection under such an intent fails that reconciliation forever (`snode/promote_replace.go:138-140`), which is a runbook repair (Plan S3-B). The promotion trigger runs after `handlePromote` reconciled the intent and passed the base CAS: a published intent never reaches it (`finishAppliedPromotion` takes it), and an intent whose REPLACE is not visible leaves `hg_safe` at the base it recorded, which the same command then rebuilds, so the trigger audits that base like any other. `finishAppliedPromotion` clears the partition's finding: `safeMappings` has just scanned the whole published partition, refused a duplicate row LtHash and proved its closure, and the journaled inventory is exactly that scan.
- **Gate (K1).** `OwnerAuditClean` is true in report mode. In repair mode it is false while the table has a finding, and from `New` (or from a detected restart) until a full pass has taken its table set and audited that table; a pass that fails on a table (a ClickHouse or schema error) leaves it held and is retried every probe interval. While no pass is due, repair mode re-audits every probe interval each partition that has a finding (`reauditFindings`, under the finding's trigger, not counted as a run), so a partition an operator repaired, or one that lacked a reference only while the arbiter was unreachable, stops holding its table without a promotion of that partition or a restart; report mode holds nothing, so its findings stand until the partition's next audit. `TableReady` folds it in, so sentio-node's table state answers Pending (`sentio-node:storageintegrityadapter/tablestate/snapshot.go:186-189`) and housegate refuses with the retryable 733. Repair mode also refuses a promotion of an unclean partition with `ErrSafePartitionUnclean` before `prepareShadow`, so the subscription redelivers it (`dispatchPromotionCommand` logs it at error level, `snode/snode.go:619-630`). Intake (`requireAdmissible`, `snode/registry.go:72-94`) is unchanged: it writes `hg_unsafe`, which the audit does not judge, and the host refuses writes to a Pending table first.
- **Report mode changes nothing.** It audits, logs and counts with the same code, but never issues a `DROP PART`, never refuses a promotion (an audit error is logged and the promotion continues), and never holds a table. The existing tests that place non-acknowledged parts in `hg_safe` on purpose (`TestHandlePromote_PreReplaceIntentRecoversAfterContentNeutralSafeRewrite` at `snode/promote_test.go:344`, an OPTIMIZE rename; `TestHandlePromote_ShadowClosureMismatchNamesReactivatedSafePart` at `:523`, a foreign insert) stay green because the default is report.
- **Restart detection.** `chrestart` uses the server's start time (`now - uptime()`), not "uptime decreased", which misses a restart whose new uptime at the next probe exceeds the previous one. The baseline is read before the startup pass and handed to the watcher (`Watcher.Baseline`), so a restart during the startup pass is detected; a restart while the server had been up for less than the skew is not, which needs two restarts within five seconds. The SNode's ClickHouse address must reach a single server (sentio-node's DSN is one address, `standalone/standalone.go:212-214`): a pool spanning servers would mix their start times. After a restart ClickHouse may accept queries while it still loads tables, and `system.parts` lists no part of an unloaded table, which would read as every acknowledged part missing; the audit therefore queries the table first (`SELECT 1 FROM <hg_safe>.<table> LIMIT 0` waits for its load; `UNKNOWN_TABLE` / `UNKNOWN_DATABASE` mean no parts yet). The restart test exercises this.
- **Locks.** A promotion holds `promotionLock(k)` through its audit; a full pass takes `auditPassMu`, then `promotionLock(k)` per partition, then the state store; nothing takes `auditPassMu` while holding a promotion lock. The audit state's mutex is a leaf.
- **Cost.** Each promotion adds one `SELECT ... LIMIT 0`, one `system.parts` listing and one `GetPartitionStates` read (bounded by `OwnerAuditFSMTimeout`); a full pass costs one FSM read per table and one listing per partition, and after its first failed FSM read no further one: an unreachable arbiter delays a pass, and so the startup that runs the startup pass before the subscription, by one `OwnerAuditFSMTimeout`, not one per table, so report mode keeps the owner's startup decoupled from the arbiter (K3).
- **CI.** The ClickHouse-gated tests run in the existing `integration-clickhouse` job (with Task 4's credentials). The restart test restarts its server, so it must not share one with other targets: Task 6's `scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh` runs it after the mechanics suite, inside the script, as a second Bazel invocation against node B (`CH_RESTART_ADDR`, `--restart always`, fixed host port) with `--test_filter=^TestOwnerAuditRepairsResurrectedPartsAcrossAClickHouseRestart$ --test_arg=-test.v --nocache_test_results --test_output=errors`, and fails unless the test log carries `--- PASS:` lines for the test and for its `repair` and `report` subtests (a filter that matches nothing, or a test that skips for a missing variable, passes silently; `-test.v` is what makes Go print the PASS lines). Because it is inside the script, the restart test runs in CI's `clickhouse-mechanics` job, in Cut Release's `validate ClickHouse mechanics` step and in the manual deployed-image run (Task 6 Step 16), not only in CI. Step 10 runs it locally with the same filter, `-test.v` and PASS grep.

```go
package chrestart

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"testing/synctest"
	"time"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
	"github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2/lib/driver"
)

var errServerDown = errors.New("dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9000: connect: connection refused")

// fakeServer is a clickhouse.Conn whose only query is uptime(), answered from a
// start time the test sets (inside a synctest bubble time is synthetic). Any
// other method is unimplemented (the embedded nil Conn panics).
type fakeServer struct {
	clickhouse.Conn
	mu      sync.Mutex
	started time.Time
	down    bool
	queries []string
}

func (s *fakeServer) QueryRow(_ context.Context, query string, _ ...any) driver.Row {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.queries = append(s.queries, query)
	if s.down {
		return uptimeRow{err: errServerDown}
	}
	return uptimeRow{uptime: uint64(time.Since(s.started) / time.Second)}
}

func (s *fakeServer) setStarted(at time.Time) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.started = at
}

func (s *fakeServer) startedAt() time.Time {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return s.started
}

func (s *fakeServer) setDown(down bool) {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	s.down = down
}

func (s *fakeServer) probes() []string {
	s.mu.Lock()
	defer s.mu.Unlock()
	return append([]string(nil), s.queries...)
}

type uptimeRow struct {
	uptime uint64
	err    error
}

func (r uptimeRow) Err() error { return r.err }

func (r uptimeRow) Scan(dest ...any) error {
	if r.err != nil {
		return r.err
	}
	if len(dest) != 1 {
		return fmt.Errorf("scan into %d destinations, want 1", len(dest))
	}
	p, ok := dest[0].(*uint64)
	if !ok {
		return fmt.Errorf("scan into %T, want *uint64", dest[0])
	}
	*p = r.uptime
	return nil
}

func (r uptimeRow) ScanStruct(any) error { return errors.New("uptimeRow: ScanStruct is not supported") }

// restarts records every OnRestart call.
type restarts struct {
	mu   sync.Mutex
	seen [][2]time.Time
}

func (r *restarts) record(_ context.Context, previous, current time.Time) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.seen = append(r.seen, [2]time.Time{previous, current})
}

func (r *restarts) all() [][2]time.Time {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	return append([][2]time.Time(nil), r.seen...)
}

// run runs w on conn in the background; stop cancels it and waits for Run to
// return.
func run(w *Watcher, conn clickhouse.Conn) (stop func()) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		w.Run(ctx, conn)
	}()
	return func() {
		cancel()
		<-done
	}
}

// TestStartedAtIsNowMinusUptime: the start time is the caller's clock minus
// uptime(), from one query; a failed probe is an error, never a time.
func TestStartedAtIsNowMinusUptime(t *testing.T) {
	synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) {
		server := &fakeServer{started: time.Now().Add(-42 * time.Second)}
		got, err := StartedAt(context.Background(), server, time.Now())
		if err != nil || !got.Equal(server.startedAt()) {
			t.Fatalf("StartedAt = %v, %v; want %v", got, err, server.startedAt())
		}
		if q := server.probes(); len(q) != 1 || q[0] != "SELECT toUInt64(uptime())" {
			t.Fatalf("queries = %q, want the one uptime() probe", q)
		}
		server.setDown(true)
		if got, err := StartedAt(context.Background(), server, time.Now()); !errors.Is(err, errServerDown) || !got.IsZero() {
			t.Fatalf("StartedAt of a down server = %v, %v; want the probe error", got, err)
		}
	})
}

// TestWatcherReportsARestart: a start time that moves later by more than the
// skew is a restart, reported once with both start times (housegate spec
// 2026-10-14 §14: the audit reruns after every ClickHouse restart).
func TestWatcherReportsARestart(t *testing.T) {
	synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) {
		server := &fakeServer{started: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)}
		var log restarts
		stop := run(&Watcher{Interval: time.Second, OnRestart: log.record}, server)
		defer stop()
		time.Sleep(10 * time.Second)
		synctest.Wait()
		if got := log.all(); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("restarts while the server ran = %v", got)
		}
		before := server.startedAt()
		server.setStarted(time.Now())
		after := server.startedAt()
		time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)
		synctest.Wait()
		got := log.all()
		if len(got) != 1 || !got[0][0].Equal(before) || !got[0][1].Equal(after) {
			t.Fatalf("restarts = %v, want one from %v to %v", got, before, after)
		}
	})
}

// TestWatcherDetectsARestartEvenWhenTheNewUptimeIsLarger: with a probe interval
// longer than the uptime the server had when it restarted, the next probe finds
// a larger uptime than the previous one. A rule of "uptime decreased" misses
// that restart; the start time does not.
func TestWatcherDetectsARestartEvenWhenTheNewUptimeIsLarger(t *testing.T) {
	synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) {
		server := &fakeServer{started: time.Now().Add(-30 * time.Second)}
		var log restarts
		stop := run(&Watcher{Interval: time.Minute, OnRestart: log.record}, server)
		defer stop()
		synctest.Wait() // the first probe: uptime 30s
		time.Sleep(time.Second)
		server.setStarted(time.Now()) // up 31s, then restarted
		time.Sleep(time.Minute)       // the next probe finds uptime 59s
		synctest.Wait()
		if got := log.all(); len(got) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("restarts = %v, want the one restart", got)
		}
	})
}

// TestWatcherIgnoresProbeErrorsAndJitter: a failed probe (the server is down)
// is not a restart and keeps the previous start time; a start time that moves
// by less than the skew (uptime()'s one-second resolution, a clock adjustment)
// is not one either. The watcher keeps probing every interval meanwhile.
func TestWatcherIgnoresProbeErrorsAndJitter(t *testing.T) {
	synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) {
		server := &fakeServer{started: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)}
		var log restarts
		stop := run(&Watcher{Interval: time.Second, OnRestart: log.record}, server)
		defer stop()
		time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
		server.setDown(true)
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Second)
		server.setDown(false)
		time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
		server.setStarted(server.startedAt().Add(DefaultRestartSkew - time.Second))
		time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)
		synctest.Wait()
		if got := log.all(); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("restarts = %v, want none", got)
		}
		if n := len(server.probes()); n < 12 {
			t.Fatalf("probes = %d, want one a second", n)
		}
	})
}

// TestWatcherReportsARestartBeforeItsFirstProbe: a Baseline the caller observed
// earlier (before the startup audit) makes a restart between that observation
// and the first probe a restart too. Without a Baseline the first probe only
// sets the baseline.
func TestWatcherReportsARestartBeforeItsFirstProbe(t *testing.T) {
	synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) {
		baseline := time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)
		server := &fakeServer{started: time.Now().Add(-10 * time.Second)}
		var log restarts
		stop := run(&Watcher{Interval: time.Second, OnRestart: log.record, Baseline: baseline}, server)
		synctest.Wait()
		stop()
		got := log.all()
		if len(got) != 1 || !got[0][0].Equal(baseline) || !got[0][1].Equal(server.startedAt()) {
			t.Fatalf("restarts = %v, want one from the baseline %v to %v", got, baseline, server.startedAt())
		}
		var none restarts
		stopNone := run(&Watcher{Interval: time.Second, OnRestart: none.record}, server)
		synctest.Wait()
		stopNone()
		if got := none.all(); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("restarts without a baseline = %v", got)
		}
	})
}

// TestWatcherStopsWithItsContext: Run returns once its context ends, also while
// it waits for the next probe, and the zero Watcher probes every second.
func TestWatcherStopsWithItsContext(t *testing.T) {
	synctest.Test(t, func(t *testing.T) {
		server := &fakeServer{started: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)}
		var w Watcher
		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
		done := make(chan struct{})
		go func() {
			defer close(done)
			w.Run(ctx, server)
		}()
		time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)
		synctest.Wait()
		cancel()
		<-done
		if n := len(server.probes()); n != 4 {
			t.Fatalf("probes of the zero Watcher in 3s = %d, want 4 (at 0s, 1s, 2s and 3s)", n)
		}
	})
}
```

```go
// Package chrestart detects that a ClickHouse server restarted, from its
// uptime(). A restart inside old_parts_lifetime reactivates the parts a
// REPLACE PARTITION retired (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §2), so every hg_safe
// audit must run again after one (spec §14; the stage-3 member's startup
// audit, §8.7, reruns on the same signal).
//
// The rule is the server's start time, now minus uptime(), not "uptime
// decreased": a restart moves the start time later by at least the uptime
// the server had when it went down, even when the next probe finds a larger
// uptime than the previous one. A probe that fails (the server is down) is
// not a restart; the next successful probe decides. One connection must
// reach one server: a pool spanning several would mix their start times.
package chrestart

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
)

// DefaultRestartSkew is how far the start time must move before a Watcher
// with a zero Skew reports a restart: uptime() has a one-second resolution and
// the caller's clock may be adjusted, so smaller movements are noise.
const DefaultRestartSkew = 5 * time.Second

// StartedAt returns when the server behind conn started: now minus its
// uptime().
func StartedAt(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, now time.Time) (time.Time, error) {
	var uptime uint64
	if err := conn.QueryRow(ctx, "SELECT toUInt64(uptime())").Scan(&uptime); err != nil {
		return time.Time{}, fmt.Errorf("chrestart: read the server uptime: %w", err)
	}
	return now.Add(-time.Duration(uptime) * time.Second), nil
}

// Watcher probes one server's start time and reports when it moved later.
type Watcher struct {
	// Interval paces the probes and bounds each one; non-positive probes
	// every second.
	Interval time.Duration
	// Skew is the movement that counts as a restart; non-positive is
	// DefaultRestartSkew.
	Skew time.Duration
	// Now is the clock; nil is time.Now.
	Now func() time.Time
	// OnRestart is called on the watcher's goroutine with the start times
	// before and after a restart; the next probe waits for it.
	OnRestart func(ctx context.Context, previous, current time.Time)
	// Baseline is a start time the caller already observed (before a startup
	// audit, say), so a restart between that observation and the first probe
	// is reported too. Zero makes the first successful probe the baseline.
	Baseline time.Time
}

// Run probes conn until ctx ends: once at once, then every Interval.
func (w *Watcher) Run(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn) {
	interval := w.Interval
	if interval <= 0 {
		interval = time.Second
	}
	skew := w.Skew
	if skew <= 0 {
		skew = DefaultRestartSkew
	}
	now := w.Now
	if now == nil {
		now = time.Now
	}
	previous := w.Baseline
	timer := time.NewTimer(0)
	defer timer.Stop()
	for {
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return
		case <-timer.C:
		}
		probeCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, interval)
		current, err := StartedAt(probeCtx, conn, now())
		cancel()
		if err == nil {
			if !previous.IsZero() && current.After(previous.Add(skew)) && w.OnRestart != nil {
				w.OnRestart(ctx, previous, current)
			}
			previous = current
		}
		timer.Reset(interval)
	}
}
```

```go
package snode

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"testing"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
)

func ackedInventoryS(names ...string) []arbiter.SafePartMapping {
	out := make([]arbiter.SafePartMapping, 0, len(names))
	for _, name := range names {
		out = append(out, arbiter.SafePartMapping{PartRowLtHash: "0xrow-" + name, SafePartName: name, PartPhysHash: "0xphys-" + name})
	}
	return out
}

// TestStateStore_AckedSafeInventorySurvivesANotAppliedAck: a base CAS refusal
// replaces LastAcks, but the owner audit's local reference stays the last
// applied inventory, across a reopen (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14).
func TestStateStore_AckedSafeInventorySurvivesANotAppliedAck(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	st, err := openStateStore(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	k := partitionKey{Table: "db.t", Partition: "all"}
	inventory := ackedInventoryS("all_2_2_0", "all_3_3_0")
	applied := arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: "s1", PromotionSeq: 3, TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "all", PostPartitionCommitment: "0xpost", Applied: true, SafePartitionParts: inventory}
	if err := st.RecordAppliedPromotion(k, 3, applied, "0xpost", "snap-3", nil, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	refused := arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: "s1", PromotionSeq: 4, TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "all", Detail: "base CAS mismatch"}
	if err := st.RecordAck(k, 4, refused, "0xpost", "snap-3"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := ackedSafeInventory{PromotionSeq: 3, Parts: inventory}
	if got, ok := st.AckedSafeInventory(k); !ok || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("inventory after a not-applied ack = %+v, %v; want %+v", got, ok, want)
	}
	reopened, err := openStateStore(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, ok := reopened.AckedSafeInventory(k); !ok || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("inventory after a reopen = %+v, %v; want %+v", got, ok, want)
	}
	if last, _ := reopened.LastAck(k); last.PromotionSeq != 4 || last.Applied {
		t.Fatalf("LastAck = %+v, want the not-applied promotion 4", last)
	}
}

// TestStateStore_AckedSafeInventoriesIsAnOptionalJSONField: a state file written
// by v0.14.1 has no acked_safe_inventories. It loads unchanged, the inventory is
// derived from its applied LastAcks entry, a write that records no inventory
// keeps v0.14.1's shape, and a not-applied acknowledgement writes the derived
// inventory down before it replaces that entry.
func TestStateStore_AckedSafeInventoriesIsAnOptionalJSONField(t *testing.T) {
	dir := t.TempDir()
	path := filepath.Join(dir, "state.json")
	v0141 := `{"watermarks":{"db.t\u0000all":5},"last_acks":{"db.t\u0000all":{"node_id":"s1","promotion_seq":5,"table_id":"db.t","partition_id":"all",` +
		`"post_partition_commitment":"0xpost","parts":null,"safe_partition_parts":[{"part_row_lthash":"0xrow","safe_part_name":"all_7_7_0","part_phys_hash":"0xphys"}],"applied":true}},` +
		`"base_roots":{"db.t\u0000all":"0xpost"},"base_snapshot_ids":{"db.t\u0000all":"snap"},"unpromoted_sums":{}}`
	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(v0141), 0o600); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	st, err := openStateStore(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a v0.14.1 state file: %v", err)
	}
	k := partitionKey{Table: "db.t", Partition: "all"}
	want := ackedSafeInventory{PromotionSeq: 5, Parts: []arbiter.SafePartMapping{{PartRowLtHash: "0xrow", SafePartName: "all_7_7_0", PartPhysHash: "0xphys"}}}
	if got, ok := st.AckedSafeInventory(k); !ok || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("derived inventory = %+v, %v; want %+v", got, ok, want)
	}
	if got := st.ackedInventoryPartitions("db.t"); !slices.Equal(got, []string{"all"}) {
		t.Fatalf("partitions with an inventory = %v, want [all]", got)
	}
	fields := func() map[string]json.RawMessage {
		t.Helper()
		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		var out map[string]json.RawMessage
		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &out); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return out
	}
	if _, err := st.NextRegistrationSeq(100); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if raw, ok := fields()["acked_safe_inventories"]; ok {
		t.Fatalf("a write that recorded no inventory wrote acked_safe_inventories %s", raw)
	}
	refused := arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: "s1", PromotionSeq: 6, TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "all", Detail: "base CAS mismatch"}
	if err := st.RecordAck(k, 6, refused, "0xpost", "snap"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var stored map[string]ackedSafeInventory
	if err := json.Unmarshal(fields()["acked_safe_inventories"], &stored); err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(stored, map[string]ackedSafeInventory{key("db.t", "all"): want}) {
		t.Fatalf("acked_safe_inventories = %v (%v), want the derived inventory", stored, err)
	}
	reopened, err := openStateStore(dir)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, ok := reopened.AckedSafeInventory(k); !ok || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("inventory after the not-applied ack and a reopen = %+v, %v; want %+v", got, ok, want)
	}
}

// TestStateStore_RecordRefreshedAckKeepsTheAppliedInventory: refreshing a
// legacy acknowledgement completes a missing inventory, but never replaces the
// one the applied promotion recorded for the same seq, which describes hg_safe
// as REPLACE left it.
func TestStateStore_RecordRefreshedAckKeepsTheAppliedInventory(t *testing.T) {
	st, err := openStateStore(t.TempDir())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	ack := arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: "s1", PromotionSeq: 4, TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "all", PostPartitionCommitment: "0xpost", Applied: true,
		SafePartitionParts: ackedInventoryS("all_4_4_0")}
	if err := st.RecordAppliedPromotion(k, 4, ack, "0xpost", "snap-4", nil, nil); err != nil {

	refreshed.SafePartitionParts = ackedInventoryS("all_4_4_1")

		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, _ := st.AckedSafeInventory(k); !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Parts, ackedInventoryS("all_4_4_0")) {
		t.Fatalf("inventory after a refresh = %+v, want the applied one", got)
	}
	legacyKey := partitionKey{Table: "db.u", Partition: "all"}
	legacy := arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: "s1", PromotionSeq: 5, TableID: "db.u", PartitionID: "all", PostPartitionCommitment: "0xpost-u", Applied: true}
	if err := st.RecordAppliedPromotion(legacyKey, 5, legacy, "0xpost-u", "snap-5", nil, nil); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := st.AckedSafeInventory(legacyKey); ok {
		t.Fatal("an applied acknowledgement without an inventory recorded one")
	}
	legacy.SafePartitionParts = ackedInventoryS("all_5_5_0")
	if err := st.RecordRefreshedAck(legacyKey, legacy); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, ok := st.AckedSafeInventory(legacyKey); !ok || got.PromotionSeq != 5 || !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Parts, ackedInventoryS("all_5_5_0")) {
		t.Fatalf("inventory after refreshing a legacy acknowledgement = %+v, %v", got, ok)
	}
}

// TestStateStore_ForgetTableForgetsAckedSafeInventories: a dropped table's
// inventory goes with its other per-partition state; another table's stays.
func TestStateStore_ForgetTableForgetsAckedSafeInventories(t *testing.T) {
	st, err := openStateStore(t.TempDir())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	k, other := partitionKey{Table: "db.t", Partition: "all"}, partitionKey{Table: "db.u", Partition: "all"}
	for i, pk := range []partitionKey{k, other} {
		seq := uint64(i + 2)
		ack := arbiter.PromotionAck{NodeID: "s1", PromotionSeq: seq, TableID: pk.Table, PartitionID: pk.Partition, PostPartitionCommitment: "0xpost", Applied: true, SafePartitionParts: ackedInventoryS("all_1_1_0")}
		if err := st.RecordAppliedPromotion(pk, seq, ack, "0xpost", "snap", nil, nil); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if err := st.ForgetTable("db.t"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := st.AckedSafeInventory(k); ok {
		t.Fatal("ForgetTable kept the dropped table's inventory")
	}
	if _, ok := st.AckedSafeInventory(other); !ok {
		t.Fatal("ForgetTable dropped another table's inventory")
	}
}
```

```go
// AckedSafeInventory returns k's acknowledged inventory (ackedSafeInventory).
func (st *stateStore) AckedSafeInventory(k partitionKey) (ackedSafeInventory, bool) {
	st.mu.Lock()
	defer st.mu.Unlock()
	return st.s.ackedSafeInventory(key(k.Table, k.Partition))
}

// ackedInventoryPartitions returns, sorted, the partitions of table that have
// an acknowledged inventory, recorded or derived.
func (st *stateStore) ackedInventoryPartitions(table string) []string {
	st.mu.Lock()
	defer st.mu.Unlock()
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, keys := range [][]string{slices.Collect(maps.Keys(st.s.AckedSafeInventories)), slices.Collect(maps.Keys(st.s.LastAcks))} {
		for _, ks := range keys {
			if pk, ok := splitKey(ks); ok && pk.Table == table {
				if _, has := st.s.ackedSafeInventory(ks); has {
					seen[pk.Partition] = true
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(seen))
}

// ackedSafeInventory returns ks's recorded inventory, else the one an applied
// LastAcks entry with a complete SafePartitionParts carries (a state written
// before acked_safe_inventories).
func (s *localState) ackedSafeInventory(ks string) (ackedSafeInventory, bool) {
	if inv, ok := s.AckedSafeInventories[ks]; ok {
		return cloneAckedSafeInventory(inv), true
	}
	if ack, ok := s.LastAcks[ks]; ok && ack.Applied && len(ack.SafePartitionParts) > 0 {
		return ackedSafeInventory{PromotionSeq: ack.PromotionSeq, Parts: slices.Clone(ack.SafePartitionParts)}, true
	}
	return ackedSafeInventory{}, false
}

// recordAckedSafeInventory makes an applied acknowledgement's complete
// inventory ks's acknowledged inventory. An applied acknowledgement without
// one (a pre-v0.7.0 promotion) leaves no stale inventory behind.
func (s *localState) recordAckedSafeInventory(ks string, ack arbiter.PromotionAck) {
	if !ack.Applied {
		return
	}
	if len(ack.SafePartitionParts) == 0 {
		delete(s.AckedSafeInventories, ks)
		return
	}
	s.AckedSafeInventories[ks] = ackedSafeInventory{PromotionSeq: ack.PromotionSeq, Parts: slices.Clone(ack.SafePartitionParts)}
}

func cloneAckedSafeInventory(inv ackedSafeInventory) ackedSafeInventory {
	inv.Parts = slices.Clone(inv.Parts)
	return inv
}
```

```go
func (st *stateStore) RecordAck(k partitionKey, seq uint64, ack arbiter.PromotionAck, newBaseRoot, newBaseSnapshotID string) error {
	st.mu.Lock()
	defer st.mu.Unlock()
	ks := key(k.Table, k.Partition)
	next := cloneLocalState(st.s)
	// A not-applied acknowledgement replaces LastAcks[ks]: write down the
	// applied inventory a state from before acked_safe_inventories carries
	// only there, so the owner audit keeps its reference.
	if inv, ok := st.s.ackedSafeInventory(ks); ok {
		next.AckedSafeInventories[ks] = inv
	}
	next.Watermarks[ks] = seq
	next.LastAcks[ks] = ack
	next.BaseRoots[ks] = newBaseRoot
	next.BaseSnapshotIDs[ks] = newBaseSnapshotID
	return st.persistStateLocked(next)
}
```

```go
// TestPlanOwnerAudit pins the repair rule (plan S3-A contract §3, clarification
// K2): of equal-hash twins keep the acknowledged name and drop the others, but
// only when that leaves exactly the reference; anything else is unclean and
// drops nothing.
func TestPlanOwnerAudit(t *testing.T) {
	part := func(name, hash string) partInfo {
		return partInfo{Name: name, PartitionID: "p0id", PartitionValue: "p0", PhysHash: hash, Rows: 2}
	}

		return ownerAuditReference{Source: "local", Seq: 7, Parts: parts}
	}

	acked := func(p ownerAuditPart) partInfo { return part(p.Name, p.PhysHash) }

		name    string

		haveRef bool

		reason  OwnerAuditReason
		parts   []string
		drop    []string
	}{
		{"the acknowledged inventory exactly", ref(a, b), true, []partInfo{acked(a), acked(b)}, "", nil, nil},
		{"a resurrected twin", ref(a, b), true, []partInfo{part("p0_1_1_0", "hA"), acked(a), acked(b)},
			OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart, []string{"p0_1_1_0"}, []string{"p0_1_1_0"}},
		{"three-way twins from two REPLACEs inside old_parts_lifetime",
			ref(ownerAuditPart{"p0_9_9_0", "hA"}, ownerAuditPart{"p0_10_10_0", "hB"}, ownerAuditPart{"p0_11_11_0", "hC"}), true,
			[]partInfo{part("p0_1_1_0", "hA"), part("p0_5_5_0", "hA"), part("p0_9_9_0", "hA"), part("p0_6_6_0", "hB"), part("p0_10_10_0", "hB"), part("p0_11_11_0", "hC")},
			OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart, []string{"p0_1_1_0", "p0_5_5_0", "p0_6_6_0"}, []string{"p0_1_1_0", "p0_5_5_0", "p0_6_6_0"}},
		{"twins without an acknowledged name", ref(a), true, []partInfo{part("p0_1_1_0", "hA"), part("p0_3_3_0", "hA")},
			OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart, []string{"p0_1_1_0", "p0_3_3_0"}, nil},
		{"a foreign part without a twin", ref(a), true, []partInfo{acked(a), part("p0_99_99_0", "hF")},

		{"a content-neutral rename (an OPTIMIZE)", ref(a), true, []partInfo{part("p0_7_7_1", "hA")}, OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart, []string{"p0_7_7_1"}, nil},

// TestOwnerAuditReferenceFor pins the reference rule (contract §3, K3): the
// newer by publish seq of this SNode's acknowledged inventory and the arbiter's
// SafeParts; the arbiter ahead of this SNode's own watermark, or disagreeing at
// the same seq, is unclean; an unreadable arbiter leaves the local inventory.
func TestOwnerAuditReferenceFor(t *testing.T) {
	mapping := func(name, hash string) arbiter.SafePartMapping {
		return arbiter.SafePartMapping{PartRowLtHash: "0xrow-" + name, SafePartName: name, PartPhysHash: hash}
	}
	entry := func(name, hash string) replay.PartManifestEntry {
		return replay.PartManifestEntry{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p_p0", PartName: name, PartPhysHash: hash, PartRowLtHash: "0xrow-" + name}
	}
	fsmAt := func(seq uint64, entries ...replay.PartManifestEntry) *wire.PartitionState {
		return &wire.PartitionState{TableID: "db.t", PartitionID: "p_p0", PublishSeq: seq, SafeParts: entries}
	}
	localAt := func(seq uint64) *ackedSafeInventory {
		return &ackedSafeInventory{PromotionSeq: seq, Parts: []arbiter.SafePartMapping{mapping("p0_8_8_0", "hA"), mapping("p0_9_9_0", "hB")}}
	}
	inventory := []ownerAuditPart{{"p0_8_8_0", "hA"}, {"p0_9_9_0", "hB"}}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		in      ownerAuditInputs
		ok      bool
		refusal OwnerAuditReason
		source  string
		seq     uint64
		parts   []ownerAuditPart
	}{
		{"the local inventory when the arbiter is unavailable", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 4, Local: localAt(4)}, true, "", "local", 4, inventory},
		{"the arbiter's when this SNode has none", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 5, FSMAvailable: true, FSM: fsmAt(4, entry("p0_8_8_0", "hA"), entry("p0_9_9_0", "hB"))},
			true, "", "fsm", 4, inventory},
		{"the local one while the arbiter has not applied the last acknowledgement", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 5, Local: localAt(5), FSMAvailable: true,
			FSM: fsmAt(4, entry("p0_1_1_0", "hA"))}, true, "", "local", 5, inventory},
		{"the arbiter's when it is newer than the local one", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 6, Local: localAt(4), FSMAvailable: true,
			FSM: fsmAt(5, entry("p0_10_10_0", "hA"))}, true, "", "fsm", 5, []ownerAuditPart{{"p0_10_10_0", "hA"}}},
		{"the same inventory at the same promotion", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 4, Local: localAt(4), FSMAvailable: true,
			FSM: fsmAt(4, entry("p0_9_9_0", "hB"), entry("p0_8_8_0", "hA"))}, true, "", "local", 4, inventory},
		{"the arbiter ahead of this SNode's watermark", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 4, Local: localAt(4), FSMAvailable: true,
			FSM: fsmAt(6, entry("p0_8_8_0", "hA"))}, false, OwnerAuditFSMAhead, "", 0, nil},
		{"another inventory at the same promotion", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 4, Local: localAt(4), FSMAvailable: true,
			FSM: fsmAt(4, entry("p0_8_8_0", "hA"), entry("p0_1_1_0", "hB"))}, false, OwnerAuditFSMDisagrees, "", 0, nil},
		{"nothing when neither is there", ownerAuditInputs{}, false, "", "", 0, nil},
		{"the arbiter's empty inventory when it never promoted the partition", ownerAuditInputs{FSMAvailable: true}, true, "", "fsm", 0, nil},
		{"the local one when the arbiter never promoted the partition", ownerAuditInputs{Watermark: 4, Local: localAt(4), FSMAvailable: true}, true, "", "local", 4, inventory},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ref, ok, refusal, detail := ownerAuditReferenceFor(tc.in)
			if ok != tc.ok || refusal != tc.refusal || (refusal != "" && detail == "") {
				t.Fatalf("reference = ok %v refusal %q detail %q, want ok %v refusal %q", ok, refusal, detail, tc.ok, tc.refusal)
			}
			if ok && (ref.Source != tc.source || ref.Seq != tc.seq || !samePartSet(ref.Parts, tc.parts)) {
				t.Fatalf("reference = %+v, want %s at %d with %v", ref, tc.source, tc.seq, tc.parts)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestOwnerAuditStateHoldsATableUntilItsAuditCompletes: before the startup pass
// takes its table set every table is held, a table of the pass is held until it
// is audited, a finding holds its table, a restart holds every table again and
// wakes the worker, and a dropped table is forgotten. A nil state holds nothing.
func TestOwnerAuditStateHoldsATableUntilItsAuditCompletes(t *testing.T) {
	a := newOwnerAuditState(true)
	if !a.blocks("db.a") || !a.due() {
		t.Fatal("before the startup pass every table is held")
	}
	if trigger := a.begin([]string{"db.a", "db.b"}); trigger != OwnerAuditTriggerStartup {
		t.Fatalf("the first pass's trigger = %q, want startup", trigger)
	}
	if !a.blocks("db.a") || !a.blocks("db.b") || a.blocks("db.c") {
		t.Fatal("a pass holds exactly its own tables until they are audited")
	}
	a.tableDone("db.a")
	if a.blocks("db.a") || !a.blocks("db.b") || !a.due() {
		t.Fatal("an audited table is released, the others of the pass stay held")
	}
	a.tableDone("db.b")
	if a.blocks("db.b") || a.due() {
		t.Fatal("a completed pass holds nothing")
	}
	k := partitionKey{Table: "db.b", Partition: "all"}
	finding := OwnerAuditFinding{TableID: k.Table, PartitionID: k.Partition, Reason: OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart, Parts: []string{"all_1_1_0"}, Trigger: OwnerAuditTriggerStartup}
	if !a.set(finding) || a.set(finding) {
		t.Fatal("set must report a new finding as changed and the same finding again as unchanged")
	}
	if !a.blocks("db.b") || a.blocks("db.a") || !slices.Equal(a.findingPartitions("db.b"), []string{"all"}) || !slices.Equal(a.findingTables(), []string{"db.b"}) {
		t.Fatal("a finding holds exactly its table")
	}
	if got, ok := a.finding(k); !ok || got.Reason != OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart {
		t.Fatalf("finding = %+v, %v", got, ok)
	}
	a.clear(k)
	if a.blocks("db.b") {
		t.Fatal("a cleared finding still holds its table")
	}
	a.restarted()
	if !a.blocks("db.a") || !a.due() {
		t.Fatal("after a ClickHouse restart every table is held again")
	}
	select {
	case <-a.wake:
	default:
		t.Fatal("a restart must wake the worker")
	}
	if trigger := a.begin([]string{"db.a"}); trigger != OwnerAuditTriggerClickHouseRestart {
		t.Fatalf("the restart pass's trigger = %q", trigger)
	}
	a.set(OwnerAuditFinding{TableID: "db.a", PartitionID: "all", Reason: OwnerAuditUnresolvedIntent})
	a.forgetTable("db.a")
	if a.blocks("db.a") {
		t.Fatal("a dropped table is still held")
	}
	var none *ownerAuditState
	if none.blocks("db.a") || none.due() {
		t.Fatal("a nil audit state holds a table")
	}
	none.clear(k)
	none.forgetTable("db.a")
}

// TestOwnerAuditStatsCountsRunsFindingsAndDrops: the host's view of the audit is
// a detached copy with every trigger present.
func TestOwnerAuditStatsCountsRunsFindingsAndDrops(t *testing.T) {
	a := newOwnerAuditState(true)
	at := time.UnixMilli(fixtureMillis)
	a.ran(OwnerAuditTriggerStartup, at)
	a.ran(OwnerAuditTriggerPromotion, at.Add(time.Second))
	a.countDropped()
	a.countDropped()
	a.countFSMUnavailable()
	a.restarted()
	a.set(OwnerAuditFinding{TableID: "db.b", PartitionID: "p_2", Reason: OwnerAuditFSMAhead, Parts: []string{"p2_1_1_0"}})
	a.set(OwnerAuditFinding{TableID: "db.a", PartitionID: "p_1", Reason: OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart, Parts: []string{"p1_1_1_0"}})
	s := a.stats(OwnerAuditRepair)
	wantRuns := map[string]uint64{OwnerAuditTriggerStartup: 1, OwnerAuditTriggerPromotion: 1, OwnerAuditTriggerClickHouseRestart: 0}
	if s.Mode != OwnerAuditRepair || len(s.Runs) != 3 || s.Runs[OwnerAuditTriggerStartup] != 1 || s.Runs[OwnerAuditTriggerPromotion] != 1 ||
		s.Runs[OwnerAuditTriggerClickHouseRestart] != 0 || s.DroppedTwins != 2 || s.ClickHouseRestarts != 1 || s.FSMUnavailable != 1 ||
		!s.LastRun.Equal(at.Add(time.Second)) {
		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, want runs %v, 2 drops, 1 restart, 1 FSM failure", s, wantRuns)
	}
	if len(s.Unclean) != 2 || s.Unclean[0].TableID != "db.a" || s.Unclean[1].TableID != "db.b" {
		t.Fatalf("unclean = %+v, want db.a then db.b", s.Unclean)
	}
	s.Unclean[0].Parts[0] = "mutated"
	s.Runs[OwnerAuditTriggerStartup] = 99
	if again := a.stats(OwnerAuditRepair); again.Unclean[0].Parts[0] != "p1_1_1_0" || again.Runs[OwnerAuditTriggerStartup] != 1 {
		t.Fatal("stats share memory with the audit state")
	}
	var none *ownerAuditState
	if s := none.stats(OwnerAuditReport); s.Mode != OwnerAuditReport || len(s.Runs) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("stats of a nil state = %+v", s)
	}
}

// TestConfigOwnerAudit: report is the default, repair the only other mode; the
// probe interval and the FSM timeout default, and are refused when negative or,
// for the interval, below one second.
func TestConfigOwnerAudit(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name               string
		mode               OwnerAuditMode
		probe, fsm         time.Duration
		wantMode           OwnerAuditMode
		wantProbe, wantFSM time.Duration
		refusal            []string
	}{
		{"defaults", "", 0, 0, OwnerAuditReport, DefaultOwnerAuditProbeInterval, DefaultOwnerAuditFSMTimeout, nil},
		{"report", OwnerAuditReport, 0, 0, OwnerAuditReport, DefaultOwnerAuditProbeInterval, DefaultOwnerAuditFSMTimeout, nil},
		{"repair with the minimum interval", OwnerAuditRepair, MinOwnerAuditProbeInterval, 2 * time.Second, OwnerAuditRepair, MinOwnerAuditProbeInterval, 2 * time.Second, nil},
		{"an unknown mode", "drop", 0, 0, "", 0, 0, []string{"owner audit mode", `"drop"`, `"report"`, `"repair"`}},
		{"a negative probe interval", "", -time.Second, 0, "", 0, 0, []string{"owner audit probe interval", "negative"}},
		{"a probe interval below the minimum", "", 500 * time.Millisecond, 0, "", 0, 0, []string{"owner audit probe interval", "500ms", "1s"}},
		{"a negative fsm timeout", "", 0, -time.Second, "", 0, 0, []string{"owner audit fsm timeout", "negative"}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			cfg := testConfigS(t)
			cfg.OwnerAudit, cfg.OwnerAuditProbeInterval, cfg.OwnerAuditFSMTimeout = tc.mode, tc.probe, tc.fsm
			err := cfg.validate()
			if tc.refusal == nil {
				if err != nil || cfg.OwnerAudit != tc.wantMode || cfg.OwnerAuditProbeInterval != tc.wantProbe || cfg.OwnerAuditFSMTimeout != tc.wantFSM {
					t.Fatalf("validate: %v; mode %q interval %v timeout %v, want %q %v %v", err, cfg.OwnerAudit, cfg.OwnerAuditProbeInterval, cfg.OwnerAuditFSMTimeout,
						tc.wantMode, tc.wantProbe, tc.wantFSM)
				}
				return
			}
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("mode %q, interval %v, timeout %v were accepted", tc.mode, tc.probe, tc.fsm)
			}
			for _, want := range tc.refusal {
				if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
					t.Errorf("err = %v, want it to name %q", err, want)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package snode

import (
	"errors"
	"time"
)

// The owner hg_safe audit (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §14; plan S3-A contract
// §3, clarifications K1-K4). A ClickHouse restart within old_parts_lifetime
// reactivates the parts a REPLACE PARTITION retired, under their old names and
// with the hash_of_all_files of their replacements (spec §2), so hg_safe
// serves rows twice and the next promotion of the partition fails its shadow
// closure gate. Before building each promotion's shadow, at startup and after
// every ClickHouse restart, the owner compares each partition's active parts
// with the newer of its own last acknowledged inventory and the arbiter's
// SafeParts.

// OwnerAuditMode selects what the audit does with an unclean partition.
type OwnerAuditMode string

const (
	// OwnerAuditReport, also the meaning of "", audits, logs at error level
	// and counts, but never drops a part and never holds a table back.
	OwnerAuditReport OwnerAuditMode = "report"
	// OwnerAuditRepair drops each resurrected equal-hash twin that carries no
	// acknowledged name (clarification K2) and holds an unclean table
	// not-ready: TableReady is false, so the host answers it Pending, and the
	// SNode builds no shadow for an unclean partition.
	OwnerAuditRepair OwnerAuditMode = "repair"
)

// OwnerAuditReason says why a partition is unclean.
type OwnerAuditReason string

const (
	// OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart: an active part whose name and
	// hash_of_all_files the reference does not carry; in repair mode it is
	// dropped only when it is the twin of an acknowledged part.
	OwnerAuditUnacknowledgedPart OwnerAuditReason = "unacknowledged_part"
	// OwnerAuditAcknowledgedPartMissing: a part of the reference is not active.
	OwnerAuditAcknowledgedPartMissing OwnerAuditReason = "acknowledged_part_missing"
	// OwnerAuditFSMAhead: the arbiter recorded an applied promotion of the
	// partition past this SNode's own promotion watermark.
	OwnerAuditFSMAhead OwnerAuditReason = "fsm_ahead"
	// OwnerAuditFSMDisagrees: this SNode and the arbiter acknowledged
	// different inventories for the same promotion.
	OwnerAuditFSMDisagrees OwnerAuditReason = "fsm_disagrees"
	// OwnerAuditNoAcknowledgedInventory: the partition has parts and there is
	// no reference at all (no local inventory, arbiter unreadable).
	OwnerAuditNoAcknowledgedInventory OwnerAuditReason = "no_acknowledged_inventory"
	// OwnerAuditUnresolvedIntent: a promotion intent of the partition is
	// journaled and not finalized; the audit skips it (clarification K4).
	OwnerAuditUnresolvedIntent OwnerAuditReason = "unresolved_intent"
)

// The audit's triggers, the keys of OwnerAuditStats.Runs.
const (
	OwnerAuditTriggerStartup           = "startup"
	OwnerAuditTriggerPromotion         = "promotion"
	OwnerAuditTriggerClickHouseRestart = "clickhouse_restart"
)

// ErrSafePartitionUnclean refuses, in repair mode, a promotion of a partition
// the audit found unclean, before its shadow is built; the subscription
// redelivers the command.
var ErrSafePartitionUnclean = errors.New("snode: hg_safe partition failed the owner audit")

// OwnerAuditFinding is the current unclean finding of one partition: why, the
// parts it names, the trigger of the audit that found it and when.
type OwnerAuditFinding struct {
	TableID     string
	PartitionID string
	Reason      OwnerAuditReason
	Parts       []string
	Trigger     string
	At          time.Time
}

// OwnerAuditStats is a point-in-time copy of the audit's counters for the host
// to export: the mode, the runs per trigger (every trigger present), the
// current findings sorted by table and partition, the twins dropped, the
// ClickHouse restarts detected, the arbiter reads that failed, and the end of
// the last run.
type OwnerAuditStats struct {
	Mode               OwnerAuditMode
	Runs               map[string]uint64
	Unclean            []OwnerAuditFinding
	DroppedTwins       uint64
	ClickHouseRestarts uint64
	FSMUnavailable     uint64
	LastRun            time.Time
}
```
