- **One script, three callers.** The CI job, Cut Release and the manual deployed-image run all call `scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh`, so the topology the deployed image is measured on is byte-for-byte the one CI uses. It follows the existing jobs (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:42-117`: one Docker network, `CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP=1`, the shared-Keeper XMLs, a readiness loop, removal on exit) and arbiter's `scripts/test-clickhouse-hardlinks.sh` PASS-grep ("A misspelled filter or skipped test must not turn this required gate green"). The required test list is read from the sources (`^func TestMechanics_`), so a test added later joins the gate without a script change.
- **Restarts from SQL; only node B restarts.** Node A hosts the embedded Keeper (`clickhouse-shared-keeper-server.xml`), so restarting it would take Keeper down mid-test; node B is a Keeper client run with `--restart always` and without `--rm`. `SYSTEM KILL` makes ClickHouse call `_exit` (effective even for PID 1 in a container, unlike a signal to itself): the on-disk state of a SIGKILL or an OOM kill. `SYSTEM SHUTDOWN` sends SIGTERM to its process group: the graceful path of a pod deletion. Docker restarts the container either way, so the Go tests need no Docker CLI. Docker may hand a restarted container a different ephemeral host port, so node B gets a fixed one, chosen in 20000–29999 (below the usual ephemeral range) and retried when taken.
- **Restart detection reuses Task 5's detector.** `restartServer` identifies the new process by `chrestart.StartedAt` moving by more than `chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew`, so every restart test also runs the owner audit's restart detector against the image under test. `ensureUptime` first waits until the server has been up for twice the skew, which also keeps Docker's restart back-off at its first step.
- **Expected outcomes, as measured, and what to do if an image differs.** Every M test passes on arrival: they pin ClickHouse, and the code they protect already exists. The red phases this task can show honestly are the opt-in gate (Step 3) and M0 on a wrong version prefix (Step 5). The suite as written here was run while drafting, through `go test` on this exact topology against upstream ClickHouse 26.3.37.3 (what the floating `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3` tag resolved to that day, the patch this task pins) on 2026-10-14, and all thirteen tests passed. The measured values it pins: both restart kinds resurrect (`SYSTEM SHUTDOWN` too, consistent with the devnet2 incident in housegate `CLAUDE.md:219`); `DROP PART` of a resurrected twin leaves no active zero-row part even when checked immediately (K2), and so does `DETACH PART` + `DROP DETACHED PART`; the incremental backup stored 6,870 bytes in 6 of the 25 files it describes against the full backup's 3,636,296 bytes in 13 of 13; `READ ON REMOTE` is refused with 497 `Not enough privileges. To execute this query, it's necessary to have the grant WRITE ON REMOTE`; a `NOT OVERRIDABLE` override is refused with 36 `Override not allowed for 'user'`. The suite was run again in review on the same day and topology, after the script's `docker pull` had moved the floating `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3` tag to 26.3.51.7: all thirteen passed in 100 s with the same backup sizes and refusal texts. Because that tag floats, CI, Cut Release and every command of this task name the exact patch image `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` with the version prefix `26.3.37.3` (clarification K9), so a gate cannot change its verdict without a code change and M0 fails if the tag ever resolved to another version; moving to a later patch is a change of that image and prefix in `ci.yml`, `cut-release.yml` and the README after a green run of the script on it. M0's `mechanics server` log line records the version each run measured. Two expectations are the ones the deployed fork is most likely to move:
  - M3's `graceful` row. If it fails with exactly the replacements active, that is a narrower hazard, not a safety failure: set that row's `wantResurrected` to `false`, record the observation in Appendix B, and never weaken the `abrupt` row. The owner audit runs after every restart either way.
  - M11 checks for an active zero-row part immediately after the drop, because the owner audit lists the partition again right after its drops and requires the result to match the reference (Task 5 Notes, "The repair rule"). If `drop_part` fails with a zero-row part while `detach_part_then_drop_detached` passes, K2 does not hold for `DROP PART` on that image: record it in Appendix B and stop before any owner is switched to `repair` (Plan S3-B), because Task 5's repair would then need `DETACH PART` followed by `DROP DETACHED PART`.
- **The SNode restart test.** After the suite, the script runs Task 5's `TestOwnerAuditRepairsResurrectedPartsAcrossAClickHouseRestart` (spec §17, "the owner audit across a ClickHouse-only restart") against node B with `ARBITER_CH_RESTART=1` and `CH_RESTART_ADDR` set, filtered to that one test (`--test_filter`, `-test.v`) and gated on `--- PASS:` lines for it and for its `repair` and `report` subtests, because a filter that matches nothing, or a test that skips for a missing variable, passes silently (Task 5 Notes, "CI"). The test restarts its server, so it runs here and nowhere else; the other SNode ClickHouse tests stay in `integration-clickhouse`. The two Bazel invocations run one after the other and nothing in `snode` or `dataplane/chmechanics` calls `t.Parallel()` (`git grep -c 't.Parallel()' origin/main -- snode dataplane` finds none), so no test shares a server with a restart. Being inside the script, the restart test also runs in Cut Release and on the deployed image (Step 16), not only in CI.
- **The deployed image is private.** `us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16` (production `charts/storage-integrity/values.yaml:36-38` at `eba93300a`; the devnet2 indexer-b source CHI, `k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source.yaml:112`) sits in Sentio's Artifact Registry. No arbiter-core workflow logs in to it, and arbiter-core is a public repository whose self-hosted jobs have no credentials for it, so CI cannot pull it until an admin provides a read-only registry secret (a follow-up outside this plan, K9). Until then CI and Cut Release run the exact upstream patch `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` (prefix `26.3.37.3`), and Step 16 runs the identical script on the deployed image as a user action, with the prefix `26.3.` because the fork's patch number is not known in advance (M0 logs the exact version); that run must pass before Plan S3-B rolls anything (K9). The public README names the image by the chart that deploys it, not by registry path, and documents the manual run.
- **Production keeps the default lifetime.** `git -C production grep old_parts_lifetime eba93300a` finds nothing, so the image default that M3 pins (480 s) is what every SI ClickHouse runs.
- **Never stop merges.** The SNode fixtures issue `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` (`snode/promote_fixtures_test.go:83-85`), which also stops outdated-part deletion (housegate `CLAUDE.md:219`) and would make M3's window unbounded. The suite builds every protocol table with `ddl.Intents`, so the pinned `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool = 0` keeps merges off exactly as in production, and it issues no `SYSTEM` merge command.
- **Existing jobs are unchanged.** `integration-clickhouse` and Cut Release's SNode pair stay on 25.8 (`ci.yml:60,68`, `cut-release.yml:60,68`); moving them is not part of P0. Cut Release's `timeout-minutes` rises from 20 to 60 for the mechanics step.
- **Credentials.** The suite connects through `chtest.Open` and, for its restricted users, `chtest.OpenAs`. Its one other connection path is `dial`, the non-fatal opener the restart loop and the post-restart cleanups need (`chtest.Open` fails the test on a refused dial); it builds its options with `chtest.Options(addr)`, so a `CH_USER` / `CH_PASSWORD` pair reaches it too. Task 4's one-time check that no `clickhouse.Open(` exists outside `dataplane/chtest/chtest.go` predates this file; anyone repeating it after this task excludes `dataplane/chmechanics/mechanics_test.go` as well. The scripted pair itself keeps the passwordless `default` (the script passes no `--test_env=CH_USER`), unlike Task 4's credentialed `integration-clickhouse` pair.
- **No consensus surface.** The package is test-only (no `go_library`); `bazel test //...` in the `test` job compiles it and every test skips. Nothing here changes a Raft command, snapshot, feature string or golden file.

```go
// "ClickHouse mechanics (measured)" and "Restart resurrection"; plan S3-A
// clarification K2), so that an image whose behaviour differs fails here
// before it reaches a storage-integrity ClickHouse. The package holds tests
// only. Every test is opt-in with ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS=1 and then fails,
// rather than skips, when a prerequisite is missing;
// scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh starts the pair and runs the suite
// (README § ClickHouse mechanics).
package chmechanics

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha1"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/chexec"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chrestart"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chtest"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
)

// The suite's environment (README § ClickHouse mechanics).
const (
	envMechanics     = "ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS"
	envIntegration   = "ARBITER_CH_INTEGRATION"
	envKeeper        = "ARBITER_CH_KEEPER"
	envAddr          = "CH_ADDR"
	envReplicaAddr   = "CH_REPLICA_ADDR"
	envPeerAddr      = "CH_PEER_ADDR"
	envRestart       = "ARBITER_CH_RESTART"
	envRestartAddr   = "CH_RESTART_ADDR"
	envVersionPrefix = "ARBITER_CH_EXPECT_VERSION_PREFIX"
	envImage         = "ARBITER_CH_IMAGE"
)

// ClickHouse error codes the suite asserts.
const (
	codeBadArguments = 36  // BAD_ARGUMENTS
	codeTooManyParts = 252 // TOO_MANY_PARTS
	codeAccessDenied = 497 // ACCESS_DENIED
)

const (
	// restartTimeout bounds one restart: the process exit, Docker's restart
	// of the container and the new server answering with a later start time.
	restartTimeout = 120 * time.Second
	// settleTimeout bounds a wait for background replication.
	settleTimeout = 60 * time.Second
)

// mechanicsEnv is the pair the suite runs on. Node A hosts the shared
// Keeper. Node B is a Keeper client and, in the scripted topology, also the
// server the restart tests restart (CH_RESTART_ADDR).
type mechanicsEnv struct {
	A, B          clickhouse.Conn
	AAddr, BAddr  string
	PeerAddr      string // node A as node B reaches it, for remote() and named collections
	Image         string
	VersionPrefix string
}

// requireMechanics skips unless ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS=1 and then fails on any
// missing prerequisite: the suite is a release gate, so a half-configured run
// must not pass by skipping.
func requireMechanics(t *testing.T) mechanicsEnv {
	t.Helper()
	if os.Getenv(envMechanics) != "1" {
		t.Skip("set ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS=1 and run scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh (README § ClickHouse mechanics) to run the ClickHouse mechanics suite")
	}
	var missing []string
	for _, flag := range []string{envIntegration, envKeeper} {
		if os.Getenv(flag) != "1" {
			missing = append(missing, flag+"=1")
		}
	}
	for _, name := range []string{envAddr, envReplicaAddr, envPeerAddr, envVersionPrefix, envImage} {
		if os.Getenv(name) == "" {
			missing = append(missing, name)
		}
	}
	if len(missing) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS=1 requires %s", strings.Join(missing, ", "))
	}
	env := mechanicsEnv{
		AAddr:         os.Getenv(envAddr),
		BAddr:         os.Getenv(envReplicaAddr),
		PeerAddr:      os.Getenv(envPeerAddr),
		Image:         os.Getenv(envImage),
		VersionPrefix: os.Getenv(envVersionPrefix),
	}
	env.A = chtest.Open(t, env.AAddr)
	env.B = chtest.Open(t, env.BAddr)
	requireKeeper(t, envAddr, env.A)
	requireKeeper(t, envReplicaAddr, env.B)
	return env
}

// requireKeeper waits until the server reaches its Keeper: node B may answer
// queries right after a restart test restarted it, before its Keeper session
// is back.
func requireKeeper(t *testing.T, name string, conn clickhouse.Conn) {
	t.Helper()
	eventually(t, settleTimeout, "the server at "+name+" reaching its Keeper (scripts/ci/clickhouse-shared-keeper-*.xml)", func() (bool, string) {
		var n uint64
		err := conn.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT count() FROM system.zookeeper WHERE path = '/'").Scan(&n)
		return err == nil, fmt.Sprintf("last error: %v", err)
	})
}

// requireRestartable returns CH_RESTART_ADDR. The restart tests are a second
// opt-in, ARBITER_CH_RESTART=1, because they need a server whose container
// Docker restarts (--restart always) and that does not host the Keeper.
func requireRestartable(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	if os.Getenv(envRestart) != "1" {
		t.Skip("set ARBITER_CH_RESTART=1 and CH_RESTART_ADDR (a server whose container runs with --restart always and does not host the Keeper) to run the restart mechanics")
	}
	addr := os.Getenv(envRestartAddr)
	if addr == "" {
		t.Fatal("ARBITER_CH_RESTART=1 requires CH_RESTART_ADDR")
	}
	return addr
}

// suffix keeps databases, users, collections and Keeper paths unique per
// test and subtest.
func suffix(t *testing.T) string {
	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(t.Name()))
	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:10]
}

// mechanicsPinned is a test's own protocol databases, replica name and Keeper
// shard, so ddl.KeeperUnsafeTables lists only that test's tables.
func mechanicsPinned(t *testing.T) ddl.Pinned {
	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(t.Name()))
	s := hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:10]
	return ddl.Pinned{
		UnsafeDB:      "hg_unsafe_m" + s,
		SafeDB:        "hg_safe_m" + s,
		PromoteDB:     "hg_promote_m" + s,
		NodeID:        "mech-" + s,
		KeeperShardID: 1_000_000 + binary.BigEndian.Uint32(sum[10:14])%1_000_000,
	}
}

// mechanicsSchema is the shape of an SI table: a String partition key and one
// value column.
func mechanicsSchema(t *testing.T) payloadexec.TableSchema {
	return payloadexec.TableSchema{
		TableID:     "mech.t_" + suffix(t),
		PartitionBy: "p",
		Columns:     []lthash.Column{{Name: "p", Type: "String"}, {Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}},
	}
}

// ident quotes a ClickHouse identifier.
func ident(name string) string {
	return "`" + strings.ReplaceAll(name, "`", "``") + "`"
}

// literal quotes a ClickHouse string literal.
func literal(s string) string {
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, `\`, `\\`)
	return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, `'`, `\'`) + "'"
}

func qualified(db, table string) string {
	return ident(db) + "." + ident(table)
}

func mustExec(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, query string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := conn.Exec(context.Background(), query); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", query, err)
	}
}

// clickHouseCode is err's server error code, or 0 when err is not a server
// exception (a transport error, or nil).
func clickHouseCode(err error) int32 {
	var exception *clickhouse.Exception
	if errors.As(err, &exception) {
		return exception.Code
	}
	return 0
}

// dial opens and pings a connection without failing the test, for the
// restart loop and for cleanups that run after a restart.
func dial(ctx context.Context, addr string) (clickhouse.Conn, error) {
	opts := chtest.Options(addr)
	opts.DialTimeout = 2 * time.Second
	conn, err := clickhouse.Open(opts)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	pingCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	if err := conn.Ping(pingCtx); err != nil {
		_ = conn.Close()
		return nil, err
	}
	return conn, nil
}

// dropDatabasesAt drops databases on the server at addr when the test ends,
// through a fresh connection, so a restart in between leaves nothing behind.
func dropDatabasesAt(t *testing.T, addr string, databases ...string) {
	t.Helper()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		conn, err := dial(context.Background(), addr)
		if err != nil {
			t.Logf("cleanup: cannot reach %s to drop %v: %v", addr, databases, err)
			return
		}
		defer func() { _ = conn.Close() }()
		for _, database := range databases {
			if err := conn.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+ident(database)+" SYNC"); err != nil {
				t.Logf("cleanup: drop database %s on %s: %v", database, addr, err)
			}
		}
	})
}

// createTables creates each intent's database and table on conn with the
// protocol DDL (TableIntent.SQL) and drops those databases when the test ends.
func createTables(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr string, intents ...ddl.TableIntent) {
	t.Helper()
	var databases []string
	for _, intent := range intents {
		if !slices.Contains(databases, intent.Database) {
			databases = append(databases, intent.Database)
		}
	}
	dropDatabasesAt(t, addr, databases...)
	for _, database := range databases {
		mustExec(t, conn, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+ident(database))
	}
	for _, intent := range intents {
		mustExec(t, conn, intent.SQL())
	}
}

// protocolTables creates p's hg_safe and hg_promote MergeTree tables for sch
// from ddl.Intents, so every pinned engine setting applies, and returns all
// three intents; a caller that needs the hg_unsafe ReplicatedMergeTree table
// passes the first one to createTables.
func protocolTables(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr string, p ddl.Pinned, sch payloadexec.TableSchema) (ddl.TableIntent, ddl.TableIntent, ddl.TableIntent) {
	t.Helper()
	unsafe, safe, promote, err := ddl.Intents(p, sch)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("protocol intents for %s: %v", sch.TableID, err)
	}
	createTables(t, conn, addr, safe, promote)
	return unsafe, safe, promote
}

// mechPart is one row of system.parts.
type mechPart struct {
	Name      string
	Partition string // system.parts.partition: the value, p0 for partition 'p0'
	PhysHash  string // system.parts.hash_of_all_files
	Rows      uint64
	MinBlock  int64
	MaxBlock  int64
	Active    bool
}

// partsOf lists every part of db.table that system.parts shows, active and
// outdated, by name.
func partsOf(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table string) []mechPart {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := conn.Query(context.Background(), `
		SELECT name, partition, hash_of_all_files, rows, min_block_number, max_block_number, toUInt8(active)
		FROM system.parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ? ORDER BY name`, db, table)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.parts of %s.%s: %v", db, table, err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []mechPart
	for rows.Next() {
		var part mechPart
		var active uint8
		if err := rows.Scan(&part.Name, &part.Partition, &part.PhysHash, &part.Rows, &part.MinBlock, &part.MaxBlock, &active); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("scan system.parts of %s.%s: %v", db, table, err)
		}
		part.Active = active == 1
		out = append(out, part)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.parts of %s.%s: %v", db, table, err)
	}
	return out
}

// activeParts is partsOf restricted to the active parts of one partition.
func activeParts(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table, partition string) []mechPart {
	t.Helper()
	var out []mechPart
	for _, part := range partsOf(t, conn, db, table) {
		if part.Active && part.Partition == partition {
			out = append(out, part)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func names(parts []mechPart) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
	for _, part := range parts {
		out = append(out, part.Name)
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

func physHashes(parts []mechPart) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
	for _, part := range parts {
		out = append(out, part.PhysHash)
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

func totalRows(parts []mechPart) uint64 {
	var n uint64
	for _, part := range parts {
		n += part.Rows
	}
	return n
}

func withRows(parts []mechPart) []mechPart {
	var out []mechPart
	for _, part := range parts {
		if part.Rows > 0 {
			out = append(out, part)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func zeroRowParts(parts []mechPart) []mechPart {
	var out []mechPart
	for _, part := range parts {
		if part.Rows == 0 {
			out = append(out, part)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func partNamed(parts []mechPart, name string) (mechPart, bool) {
	for _, part := range parts {
		if part.Name == name {
			return part, true
		}
	}
	return mechPart{}, false
}

func partWithHash(parts []mechPart, physHash string) (mechPart, bool) {
	for _, part := range parts {
		if part.PhysHash == physHash {
			return part, true
		}
	}
	return mechPart{}, false
}

// rowHashes scans parts of db.table with chexec.ScanParts, the SNode's row
// identity, and returns each part's row LtHash by name. Every part must hold
// rows: ScanParts refuses an empty one.
func rowHashes(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table string, sch payloadexec.TableSchema, parts []mechPart) map[string]string {
	t.Helper()
	scans, err := chexec.ScanParts(context.Background(), conn, db+"."+table, sch, names(parts))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("scan %s.%s parts %v: %v", db, table, names(parts), err)
	}
	out := make(map[string]string, len(scans))
	for _, scan := range scans {
		out[scan.PartName] = scan.RowLtHash
	}
	return out
}

// rowHashList is rowHashes as a sorted multiset.
func rowHashList(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table string, sch payloadexec.TableSchema, parts []mechPart) []string {
	t.Helper()
	var out []string
	for _, h := range rowHashes(t, conn, db, table, sch, parts) {
		out = append(out, h)
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

// sumRowHashes adds row LtHash accumulators: the content root of the parts.
func sumRowHashes(t *testing.T, hashes ...string) string {
	t.Helper()
	acc := lthash.New()
	for _, h := range hashes {
		raw, err := hex.DecodeString(strings.TrimPrefix(h, "0x"))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("row LtHash %s: %v", abbreviate(h), err)
		}
		part, err := lthash.FromBytes(raw)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("row LtHash %s: %v", abbreviate(h), err)
		}
		acc.AddHash(part)
	}
	return "0x" + hex.EncodeToString(acc.Bytes())
}

// abbreviate shortens a 4098-character accumulator for messages.
func abbreviate(h string) string {
	if len(h) <= 26 {
		return h
	}
	return h[:18] + "…" + h[len(h)-8:]
}

// insertRows writes n rows of partition into db.table with one
// single-threaded INSERT ... SELECT. v runs from `from` and _hg_row_id is the
// SHA-256 of the partition and v, so equal (partition, from, n) writes equal
// rows, with equal row LtHash, into any table of mechanicsSchema. Without
// extra settings one call writes one part for n up to the default
// min_insert_block_size_rows.
func insertRows(conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table, partition string, from, n uint64, extra clickhouse.Settings) error {
	settings := clickhouse.Settings{"max_threads": 1, "max_insert_threads": 1}
	for name, value := range extra {
		settings[name] = value
	}
	ctx := clickhouse.Context(context.Background(), clickhouse.WithSettings(settings))
	return conn.Exec(ctx, fmt.Sprintf(
		"INSERT INTO %s (%s, `p`, `v`) SELECT SHA256(concat('mech:', %s, ':', toString(number))), %s, number FROM numbers(%d, %d)",
		qualified(db, table), ident(ddl.RowIDColumn), literal(partition), literal(partition), from, n))
}

func mustInsert(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table, partition string, from, n uint64, extra clickhouse.Settings) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := insertRows(conn, db, table, partition, from, n, extra); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("insert %d rows into %s.%s partition %s: %v", n, db, table, partition, err)
	}
}

// countRows is SELECT count() FROM source, where source is a table or a table
// function.
func countRows(conn clickhouse.Conn, source string) (uint64, error) {
	var n uint64
	err := conn.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT count() FROM "+source).Scan(&n)
	return n, err
}

func mustCountRows(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, source string) uint64 {
	t.Helper()
	n, err := countRows(conn, source)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("count %s: %v", source, err)
	}
	return n
}

func randomHex(t *testing.T, n int) string {
	t.Helper()
	b := make([]byte, n)
	if _, err := rand.Read(b); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(b)
}

// eventually polls cond every 500 ms until it holds or timeout passes; cond
// reports the state it saw for the failure message.
func eventually(t *testing.T, timeout time.Duration, what string, cond func() (bool, string)) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(timeout)
	for {
		ok, state := cond()
		if ok {
			return
		}
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: not reached within %s: %s", what, timeout, state)
		}
		time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// restartKind is the SQL statement that ends the server process. Docker
// restarts the container (--restart always), so the tests need no Docker
// CLI.
type restartKind string

const (
	// restartAbrupt exits at once without shutting tables down, as a SIGKILL
	// or an OOM kill does (SYSTEM KILL calls _exit).
	restartAbrupt restartKind = "SYSTEM KILL"
	// restartGraceful shuts the server down through its SIGTERM handler, as a
	// pod deletion does.
	restartGraceful restartKind = "SYSTEM SHUTDOWN"
)

func startedAt(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn) time.Time {
	t.Helper()
	at, err := chrestart.StartedAt(context.Background(), conn, time.Now())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ClickHouse start time: %v", err)
	}
	return at
}

// ensureUptime waits until the server has been up for at least atLeast, so a
// restart moves its start time by more than chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew and
// Docker's restart back-off stays at its first step.
func ensureUptime(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, atLeast time.Duration) {
	t.Helper()
	if up := time.Since(startedAt(t, conn)); up < atLeast {
		time.Sleep(atLeast - up)
	}
}

// restartServer ends the server at addr with kind and returns a connection to
// the server Docker started in its place: the one whose start time
// (chrestart.StartedAt, the owner audit's restart detector) is later than the
// old one by more than chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew.
func restartServer(t *testing.T, addr string, kind restartKind) clickhouse.Conn {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	old, err := dial(ctx, addr)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connect to %s before %s: %v", addr, kind, err)
	}
	ensureUptime(t, old, 2*chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew)
	before := startedAt(t, old)
	execCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second)
	err = old.Exec(execCtx, string(kind))
	cancel()
	_ = old.Close()
	t.Logf("%s on %s returned %v", kind, addr, err)
	deadline := time.Now().Add(restartTimeout)
	last := errors.New("no reconnect attempt")
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
		conn, err := dial(ctx, addr)
		if err != nil {
			last = err
			continue
		}
		at, err := chrestart.StartedAt(ctx, conn, time.Now())
		if err == nil && at.After(before.Add(chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew)) {
			t.Cleanup(func() { _ = conn.Close() })
			t.Logf("%s restarted %s: start time %s, then %s", kind, addr, before.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339), at.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339))
			return conn
		}
		if err == nil {
			err = fmt.Errorf("the server still reports start time %s", at.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339))
		}
		last = err
		_ = conn.Close()
	}
	t.Fatalf("%s did not restart %s within %s (does its container run with --restart always?): %v", kind, addr, restartTimeout, last)
	return nil
}

// waitLoaded waits until a restarted server has loaded db.table's parts:
// SYSTEM WAIT LOADING PARTS covers parts loaded asynchronously, and the count
// forces a table that loads lazily at startup.
func waitLoaded(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table string) {
	t.Helper()
	mustExec(t, conn, "SYSTEM WAIT LOADING PARTS "+qualified(db, table))
	mustCountRows(t, conn, qualified(db, table))
}

// TestMechanics_ServerIsTheDeployedImage (M0) records which server the suite
// measured: every server runs a ClickHouse whose version has the expected
// prefix, all the same one, and the log names the image, so a green run on
// upstream 26.3.37.3 is never mistaken for one on the deployed
// 26.3-lts-decimal512 image.
func TestMechanics_ServerIsTheDeployedImage(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	type server struct {
		name string
		conn clickhouse.Conn
	}
	servers := []server{{envAddr, env.A}, {envReplicaAddr, env.B}}
	if addr := os.Getenv(envRestartAddr); os.Getenv(envRestart) == "1" && addr != "" {
		servers = append(servers, server{envRestartAddr, chtest.Open(t, addr)})
	}
	var first string
	for _, s := range servers {
		var version string
		var uptime uint32
		if err := s.conn.QueryRow(context.Background(), "SELECT version(), uptime()").Scan(&version, &uptime); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: SELECT version(): %v", s.name, err)
		}
		t.Logf("mechanics server %s: image %s, ClickHouse %s, up %ds", s.name, env.Image, version, uptime)
		if !strings.HasPrefix(version, env.VersionPrefix) {
			t.Fatalf("%s runs ClickHouse %s, want the %s prefix of image %s", s.name, version, env.VersionPrefix, env.Image)
		}
		if first == "" {
			first = version
		} else if version != first {
			t.Fatalf("%s runs ClickHouse %s but %s runs %s: the pair must run one image", s.name, version, servers[0].name, first)
		}
	}
}
```

Create `scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh` (bash 3.2 compatible, so it also runs under macOS `/bin/bash`):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the ClickHouse mechanics suite (//dataplane/chmechanics) on one image.
#
# Usage:
#   bash scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh <image> <version prefix>
#   bash scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics.sh --cleanup
#
# Starts two servers of <image> on one Docker network. Node A hosts the shared
# Keeper (clickhouse-shared-keeper-server.xml). Node B is a Keeper client that
# runs with --restart always on a fixed host port, so the suite can restart it
# from SQL (SYSTEM KILL, SYSTEM SHUTDOWN) and reconnect. Both mount the backup
# disk and the default user's access-management settings. Then runs the suite
# and, against node B, the SNode's owner-audit restart test, and removes the
# containers and the network. Every TestMechanics_ function and the restart
# test must report PASS; a skipped test fails the run.
#
# Environment: ARBITER_CH_PLATFORM (for example linux/amd64) is passed to
# docker pull and docker run. ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS_FILTER (a Go regexp)
# limits the suite to the TestMechanics_ functions it matches and skips the
# SNode run.
set -euo pipefail

repo_root="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "${repo_root}"

suffix="${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}-${GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT:-0}"
network="arbiter-core-mech-${suffix}"
ch_a="arbiter-core-mech-a-${suffix}"
ch_b="arbiter-core-mech-b-${suffix}"

cleanup() {
  docker rm -f "${ch_a}" "${ch_b}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker network rm "${network}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

if [ "${1:-}" = "--cleanup" ]; then
  cleanup
  exit 0
fi
if [ "$#" -ne 2 ]; then
  echo "usage: $0 <image> <version prefix> | --cleanup" >&2
  exit 2
fi
image="$1"
version_prefix="$2"
platform_flag=""
if [ -n "${ARBITER_CH_PLATFORM:-}" ]; then
  platform_flag="--platform=${ARBITER_CH_PLATFORM}"
fi

on_exit() {
  status=$?
  if [ "${status}" -ne 0 ]; then
    # ClickHouse logs to the container's stderr, so both streams go to ours.
    docker logs --tail 100 "${ch_a}" >&2 2>&1 || true
    docker logs --tail 100 "${ch_b}" >&2 2>&1 || true
  fi
  cleanup
  exit "${status}"
}
trap on_exit EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM

cleanup
docker pull ${platform_flag:+"${platform_flag}"} "${image}" >/dev/null
docker network create "${network}" >/dev/null

common=(
  --network "${network}"
  -e CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP=1
  -v "${repo_root}/scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics-backups.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/backups.xml:ro"
  -v "${repo_root}/scripts/ci/clickhouse-mechanics-users.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/users.d/mechanics.xml:ro"
)

docker run -d ${platform_flag:+"${platform_flag}"} \
  --name "${ch_a}" --hostname "${ch_a}" \
  --network-alias arbiter-core-clickhouse-a \
  -p 127.0.0.1::9000 \
  -v "${repo_root}/scripts/ci/clickhouse-shared-keeper-server.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/keeper.xml:ro" \
  "${common[@]}" "${image}" >/dev/null
port_a="$(docker inspect --format '{{(index (index .NetworkSettings.Ports "9000/tcp") 0).HostPort}}' "${ch_a}")"

# Node B is the server the suite restarts. Docker may move an ephemeral host
# port when it restarts a container, so B gets a fixed one, below the usual
# ephemeral range, retried when taken.
port_b=""
run_output=""
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do
  candidate=$((20000 + RANDOM % 10000))
  if run_output="$(docker run -d ${platform_flag:+"${platform_flag}"} --restart always \
    --name "${ch_b}" --hostname "${ch_b}" \
    --network-alias arbiter-core-clickhouse-b \
    -p "127.0.0.1:${candidate}:9000" \
    -v "${repo_root}/scripts/ci/clickhouse-shared-keeper-client.xml:/etc/clickhouse-server/config.d/keeper.xml:ro" \
    "${common[@]}" "${image}" 2>&1)"; then
    port_b="${candidate}"
    break
  fi
  docker rm -f "${ch_b}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done
if [ -z "${port_b}" ]; then
  echo "node B did not start on any of 20 host ports; the last attempt said: ${run_output}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

ready=false
for _ in $(seq 1 120); do
  if docker exec "${ch_a}" clickhouse-client --query "SELECT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    docker exec "${ch_b}" clickhouse-client --query "SELECT 1" >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
    docker exec "${ch_b}" clickhouse-client --query "SELECT count() FROM system.zookeeper WHERE path = '/'" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ready=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "${ready}" != true ]; then
  echo "the ClickHouse pair did not become ready" >&2
  exit 1
fi

export ARBITER_CH_INTEGRATION=1 ARBITER_CH_KEEPER=1 ARBITER_CH_REPLICA=1 ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS=1 ARBITER_CH_RESTART=1
export CH_ADDR="127.0.0.1:${port_a}"
export CH_REPLICA_ADDR="127.0.0.1:${port_b}"
export CH_RESTART_ADDR="127.0.0.1:${port_b}"
export CH_PEER_ADDR="arbiter-core-clickhouse-a:9000"
export ARBITER_CH_EXPECT_VERSION_PREFIX="${version_prefix}"
export ARBITER_CH_IMAGE="${image}"
env_flags=(
  --test_env=ARBITER_CH_INTEGRATION --test_env=ARBITER_CH_KEEPER --test_env=ARBITER_CH_REPLICA
  --test_env=ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS --test_env=ARBITER_CH_RESTART
  --test_env=CH_ADDR --test_env=CH_REPLICA_ADDR --test_env=CH_RESTART_ADDR --test_env=CH_PEER_ADDR
  --test_env=ARBITER_CH_EXPECT_VERSION_PREFIX --test_env=ARBITER_CH_IMAGE
)

required="$(grep -ho '^func TestMechanics_[A-Za-z0-9_]*' dataplane/chmechanics/*_test.go | sed 's/^func //' | sort -u || true)"
filter_flag=""
if [ -n "${ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS_FILTER:-}" ]; then
  required="$(printf '%s\n' "${required}" | grep -E -- "${ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS_FILTER}" || true)"
  filter_flag="--test_filter=${ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS_FILTER}"
fi
if [ -z "${required}" ]; then
  echo "no TestMechanics_ function to run" >&2
  exit 1
fi

bazel test //dataplane/chmechanics:chmechanics_test "${env_flags[@]}" ${filter_flag:+"${filter_flag}"} \
  --test_arg=-test.v --nocache_test_results --test_timeout=1800 --test_output=errors

log="$(bazel info bazel-testlogs)/dataplane/chmechanics/chmechanics_test/test.log"
# A misspelled filter or a skipped test must not turn this gate green.
for name in ${required}; do
  if ! grep -Eq -- "^--- PASS: ${name} \(" "${log}"; then
    echo "mechanics test ${name} did not run and pass" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
if grep -q -- "--- SKIP:" "${log}"; then
  echo "a mechanics test was skipped:" >&2
  grep -- "--- SKIP:" "${log}" >&2
  exit 1
fi
grep -F 'mechanics server ' "${log}" || true
echo "mechanics: $(printf '%s\n' "${required}" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') test(s) passed on ${image}"

if [ -z "${ARBITER_CH_MECHANICS_FILTER:-}" ]; then
  # The SNode's owner audit across a ClickHouse-only restart (Task 5). It
  # restarts node B, so it runs only here, on its own, after the suite. A
  # filter that matches nothing, or a test that skips, passes silently, hence
  # the grep.
  snode_test="TestOwnerAuditRepairsResurrectedPartsAcrossAClickHouseRestart"
  bazel test //snode:snode_test "${env_flags[@]}" "--test_filter=^${snode_test}\$" \
    --test_arg=-test.v --nocache_test_results --test_timeout=1800 --test_output=errors
  snode_log="$(bazel info bazel-testlogs)/snode/snode_test/test.log"
  for name in "${snode_test}" "${snode_test}/repair" "${snode_test}/report"; do
    if ! grep -Eq -- "^ *--- PASS: ${name} \(" "${snode_log}"; then
      echo "SNode restart test ${name} did not run and pass" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
  done
  echo "snode: ${snode_test} passed on ${image}"
fi
```

Create `dataplane/chmechanics/parts_test.go`:

```go
package chmechanics

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chrestart"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chtest"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
)

// The promotion replaceAPartition performs: two base parts and one candidate,
// so REPLACE publishes 9 rows and a restart that brings the two base parts
// back shows 14 (spec §2 measured 3 rows becoming 5).
const (
	baseRowsA     = 2
	baseRowsB     = 3
	candidateRows = 4
)

// replaceFixture is one promotion of partition p0 as the SNode performs it.
type replaceFixture struct {
	p                ddl.Pinned
	sch              payloadexec.TableSchema
	table            string     // the physical table name in hg_safe and hg_promote
	retired          []mechPart // hg_safe's active parts before REPLACE
	shadow           []mechPart // hg_promote's parts that REPLACE copied
	replacements     []mechPart // hg_safe's active parts after REPLACE
	retiredRowHashes map[string]string
	shadowRowHashes  map[string]string
}

// replaceAPartition performs the SNode's promotion of p0 on the server at
// addr with the protocol DDL (snode/promote_replace.go buildAndReplace): two
// base parts in hg_safe, the shadow built with ATTACH PARTITION FROM hg_safe
// plus one candidate part, REPLACE PARTITION, and the shadow partition
// dropped.
func replaceAPartition(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr string) replaceFixture {
	t.Helper()
	fx := replaceFixture{p: mechanicsPinned(t), sch: mechanicsSchema(t)}
	_, safe, promote := protocolTables(t, conn, addr, fx.p, fx.sch)
	fx.table = safe.Table
	safeTable := qualified(fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table)
	promoteTable := qualified(fx.p.PromoteDB, promote.Table)
	// A restart test restarts right after REPLACE: wait for the uptime first.
	ensureUptime(t, conn, 2*chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew)
	mustInsert(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, "p0", 0, baseRowsA, nil)
	mustInsert(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, "p0", baseRowsA, baseRowsB, nil)
	fx.retired = activeParts(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, "p0")
	if len(fx.retired) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("base: hg_safe holds %d active parts, want 2: %+v", len(fx.retired), fx.retired)
	}
	fx.retiredRowHashes = rowHashes(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, fx.sch, fx.retired)
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s ATTACH PARTITION 'p0' FROM %s", promoteTable, safeTable))
	mustInsert(t, conn, fx.p.PromoteDB, promote.Table, "p0", baseRowsA+baseRowsB, candidateRows, nil)
	fx.shadow = activeParts(t, conn, fx.p.PromoteDB, promote.Table, "p0")
	if len(fx.shadow) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("shadow: hg_promote holds %d active parts, want 3: %+v", len(fx.shadow), fx.shadow)
	}
	fx.shadowRowHashes = rowHashes(t, conn, fx.p.PromoteDB, promote.Table, fx.sch, fx.shadow)
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s REPLACE PARTITION 'p0' FROM %s", safeTable, promoteTable))
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s DROP PARTITION 'p0'", promoteTable))
	fx.replacements = activeParts(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, "p0")
	return fx
}

// TestMechanics_ReplacePartitionKeepsHashOfAllFiles (M1) pins what the SNode's
// promotion and the owner audit rely on: REPLACE PARTITION publishes a copy
// of every shadow part with its hash_of_all_files and row LtHash, under a new
// name whose block range lies above every part it replaced, so the
// replacements cover none of the parts they replace.
func TestMechanics_ReplacePartitionKeepsHashOfAllFiles(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	fx := replaceAPartition(t, env.A, env.AAddr)
	if got, want := totalRows(fx.replacements), uint64(baseRowsA+baseRowsB+candidateRows); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("hg_safe holds %d rows after REPLACE, want %d: %+v", got, want, fx.replacements)
	}
	if got, want := physHashes(fx.replacements), physHashes(fx.shadow); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("REPLACE PARTITION changed hash_of_all_files: hg_safe %v, shadow %v", got, want)
	}
	published := physHashes(fx.replacements)
	var maxRetiredBlock int64
	for _, retired := range fx.retired {
		if !slices.Contains(published, retired.PhysHash) {
			t.Fatalf("base part %s (%s) has no copy with its hash_of_all_files after REPLACE: %+v", retired.Name, retired.PhysHash, fx.replacements)
		}
		maxRetiredBlock = max(maxRetiredBlock, retired.MaxBlock)
	}
	safeRowHashes := rowHashes(t, env.A, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, fx.sch, fx.replacements)
	for _, part := range fx.replacements {
		if _, reused := partNamed(fx.retired, part.Name); reused {
			t.Fatalf("replacement %s reuses a retired part's name", part.Name)
		}
		if part.MinBlock <= maxRetiredBlock {
			t.Fatalf("replacement %s starts at block %d, at or below the retired parts' last block %d", part.Name, part.MinBlock, maxRetiredBlock)
		}
		source, ok := partWithHash(fx.shadow, part.PhysHash)
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("replacement %s has no shadow part with hash_of_all_files %s", part.Name, part.PhysHash)
		}
		if got, want := safeRowHashes[part.Name], fx.shadowRowHashes[source.Name]; got != want {
			t.Fatalf("replacement %s row LtHash %s differs from its shadow part %s (%s)", part.Name, abbreviate(got), source.Name, abbreviate(want))
		}
	}
}

// TestMechanics_AttachPartitionFromKeepsHashOfAllFiles (M2) pins the shadow
// build and the install path (snode/promote_replace.go prepareShadow and
// attachCandidateParts; spec §8.5 step 5): ATTACH PARTITION FROM copies every
// part with its hash_of_all_files and row LtHash, across databases and from
// the hg_unsafe ReplicatedMergeTree into a MergeTree, and leaves its source
// unchanged.
func TestMechanics_AttachPartitionFromKeepsHashOfAllFiles(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	t.Run("across_databases", func(t *testing.T) {
		p := mechanicsPinned(t)
		sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
		_, safe, promote := protocolTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, p, sch)
		mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 0, 2, nil)
		mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 2, 3, nil)
		assertAttachCopies(t, env.A, sch, safe, promote)
	})
	t.Run("from_replicated_merge_tree", func(t *testing.T) {
		p := mechanicsPinned(t)
		sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
		unsafe, _, promote := protocolTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, p, sch)
		createTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, unsafe)
		mustInsert(t, env.A, p.UnsafeDB, unsafe.Table, "p0", 0, 2, nil)
		mustInsert(t, env.A, p.UnsafeDB, unsafe.Table, "p0", 2, 3, nil)
		assertAttachCopies(t, env.A, sch, unsafe, promote)
	})
}

// assertAttachCopies runs ATTACH PARTITION 'p0' FROM source into target and
// checks that target's p0 holds a copy of every source part: the same
// multisets of hash_of_all_files and of row LtHash, with the source unchanged.
func assertAttachCopies(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, sch payloadexec.TableSchema, source, target ddl.TableIntent) {
	t.Helper()
	before := activeParts(t, conn, source.Database, source.Table, "p0")
	sourceRows := rowHashList(t, conn, source.Database, source.Table, sch, before)
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s ATTACH PARTITION 'p0' FROM %s",
		qualified(target.Database, target.Table), qualified(source.Database, source.Table)))
	copied := activeParts(t, conn, target.Database, target.Table, "p0")
	if got, want := physHashes(copied), physHashes(before); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("ATTACH PARTITION FROM %s.%s changed hash_of_all_files: %v, source %v", source.Database, source.Table, got, want)
	}
	if got := rowHashList(t, conn, target.Database, target.Table, sch, copied); !slices.Equal(got, sourceRows) {
		t.Fatalf("ATTACH PARTITION FROM %s.%s changed the rows", source.Database, source.Table)
	}
	if after := activeParts(t, conn, source.Database, source.Table, "p0"); !slices.Equal(names(after), names(before)) {
		t.Fatalf("ATTACH PARTITION FROM changed its source: %v, was %v", names(after), names(before))
	}
}

// TestMechanics_AttachPartitionFromIsNotThrottledByPartsToThrowInsert (M2)
// pins why an install may attach more parts than an INSERT could write
// (spec §2, §8.5 step 5): ATTACH PARTITION FROM into a table whose
// parts_to_throw_insert is 3 attaches 5 parts, while an INSERT into that
// partition is refused with TOO_MANY_PARTS.
func TestMechanics_AttachPartitionFromIsNotThrottledByPartsToThrowInsert(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	p := mechanicsPinned(t)
	sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
	_, safe, promote := protocolTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, p, sch)
	throttled := promote
	throttled.Table = promote.Table + "_throttled"
	throttled.Settings = append(slices.Clone(promote.Settings),
		ddl.PinnedSetting{Name: "parts_to_delay_insert", Value: "2"},
		ddl.PinnedSetting{Name: "parts_to_throw_insert", Value: "3"})
	mustExec(t, env.A, throttled.SQL())
	for i := uint64(0); i < 5; i++ {
		mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 10*i, 2, nil)
	}
	source := activeParts(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0")
	if len(source) != 5 {
		t.Fatalf("source holds %d parts, want 5: %v", len(source), names(source))
	}
	mustExec(t, env.A, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s ATTACH PARTITION 'p0' FROM %s",
		qualified(throttled.Database, throttled.Table), qualified(safe.Database, safe.Table)))
	attached := activeParts(t, env.A, throttled.Database, throttled.Table, "p0")
	if got, want := physHashes(attached), physHashes(source); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("attached %v, want the 5 source parts %v", got, want)
	}
	err := insertRows(env.A, throttled.Database, throttled.Table, "p0", 1000, 1, nil)
	if clickHouseCode(err) != codeTooManyParts {
		t.Fatalf("INSERT into a partition of 5 parts with parts_to_throw_insert = 3: err = %v, want TOO_MANY_PARTS (252)", err)
	}
}

// assertOldPartsLifetime pins the window in which a restart resurrects the
// parts a REPLACE PARTITION retired: the server's old_parts_lifetime is 480 s.
func assertOldPartsLifetime(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn) {
	t.Helper()
	var value string
	var changed uint8
	if err := conn.QueryRow(context.Background(),
		"SELECT value, toUInt8(changed) FROM system.merge_tree_settings WHERE name = 'old_parts_lifetime'").Scan(&value, &changed); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.merge_tree_settings: %v", err)
	}
	if value != "480" {
		t.Fatalf("old_parts_lifetime = %s (changed by the server config: %d), want 480", value, changed)
	}
}

// assertProtocolDDLKeepsOldPartsLifetime pins that the protocol DDL does not
// override old_parts_lifetime, so its tables inherit the server's 480 s.
func assertProtocolDDLKeepsOldPartsLifetime(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, fx replaceFixture) {
	t.Helper()
	unsafe, safe, promote, err := ddl.Intents(fx.p, fx.sch)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, intent := range []ddl.TableIntent{unsafe, safe, promote} {
		for _, setting := range intent.Settings {
			if setting.Name == "old_parts_lifetime" {
				t.Fatalf("the protocol DDL of %s.%s pins old_parts_lifetime = %s", intent.Database, intent.Table, setting.Value)
			}
		}
	}
	for _, intent := range []ddl.TableIntent{safe, promote} {
		var create string
		if err := conn.QueryRow(context.Background(),
			"SELECT create_table_query FROM system.tables WHERE database = ? AND name = ?", intent.Database, intent.Table).Scan(&create); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("create_table_query of %s.%s: %v", intent.Database, intent.Table, err)
		}
		if strings.Contains(create, "old_parts_lifetime") {
			t.Fatalf("%s.%s sets old_parts_lifetime: %s", intent.Database, intent.Table, create)
		}
	}
}

// assertRetiredPartsAreOutdated pins the window M3 depends on: right after
// REPLACE the retired parts are still on disk, listed as outdated, not
// removed.
func assertRetiredPartsAreOutdated(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, fx replaceFixture) {
	t.Helper()
	all := partsOf(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table)
	for _, retired := range fx.retired {
		part, ok := partNamed(all, retired.Name)
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("REPLACE PARTITION removed retired part %s at once; system.parts lists %v", retired.Name, names(all))
		}
		if part.Active {
			t.Fatalf("retired part %s is still active after REPLACE PARTITION", retired.Name)
		}
	}
}

// assertResurrected checks the state a restart inside old_parts_lifetime
// leaves after replaceAPartition: every retired part is active again under its
// own name and hash_of_all_files, beside its replacement twin with the same
// hash_of_all_files and row LtHash, so p0 holds the retired rows twice. This
// is the state the owner audit repairs (spec §14).
func assertResurrected(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, fx replaceFixture) {
	t.Helper()
	active := activeParts(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, "p0")
	wantNames := append(names(fx.replacements), names(fx.retired)...)
	slices.Sort(wantNames)
	if got := names(active); !slices.Equal(got, wantNames) {
		t.Fatalf("active p0 parts %v, want the replacements and the resurrected retired parts %v", got, wantNames)
	}
	if got, want := totalRows(active), totalRows(fx.replacements)+totalRows(fx.retired); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("p0 holds %d rows, want %d: the replacements' and the resurrected parts'", got, want)
	}
	now := rowHashes(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, fx.sch, active)
	for _, retired := range fx.retired {
		part, _ := partNamed(active, retired.Name)
		if part.PhysHash != retired.PhysHash {
			t.Fatalf("resurrected %s has hash_of_all_files %s, it had %s", retired.Name, part.PhysHash, retired.PhysHash)
		}
		twin, ok := partWithHash(fx.replacements, retired.PhysHash)
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("resurrected %s has no replacement twin with hash_of_all_files %s", retired.Name, retired.PhysHash)
		}
		if now[retired.Name] != now[twin.Name] || now[retired.Name] != fx.retiredRowHashes[retired.Name] {
			t.Fatalf("resurrected %s row LtHash %s; its twin %s has %s; before REPLACE it had %s",
				retired.Name, abbreviate(now[retired.Name]), twin.Name, abbreviate(now[twin.Name]), abbreviate(fx.retiredRowHashes[retired.Name]))
		}
	}
}

// assertExactlyTheReplacements checks that p0's active parts are exactly what
// REPLACE published: the replacement parts by name and hash_of_all_files,
// with their rows, and no zero-row part (clarification K2).
func assertExactlyTheReplacements(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, fx replaceFixture, when string) {
	t.Helper()
	active := activeParts(t, conn, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table, "p0")
	if empty := zeroRowParts(active); len(empty) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s: active zero-row parts %v in p0; clarification K2 says none stays active", when, names(empty))
	}
	if got, want := names(active), names(fx.replacements); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("%s: active p0 parts %v, want exactly the replacements %v", when, got, want)
	}
	if got, want := physHashes(active), physHashes(fx.replacements); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("%s: hash_of_all_files %v, want %v", when, got, want)
	}
	if got, want := totalRows(active), totalRows(fx.replacements); got != want {
		t.Fatalf("%s: p0 holds %d rows, want %d", when, got, want)
	}
}

// assertNotDetached checks that no retired part is left in detached/.
func assertNotDetached(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, fx replaceFixture) {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := conn.Query(context.Background(),
		"SELECT name FROM system.detached_parts WHERE database = ? AND table = ?", fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.detached_parts: %v", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	for rows.Next() {
		var name string
		if err := rows.Scan(&name); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("scan system.detached_parts: %v", err)
		}
		if _, retired := partNamed(fx.retired, name); retired {
			t.Fatalf("retired part %s is left in detached/", name)
		}
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.detached_parts: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestMechanics_ReplacePartitionResurrectsReplacedPartsAfterARestart (M3)
// pins the hazard the owner audit exists for (spec §2 "Restart resurrection",
// §14): REPLACE PARTITION leaves the parts it retired on disk as outdated for
// old_parts_lifetime (480 s, which the protocol DDL does not override), and a
// restart inside that window makes them active again beside their equal-hash
// replacements, because the replacements' block ranges do not cover them. It
// pins both restart kinds production sees: an abrupt exit (SIGKILL, OOM kill)
// and a graceful shutdown (a pod deletion's SIGTERM). A row whose outcome
// changes on an image is a measured fact to record in Appendix B, not a test
// to weaken.
func TestMechanics_ReplacePartitionResurrectsReplacedPartsAfterARestart(t *testing.T) {
	requireMechanics(t)
	addr := requireRestartable(t)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name            string
		kind            restartKind
		wantResurrected bool
	}{
		{name: "abrupt", kind: restartAbrupt, wantResurrected: true},
		{name: "graceful", kind: restartGraceful, wantResurrected: true},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			conn := chtest.Open(t, addr)
			assertOldPartsLifetime(t, conn)
			fx := replaceAPartition(t, conn, addr)
			assertProtocolDDLKeepsOldPartsLifetime(t, conn, fx)
			assertRetiredPartsAreOutdated(t, conn, fx)
			restarted := restartServer(t, addr, tc.kind)
			waitLoaded(t, restarted, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table)
			if tc.wantResurrected {
				assertResurrected(t, restarted, fx)
			} else {
				assertExactlyTheReplacements(t, restarted, fx, "after a "+tc.name+" restart")
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestMechanics_DropPartitionThenAttachDoesNotResurrect (M4) pins the repair
// the spec uses instead of REPLACE PARTITION for a copy (§2, §8.5 step 2):
// DROP PARTITION followed by ATTACH PARTITION FROM a rebuilt scratch leaves
// exactly the attached rows active, and an abrupt restart inside the outdated
// window brings none of the dropped parts back.
func TestMechanics_DropPartitionThenAttachDoesNotResurrect(t *testing.T) {
	requireMechanics(t)
	addr := requireRestartable(t)
	conn := chtest.Open(t, addr)
	p := mechanicsPinned(t)
	sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
	_, safe, promote := protocolTables(t, conn, addr, p, sch)
	copyTable := qualified(p.SafeDB, safe.Table)
	scratchTable := qualified(p.PromoteDB, promote.Table)
	ensureUptime(t, conn, 2*chrestart.DefaultRestartSkew)
	// The copy holds two verified parts and a foreign one.
	mustInsert(t, conn, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 0, 2, nil)
	mustInsert(t, conn, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 2, 3, nil)
	mustInsert(t, conn, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 100, 4, nil)
	dropped := activeParts(t, conn, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0")
	if len(dropped) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("copy holds %d parts, want 3: %v", len(dropped), names(dropped))
	}
	// The rebuilt partition holds the verified rows only, written afresh.
	mustInsert(t, conn, p.PromoteDB, promote.Table, "p0", 0, 2, nil)
	mustInsert(t, conn, p.PromoteDB, promote.Table, "p0", 2, 3, nil)
	rebuilt := activeParts(t, conn, p.PromoteDB, promote.Table, "p0")
	rebuiltRows := rowHashList(t, conn, p.PromoteDB, promote.Table, sch, rebuilt)
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s DROP PARTITION 'p0'", copyTable))
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s ATTACH PARTITION 'p0' FROM %s", copyTable, scratchTable))
	check := func(c clickhouse.Conn, when string) {
		t.Helper()
		active := activeParts(t, c, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0")
		for _, part := range dropped {
			if _, back := partNamed(active, part.Name); back {
				t.Fatalf("%s: dropped part %s is active: %v", when, part.Name, names(active))
			}
		}
		if empty := zeroRowParts(active); len(empty) > 0 {
			t.Logf("%s: zero-row parts %v (DROP PARTITION's covering parts)", when, names(empty))
		}
		data := withRows(active)
		if got, want := physHashes(data), physHashes(rebuilt); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: parts with rows %v, want the attached rebuild %v", when, got, want)
		}
		if got := totalRows(data); got != 5 {
			t.Fatalf("%s: p0 holds %d rows, want the 5 verified rows", when, got)
		}
		if got := rowHashList(t, c, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, sch, data); !slices.Equal(got, rebuiltRows) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the copy's rows differ from the rebuild's", when)
		}
	}
	check(conn, "after the repair")
	restarted := restartServer(t, addr, restartAbrupt)
	waitLoaded(t, restarted, p.SafeDB, safe.Table)
	check(restarted, "after an abrupt restart")
}

// TestMechanics_DropPartOfAResurrectedTwinLeavesNoActivePartAndStaysDropped
// (M11) pins clarification K2, on which the owner audit's repair mode rests:
// after an abrupt restart resurrects the parts a REPLACE PARTITION retired,
// removing each resurrected twin leaves exactly the replacement parts active,
// leaves no active zero-row part, and the removed parts stay removed across a
// second abrupt restart. The audit uses ALTER TABLE ... DROP PART; DETACH
// PART followed by DROP DETACHED PART is the alternative K2 measured as
// equivalent. The zero-row check runs right after the drop, because the audit
// lists system.parts right after its drops.
func TestMechanics_DropPartOfAResurrectedTwinLeavesNoActivePartAndStaysDropped(t *testing.T) {
	requireMechanics(t)
	addr := requireRestartable(t)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		remove func(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, table, part string)
	}{
		{name: "drop_part", remove: func(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, table, part string) {
			mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s DROP PART %s", table, literal(part)))
		}},
		{name: "detach_part_then_drop_detached", remove: func(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, table, part string) {
			mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s DETACH PART %s", table, literal(part)))
			ctx := clickhouse.Context(context.Background(), clickhouse.WithSettings(clickhouse.Settings{"allow_drop_detached": 1}))
			if err := conn.Exec(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("ALTER TABLE %s DROP DETACHED PART %s", table, literal(part))); err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("drop detached part %s: %v", part, err)
			}
		}},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			fx := replaceAPartition(t, chtest.Open(t, addr), addr)
			restarted := restartServer(t, addr, restartAbrupt)
			waitLoaded(t, restarted, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table)
			assertResurrected(t, restarted, fx)
			safeTable := qualified(fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table)
			for _, retired := range fx.retired {
				tc.remove(t, restarted, safeTable, retired.Name)
			}
			assertExactlyTheReplacements(t, restarted, fx, "right after removing the resurrected twins")
			assertNotDetached(t, restarted, fx)
			again := restartServer(t, addr, restartAbrupt)
			waitLoaded(t, again, fx.p.SafeDB, fx.table)
			assertExactlyTheReplacements(t, again, fx, "after a second abrupt restart")
			assertNotDetached(t, again, fx)
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package chmechanics

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"testing"
	"time"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
)

// backupStats is a BACKUP or RESTORE result with its system.backups sizes.
type backupStats struct {
	ID               string
	Status           string
	NumFiles         uint64
	NumEntries       uint64
	TotalSize        uint64
	UncompressedSize uint64
	CompressedSize   uint64
}

// runBackup runs one synchronous BACKUP or RESTORE statement, requires the
// status it answers, and returns its system.backups row.
func runBackup(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, statement, wantStatus string) backupStats {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	var s backupStats
	if err := conn.QueryRow(ctx, statement).Scan(&s.ID, &s.Status); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", statement, err)
	}
	if s.Status != wantStatus {
		t.Fatalf("%s: status %s, want %s", statement, s.Status, wantStatus)
	}
	if err := conn.QueryRow(ctx,
		"SELECT num_files, num_entries, total_size, uncompressed_size, compressed_size FROM system.backups WHERE id = ?", s.ID).
		Scan(&s.NumFiles, &s.NumEntries, &s.TotalSize, &s.UncompressedSize, &s.CompressedSize); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.backups row %s: %v", s.ID, err)
	}
	return s
}

// TestMechanics_BackupRestorePartitionsKeepsHashOfAllFiles (M5) pins the
// object-store transport of P1 and the restore source of spec §8.6: BACKUP
// ... PARTITIONS with base_backup stores only what its base lacks (fewer
// bytes, and fewer stored entries than the files it describes), and
// RESTORE ... AS <staging> PARTITIONS from it restores every part of the
// partition, the base's included, with its hash_of_all_files and rows, and no
// other partition.
func TestMechanics_BackupRestorePartitionsKeepsHashOfAllFiles(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	p := mechanicsPinned(t)
	sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
	_, safe, _ := protocolTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, p, sch)
	source := qualified(p.SafeDB, safe.Table)
	mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 0, 100_000, nil)
	mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p1", 0, 10, nil)
	name := fmt.Sprintf("mech_%s_%d", suffix(t), time.Now().UnixNano())
	fullDisk := fmt.Sprintf("Disk('backups', %s)", literal(name+"_full"))
	incDisk := fmt.Sprintf("Disk('backups', %s)", literal(name+"_inc"))
	full := runBackup(t, env.A, fmt.Sprintf("BACKUP TABLE %s PARTITIONS 'p0' TO %s", source, fullDisk), "BACKUP_CREATED")
	mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 100_000, 10, nil)
	inc := runBackup(t, env.A, fmt.Sprintf("BACKUP TABLE %s PARTITIONS 'p0' TO %s SETTINGS base_backup = %s", source, incDisk, fullDisk), "BACKUP_CREATED")
	t.Logf("full backup %+v; incremental backup %+v", full, inc)
	if inc.UncompressedSize >= full.UncompressedSize {
		t.Fatalf("the incremental backup stores %d bytes, not less than the full backup's %d: base_backup was not used", inc.UncompressedSize, full.UncompressedSize)
	}
	// It describes every file of the partition but stores only the new ones.
	if inc.NumEntries >= inc.NumFiles {
		t.Fatalf("the incremental backup stores %d of the %d files it describes: base_backup was not used", inc.NumEntries, inc.NumFiles)
	}
	stage := "hg_rstage_m" + suffix(t)
	dropDatabasesAt(t, env.AAddr, stage)
	mustExec(t, env.A, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+ident(stage))
	runBackup(t, env.A, fmt.Sprintf("RESTORE TABLE %s AS %s PARTITIONS 'p0' FROM %s", source, qualified(stage, safe.Table), incDisk), "RESTORED")
	want := activeParts(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0")
	got := activeParts(t, env.A, stage, safe.Table, "p0")
	if len(want) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("source p0 holds %d parts, want 2: %v", len(want), names(want))
	}
	if gotHashes, wantHashes := physHashes(got), physHashes(want); !slices.Equal(gotHashes, wantHashes) {
		t.Fatalf("RESTORE from the incremental backup: hash_of_all_files %v, source %v", gotHashes, wantHashes)
	}
	if rows := totalRows(got); rows != 100_010 {
		t.Fatalf("the staging p0 holds %d rows, want 100010", rows)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(rowHashList(t, env.A, stage, safe.Table, sch, got), rowHashList(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, sch, want)) {
		t.Fatal("the restored rows differ from the source's")
	}
	if other := activeParts(t, env.A, stage, safe.Table, "p1"); len(other) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("RESTORE ... PARTITIONS 'p0' restored partition p1: %v", names(other))
	}
}
```

```go
package chmechanics

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/chtest"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/ddl"
)

// pullRows is above the default min_insert_block_size_rows (1,048,449), so an
// INSERT ... SELECT with default settings splits a part this large.
const pullRows = 1_200_000

// noSplitSettings are spec §2's measured settings under which INSERT ...
// SELECT writes a source part of rows rows as one part.
func noSplitSettings(rows uint64) clickhouse.Settings {
	return clickhouse.Settings{
		"min_insert_block_size_rows":  rows,
		"min_insert_block_size_bytes": 0,
		"max_threads":                 1,
		"max_insert_threads":          1,
	}
}

// remoteTable is the remote() table function over db.table on peer.
func remoteTable(peer, db, table, user, password string) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("remote(%s, %s, %s, %s, %s)", literal(peer), literal(db), literal(table), literal(user), literal(password))
}

// pullPart copies the part named name out of source (a remote() table
// function) into db.table with INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE _part = name, the
// member's owner pull (spec §8.6): single-threaded, plus extra settings.
func pullPart(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, db, table, source, name string, extra clickhouse.Settings) {
	t.Helper()
	settings := clickhouse.Settings{"max_threads": 1, "max_insert_threads": 1}
	for key, value := range extra {
		settings[key] = value
	}
	ctx := clickhouse.Context(context.Background(), clickhouse.WithSettings(settings))
	rowID := ident(ddl.RowIDColumn)
	query := fmt.Sprintf("INSERT INTO %s (%s, `p`, `v`) SELECT %s, `p`, `v` FROM %s WHERE _part = %s",
		qualified(db, table), rowID, rowID, source, literal(name))
	if err := conn.Exec(ctx, query); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("pull part %s into %s.%s: %v", name, db, table, err)
	}
}

// writeThroughRemote inserts one row into target, an INSERT INTO FUNCTION
// remote(...) target.
func writeThroughRemote(conn clickhouse.Conn, target string) error {
	return conn.Exec(context.Background(), fmt.Sprintf(
		"INSERT INTO FUNCTION %s (%s, `p`, `v`) VALUES (%s, 'p0', 1000)",
		target, ident(ddl.RowIDColumn), literal(strings.Repeat("0", 31)+"1")))
}

// createUser creates a password user on conn, applies each grant (a format
// string whose one %s is the user's quoted name), and drops the user when the
// test ends.
func createUser(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr, name string, grants ...string) string {
	t.Helper()
	password := randomHex(t, 16)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		c, err := dial(context.Background(), addr)
		if err != nil {
			t.Logf("cleanup: cannot reach %s to drop user %s: %v", addr, name, err)
			return
		}
		defer func() { _ = c.Close() }()
		if err := c.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP USER IF EXISTS "+ident(name)); err != nil {
			t.Logf("cleanup: drop user %s: %v", name, err)
		}
	})
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("CREATE USER %s IDENTIFIED WITH sha256_password BY %s", ident(name), literal(password)))
	for _, grant := range grants {
		mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf(grant, ident(name)))
	}
	return password
}

// accessTypes lists the user's system.grants access types.
func accessTypes(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, user string) []string {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := conn.Query(context.Background(), "SELECT toString(access_type) FROM system.grants WHERE user_name = ?", user)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.grants of %s: %v", user, err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var out []string
	for rows.Next() {
		var accessType string
		if err := rows.Scan(&accessType); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("scan system.grants: %v", err)
		}
		out = append(out, accessType)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system.grants of %s: %v", user, err)
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

// createCollection creates a named collection on conn holding the owner
// connection of spec §8.6 (host, port, user and password; database and table
// are passed per call), each key NOT OVERRIDABLE when locked, and drops it
// when the test ends. name must be a plain identifier.
func createCollection(t *testing.T, conn clickhouse.Conn, addr, name string, locked bool, host string, port uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	modifier := ""
	if locked {
		modifier = " NOT OVERRIDABLE"
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		c, err := dial(context.Background(), addr)
		if err != nil {
			t.Logf("cleanup: cannot reach %s to drop named collection %s: %v", addr, name, err)
			return
		}
		defer func() { _ = c.Close() }()
		if err := c.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP NAMED COLLECTION IF EXISTS "+name); err != nil {
			t.Logf("cleanup: drop named collection %s: %v", name, err)
		}
	})
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf("CREATE NAMED COLLECTION %s AS host = %s%s, port = %d%s, user = 'default'%s, password = ''%s",
		name, literal(host), modifier, port, modifier, modifier, modifier))
}

func splitPeer(t *testing.T, peer string) (string, uint64) {
	t.Helper()
	host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(peer)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s %q: %v", envPeerAddr, peer, err)
	}
	n, err := strconv.ParseUint(port, 10, 16)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s %q port: %v", envPeerAddr, peer, err)
	}
	return host, n
}

// TestMechanics_NoSplitPullYieldsOnePart (M6) pins the owner pull of spec
// §8.6: node B copies one 1.2M-row part of node A with INSERT ... SELECT FROM
// remote(...) WHERE _part = <name>. With default settings the copy splits into
// parts whose row LtHashes sum to the source's; with the no-split settings it
// is one part with the source's row LtHash; and the name resolves by
// hash_of_all_files under the reader grant of §8.6.
func TestMechanics_NoSplitPullYieldsOnePart(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	src := mechanicsPinned(t)
	sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
	_, safe, promote := protocolTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, src, sch)
	mustInsert(t, env.A, src.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 0, pullRows, noSplitSettings(pullRows))
	sourceParts := activeParts(t, env.A, src.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0")
	if len(sourceParts) != 1 || sourceParts[0].Rows != pullRows {
		t.Fatalf("source %+v, want one part of %d rows (the no-split settings hold for a local INSERT ... SELECT too)", sourceParts, pullRows)
	}
	source := sourceParts[0]
	sourceRowHash := rowHashes(t, env.A, src.SafeDB, safe.Table, sch, sourceParts)[source.Name]
	// scratch is an empty table of the same structure on node B, the member's
	// hg_rstage scratch (spec §8.5 step 3).
	scratch := func(t *testing.T) (string, string) {
		t.Helper()
		intent := promote
		intent.Database = mechanicsPinned(t).PromoteDB
		createTables(t, env.B, env.BAddr, intent)
		return intent.Database, intent.Table
	}
	asDefault := remoteTable(env.PeerAddr, src.SafeDB, safe.Table, "default", "")

	t.Run("default_settings_split_the_part", func(t *testing.T) {
		db, table := scratch(t)
		pullPart(t, env.B, db, table, asDefault, source.Name, nil)
		parts := activeParts(t, env.B, db, table, "p0")
		if len(parts) < 2 {
			t.Fatalf("control: the default settings wrote %d part(s), want a split: %+v", len(parts), parts)
		}
		if rows := totalRows(parts); rows != pullRows {
			t.Fatalf("control: %d rows, want %d", rows, pullRows)
		}
		var hashes []string
		for _, h := range rowHashes(t, env.B, db, table, sch, parts) {
			hashes = append(hashes, h)
		}
		if got := sumRowHashes(t, hashes...); got != sourceRowHash {
			t.Fatalf("control: the split parts sum to %s, the source part is %s", abbreviate(got), abbreviate(sourceRowHash))
		}
	})
	t.Run("no_split_settings_keep_one_part", func(t *testing.T) {
		db, table := scratch(t)
		pullPart(t, env.B, db, table, asDefault, source.Name, noSplitSettings(pullRows))
		parts := activeParts(t, env.B, db, table, "p0")
		if len(parts) != 1 || parts[0].Rows != pullRows {
			t.Fatalf("no-split pull wrote %+v, want one part of %d rows", parts, pullRows)
		}
		if got := rowHashes(t, env.B, db, table, sch, parts)[parts[0].Name]; got != sourceRowHash {
			t.Fatalf("no-split pull row LtHash %s, source %s", abbreviate(got), abbreviate(sourceRowHash))
		}
	})
	t.Run("reader_grant_resolves_the_part_by_hash_of_all_files", func(t *testing.T) {
		reader := "mech_reader_" + suffix(t)
		password := createUser(t, env.A, env.AAddr, reader,
			"GRANT SELECT ON "+ident(src.SafeDB)+".* TO %s",
			"GRANT SHOW COLUMNS ON system.parts TO %s",
			"GRANT SELECT(database, table, name, active, rows, partition_id, hash_of_all_files) ON system.parts TO %s")
		parts := fmt.Sprintf("remote(%s, 'system', 'parts', %s, %s)", literal(env.PeerAddr), literal(reader), literal(password))
		var resolved string
		if err := env.B.QueryRow(context.Background(), fmt.Sprintf(
			"SELECT name FROM %s WHERE database = %s AND table = %s AND active AND hash_of_all_files = %s",
			parts, literal(src.SafeDB), literal(safe.Table), literal(source.PhysHash))).Scan(&resolved); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("resolve the part by hash_of_all_files as %s: %v", reader, err)
		}
		if resolved != source.Name {
			t.Fatalf("hash_of_all_files %s resolved to %s, want %s", source.PhysHash, resolved, source.Name)
		}
		db, table := scratch(t)
		pullPart(t, env.B, db, table, remoteTable(env.PeerAddr, src.SafeDB, safe.Table, reader, password), resolved, noSplitSettings(pullRows))
		pulled := activeParts(t, env.B, db, table, "p0")
		if len(pulled) != 1 || rowHashes(t, env.B, db, table, sch, pulled)[pulled[0].Name] != sourceRowHash {
			t.Fatalf("the reader's no-split pull wrote %+v, want one part with the source's row LtHash", pulled)
		}
	})
}

// TestMechanics_ReadOnRemoteRefusesWrites (M7) pins the member's transport
// grant (spec §8.2, §8.6): a user with READ ON REMOTE reads through remote()
// but its INSERT INTO FUNCTION remote(...) is refused with ACCESS_DENIED and
// writes nothing, and system.grants shows READ and no WRITE; a user granted
// REMOTE, with the same target user, writes.
func TestMechanics_ReadOnRemoteRefusesWrites(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	p := mechanicsPinned(t)
	sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
	_, safe, _ := protocolTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, p, sch)
	mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 0, 3, nil)
	target := remoteTable(env.PeerAddr, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "default", "")
	onA := qualified(p.SafeDB, safe.Table)

	t.Run("read_on_remote", func(t *testing.T) {
		user := "mech_member_" + suffix(t)
		password := createUser(t, env.B, env.BAddr, user, "GRANT READ ON REMOTE TO %s", "GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.* TO %s")
		member := chtest.OpenAs(t, env.BAddr, user, password)
		if n := mustCountRows(t, member, target); n != 3 {
			t.Fatalf("read through remote(): %d rows, want 3", n)
		}
		err := writeThroughRemote(member, target)
		if clickHouseCode(err) != codeAccessDenied || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "WRITE ON REMOTE") {
			t.Fatalf("a READ ON REMOTE user wrote through remote(): err = %v, want ACCESS_DENIED (497) naming WRITE ON REMOTE", err)
		}
		t.Logf("READ ON REMOTE refusal: %v", err)
		if n := mustCountRows(t, env.A, onA); n != 3 {
			t.Fatalf("the refused write reached node A: %d rows, want 3", n)
		}
		grants := accessTypes(t, env.B, user)
		if !slices.Contains(grants, "READ") || slices.Contains(grants, "WRITE") {
			t.Fatalf("system.grants of %s: %v, want READ and no WRITE", user, grants)
		}
	})
	t.Run("remote_grant_allows_writes", func(t *testing.T) {
		user := "mech_remote_" + suffix(t)
		password := createUser(t, env.B, env.BAddr, user, "GRANT REMOTE ON *.* TO %s", "GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.* TO %s")
		if err := writeThroughRemote(chtest.OpenAs(t, env.BAddr, user, password), target); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("a REMOTE user's write through remote(): %v", err)
		}
		if n := mustCountRows(t, env.A, onA); n != 4 {
			t.Fatalf("node A holds %d rows after the REMOTE user's write, want 4", n)
		}
	})
}

// TestMechanics_NotOverridableCollectionRefusesOverride (M8) pins the owner
// collection of spec §8.6: with host, port, user and password NOT OVERRIDABLE
// a call that overrides user is refused with BAD_ARGUMENTS (even with the
// same value), while the same override of a control collection without the
// clause works; and a user without GRANT NAMED COLLECTION cannot use the
// collection until granted.
func TestMechanics_NotOverridableCollectionRefusesOverride(t *testing.T) {
	env := requireMechanics(t)
	p := mechanicsPinned(t)
	sch := mechanicsSchema(t)
	_, safe, _ := protocolTables(t, env.A, env.AAddr, p, sch)
	mustInsert(t, env.A, p.SafeDB, safe.Table, "p0", 0, 3, nil)
	host, port := splitPeer(t, env.PeerAddr)
	locked := "mech_nc_locked_" + suffix(t)
	open := "mech_nc_open_" + suffix(t)
	createCollection(t, env.B, env.BAddr, locked, true, host, port)
	createCollection(t, env.B, env.BAddr, open, false, host, port)
	through := func(collection, overrides string) string {
		return fmt.Sprintf("remote(%s, database = %s, table = %s%s)", collection, literal(p.SafeDB), literal(safe.Table), overrides)
	}
	if n := mustCountRows(t, env.B, through(locked, "")); n != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("read through %s: %d rows, want 3", locked, n)
	}
	_, err := countRows(env.B, through(locked, ", user = 'default'"))
	var exception *clickhouse.Exception
	if !errors.As(err, &exception) || exception.Code != codeBadArguments || !strings.Contains(exception.Message, "Override not allowed for 'user'") {
		t.Fatalf("overriding a NOT OVERRIDABLE key: err = %v, want BAD_ARGUMENTS (36) Override not allowed for 'user'", err)
	}
	t.Logf("NOT OVERRIDABLE refusal: code %d: %s", exception.Code, exception.Message)
	if n := mustCountRows(t, env.B, through(open, ", user = 'default'")); n != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("the control collection with the same override read %d rows, want 3", n)
	}
	user := "mech_nc_user_" + suffix(t)
	password := createUser(t, env.B, env.BAddr, user, "GRANT READ ON REMOTE TO %s", "GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.* TO %s")
	if _, err := countRows(chtest.OpenAs(t, env.BAddr, user, password), through(locked, "")); clickHouseCode(err) != codeAccessDenied {
		t.Fatalf("a user without GRANT NAMED COLLECTION used %s: err = %v, want ACCESS_DENIED (497)", locked, err)
	}
	mustExec(t, env.B, fmt.Sprintf("GRANT NAMED COLLECTION ON %s TO %s", locked, ident(user)))
	if n := mustCountRows(t, chtest.OpenAs(t, env.BAddr, user, password), through(locked, "")); n != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("the granted user read %d rows through %s, want 3", n, locked)
	}
}
```
