```go
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority/authoritytest"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter/fsm"
)

// recordingIssuanceGate is an IssuanceGate that holds the rows hold selects
// and records every call with the FSM's PromotionSeq when the lease began
// and when it was released.
type recordingIssuanceGate struct {
	f *fsm.FSM

	mu           sync.Mutex
	hold         func(fsm.PromotionWork) string
	calls        []fsm.PromotionWork
	held         []fsm.PromotionWork
	seqAtBegin   []uint64
	seqAtRelease []uint64
}

func (g *recordingIssuanceGate) BeginPromotionIssuance(work fsm.PromotionWork) (func(), bool, string) {
	g.mu.Lock()
	defer g.mu.Unlock()
	g.calls = append(g.calls, work)
	g.seqAtBegin = append(g.seqAtBegin, g.f.PromotionSeqView())
	if g.hold != nil {
		if reason := g.hold(work); reason != "" {
			g.held = append(g.held, work)
			return func() {}, true, reason
		}
	}
	return func() {
		g.mu.Lock()
		defer g.mu.Unlock()
		g.seqAtRelease = append(g.seqAtRelease, g.f.PromotionSeqView())
	}, false, ""
}

func (g *recordingIssuanceGate) setHold(hold func(fsm.PromotionWork) string) {
	g.mu.Lock()
	defer g.mu.Unlock()
	g.hold = hold
}

func (g *recordingIssuanceGate) snapshot() (calls, held []fsm.PromotionWork, atBegin, atRelease []uint64) {
	g.mu.Lock()
	defer g.mu.Unlock()
	return slices.Clone(g.calls), slices.Clone(g.held), slices.Clone(g.seqAtBegin), slices.Clone(g.seqAtRelease)
}

// TestIssuanceLeaseSpansThePromotionSeqReadAndTheProposal: clarification K7.
// The gate is asked before PromotionSeq is read and released only once the
// RecordPromotionIssued proposal applied, with the row's block and track.
func TestIssuanceLeaseSpansThePromotionSeqReadAndTheProposal(t *testing.T) {
	f, node, _, o, params, _ := tracksHarnessO(t)
	gate := &recordingIssuanceGate{f: f}
	o.d.Issuance = gate
	key0 := authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex0)
	submitTrackStatementO(t, node, params, testAccountO(t), 1)
	sealViaNode(t, node)
	verifyTrackBlockO(t, node, f, key0, 1, "p0", 2)
	drivePromotionsO(t, o, f, "promotion 1 issued", func(ws fsm.WorkSet) bool { return len(ws.IssuedUnacked) == 1 })
	calls, held, atBegin, atRelease := gate.snapshot()
	if len(calls) != 1 || len(held) != 0 || calls[0].BlockSeq != 1 || calls[0].Track == nil || calls[0].Track.IndexerID != 1 || calls[0].Partition.PartitionID != "p0" {
		t.Fatalf("gate calls = %+v, held %+v", calls, held)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(atBegin, []uint64{0}) || !slices.Equal(atRelease, []uint64{1}) {
		t.Fatalf("PromotionSeq at begin %v and release %v, want [0] and [1]", atBegin, atRelease)
	}
}

// TestHeldIssuanceStopsRecordPromotionIssuedButNotAcksOrCleanups: spec
// §10.1. Under a hold that refuses every issuance, the next block's
// promotion is neither signed nor proposed nor streamed, while publication,
// cleanup scheduling and the cleanup's stream to the source continue.
func TestHeldIssuanceStopsRecordPromotionIssuedButNotAcksOrCleanups(t *testing.T) {
	f, node, fsn, o, params, _ := tracksHarnessO(t)
	gate := &recordingIssuanceGate{f: f}
	o.d.Issuance = gate
	key0 := authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex0)
	acct := testAccountO(t)
	submitTrackStatementO(t, node, params, acct, 1)
	sealViaNode(t, node)
	verifyTrackBlockO(t, node, f, key0, 1, "p0", 2)
	drivePromotionsO(t, o, f, "promotion 1 issued", func(ws fsm.WorkSet) bool { return len(ws.IssuedUnacked) == 1 })
	ackSignedPromotionViaNode(t, node, f, key0, "s1", 1)
	submitTrackStatementO(t, node, params, acct, 2)
	sealViaNode(t, node)
	verifyTrackBlockO(t, node, f, key0, 2, "p1", 2)

	gate.setHold(func(fsm.PromotionWork) string { return "an issuance hold refuses every new promotion" })
	sent := sentLenO(fsn)
	drivePromotionsO(t, o, f, "cleanup of promotion 1 scheduled", func(ws fsm.WorkSet) bool { return len(ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups) == 1 })
	ws, err := f.WorkSet()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := o.handlePromotionRows(t.Context(), ws); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := f.PromotionSeqView(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("PromotionSeq = %d under the hold, want 1", got)
	}
	if f.SafeWatermarkView().SafeBlockSeq != 1 || ws.ScheduledUnackedCleanups[0].PromotionSeq != 1 || len(ws.PromotablePending) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("publication and cleanup must continue under the hold: watermark %+v, work %+v", f.SafeWatermarkView(), ws)
	}
	_, held, _, _ := gate.snapshot()
	if len(held) == 0 || held[len(held)-1].BlockSeq != 2 || held[len(held)-1].Partition.PartitionID != "p1" {
		t.Fatalf("held rows = %+v, want block 2's", held)
	}
	msgs, to := sentSinceO(fsn, sent)
	cleanups := 0
	for i, m := range msgs {
		if m.GetPromote() != nil {
			t.Fatalf("a promotion was streamed under the hold: %v", m)
		}
		if m.GetCleanup() != nil {
			cleanups++
			if to[i] != "s1" {
				t.Fatalf("cleanup sent to %s", to[i])
			}
		}
	}
	if cleanups == 0 {
		t.Fatal("the cleanup of promotion 1 was not streamed under the hold")
	}
}

// TestNilIssuanceGateIssuesAsBefore: a loop without a gate issues and
// streams promotions exactly as before this task.
func TestNilIssuanceGateIssuesAsBefore(t *testing.T) {
	f, node, fsn, o, params, _ := tracksHarnessO(t)
	if o.IssuanceGate() != nil {
		t.Fatal("the harness loop has a gate")
	}
	key0 := authoritytest.MustSigner(t, authoritytest.IndexerKeyHex0)
	submitTrackStatementO(t, node, params, testAccountO(t), 1)
	sealViaNode(t, node)
	verifyTrackBlockO(t, node, f, key0, 1, "p0", 2)
	sent := sentLenO(fsn)
	drivePromotionsO(t, o, f, "promotion 1 issued", func(ws fsm.WorkSet) bool { return len(ws.IssuedUnacked) == 1 })
	msgs, to := sentSinceO(fsn, sent)
	if f.PromotionSeqView() != 1 || len(msgs) == 0 || msgs[0].GetPromote() == nil || to[0] != "s1" {
		t.Fatalf("PromotionSeq %d, sent %v to %v", f.PromotionSeqView(), msgs, to)
	}
}
```

```go
// IssuanceGate is the leader's consensus-hold gate around promotion issuance
// (plan S3-A clarification K7; *server.ConsensusHolds implements it). The
// loop calls BeginPromotionIssuance before it reads PromotionSeq for a new
// promotion. held means the leader's hold refuses this promotion now (an
// issuance hold refuses every one, drain mode one beyond its track's
// recorded frontier block) and nothing is signed or proposed; otherwise the
// loop holds the shared issuance lease until its RecordPromotionIssued
// proposal returned and then calls release, so a hold, which takes the lease
// exclusively, reads a PromotionSeq no issuance can still move.
type IssuanceGate interface {
	BeginPromotionIssuance(fsm.PromotionWork) (release func(), held bool, reason string)
}
```

```go
func (o *Loop) issuePromotion(ctx context.Context, pw fsm.PromotionWork) error {
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !o.authoritySignerReady("promotion issuance") {
		return nil
	}
	// The issuance lease (plan S3-A clarification K7): held from before the
	// PromotionSeq read through the RecordPromotionIssued proposal, so a
	// consensus hold, which takes it exclusively, freezes an exact sequence.
	release := func() {}
	if o.d.Issuance != nil {
		var held bool
		var reason string
		release, held, reason = o.d.Issuance.BeginPromotionIssuance(pw)
		if held {
			o.d.Logger.Debug("promotion issuance held by a consensus hold", "partition", pw.Partition, "block", pw.BlockSeq, "reason", reason)
			return nil
		}
	}
	cmd, jws, recorded, err := o.recordPromotion(ctx, pw)
	release()
	if err != nil || !recorded {
		return err
	}
	return o.streamPromotionSigned(ctx, cmd, jws)
}

// recordPromotion signs pw as the next promotion and proposes its
// RecordPromotionIssued. recorded is false with a nil error when the signing
// context is not ready, signing fails or the FSM refuses the proposal; those
// cases are logged and retried on a later pass, as before.
func (o *Loop) recordPromotion(ctx context.Context, pw fsm.PromotionWork) (arbiter.PromoteSafePartition, string, bool, error) {
	if err := o.d.Node.VerifyLeader(); err != nil {
		return arbiter.PromoteSafePartition{}, "", false, fmt.Errorf("verify leader before promotion sign: %w", err)
	}
	cmd := arbiter.PromoteSafePartition{
		TableID:            pw.Partition.TableID,
		PartitionID:        pw.Partition.PartitionID,
		PromotionSeq:       o.d.FSM.PromotionSeqView() + 1,
		BaseSafeSnapshotID: pw.BaseSafeSnapshotID,
		BasePartitionRoot:  pw.BasePartitionRoot,
		CandidateParts:     append([]arbiter.PartRef(nil), pw.Parts...),
	}
	signingContext, ready := o.authoritySigningContext("promotion signing")
	if !ready {
		return cmd, "", false, nil
	}
	jws, err := o.d.Signer.SignPromotionWithContext(cmd, signingContext)
	if err != nil {
		o.d.Logger.Warn("sign promotion failed", "partition", pw.Partition, "err", err)
		return cmd, "", false, nil
	}
	if _, err := o.propose(ctx, wire.Command{RecordPromotionIssued: &wire.RecordPromotionIssued{Promote: cmd, AuthorityJWS: jws}}); err != nil {
		if errors.Is(err, ErrRejected) {
			return cmd, "", false, nil
		}
		return cmd, "", false, fmt.Errorf("record promotion issued seq %d: %w", cmd.PromotionSeq, err)
	}
	return cmd, jws, true, nil
}
```

```go
// TestLoadConsensusHoldLimits: plan S3-A contract §4. max_issuance_hold
// defaults to 2m and max_drain_mode to 10m; both must be positive.
func TestLoadConsensusHoldLimits(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name         string
		block        string
		wantIssuance time.Duration
		wantDrain    time.Duration
		wantErr      string
	}{
		{name: "absent", wantIssuance: 2 * time.Minute, wantDrain: 10 * time.Minute},
		{name: "configured", block: "consensus_admin:\n  max_issuance_hold: 45s\n  max_drain_mode: 20m\n", wantIssuance: 45 * time.Second, wantDrain: 20 * time.Minute},
		{name: "zero issuance hold", block: "consensus_admin:\n  max_issuance_hold: 0s\n", wantErr: "consensus_admin.max_issuance_hold must be positive"},
		{name: "negative drain mode", block: "consensus_admin:\n  max_drain_mode: -1m\n", wantErr: "consensus_admin.max_drain_mode must be positive"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			cfg, err := Load(writeConfig(t, minimal+tc.block))
			if tc.wantErr != "" {
				if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.wantErr) {
					t.Fatalf("got %v, want %q", err, tc.wantErr)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if cfg.ConsensusAdmin.MaxIssuanceHold.Duration != tc.wantIssuance || cfg.ConsensusAdmin.MaxDrainMode.Duration != tc.wantDrain {
				t.Fatalf("consensus_admin = %+v, want issuance %v drain %v", cfg.ConsensusAdmin, tc.wantIssuance, tc.wantDrain)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestLoad_RejectsOversizedConsensusHolds: a hold stops promotion issuance,
// so its caps are short: at most 10m for an issuance hold, 1h for drain mode.
func TestLoad_RejectsOversizedConsensusHolds(t *testing.T) {
	for block, want := range map[string]string{
		"consensus_admin:\n  max_issuance_hold: 11m\n": "consensus_admin.max_issuance_hold must be at most 10m0s",
		"consensus_admin:\n  max_drain_mode: 61m\n":    "consensus_admin.max_drain_mode must be at most 1h0m0s",
	} {
		if _, err := Load(writeConfig(t, minimal+block)); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), want) {
			t.Fatalf("%q: got %v, want %q", block, err, want)
		}
	}
	cfg, err := Load(writeConfig(t, minimal+"consensus_admin:\n  max_issuance_hold: 10m\n  max_drain_mode: 1h\n"))
	if err != nil || cfg.ConsensusAdmin.MaxIssuanceHold.Duration != 10*time.Minute || cfg.ConsensusAdmin.MaxDrainMode.Duration != time.Hour {
		t.Fatalf("the caps themselves = %+v, %v", cfg.ConsensusAdmin, err)
	}
}
```

```go
package metrics

import (
	"strings"

// TestConsensusHoldMetrics: both mode series of the active gauge exist at 0
// from the start, the gauge follows a hold, and the outcome and held-issuance
// counters count.
func TestConsensusHoldMetrics(t *testing.T) {
	m := New(laneSnapshot{fsm.MetricsSnapshot{}})
	gauge := func(drain, issuance string) string {
		return `
# HELP arbiter_consensus_hold_active Whether this leader holds a consensus hold of the mode (issuance or drain): 0 or 1. Holds are leader-local and end on commit, refusal, release, timeout or leadership loss.
# TYPE arbiter_consensus_hold_active gauge
arbiter_consensus_hold_active{mode="drain"} ` + drain + `
arbiter_consensus_hold_active{mode="issuance"} ` + issuance + `
`
	}
	if err := testutil.GatherAndCompare(m.registry, strings.NewReader(gauge("0", "0")), "arbiter_consensus_hold_active"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.ConsensusHoldActive("drain", true)
	if err := testutil.GatherAndCompare(m.registry, strings.NewReader(gauge("1", "0")), "arbiter_consensus_hold_active"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	m.ConsensusHoldActive("drain", false)
	m.ConsensusHoldEnded("drain", "committed")
	m.ConsensusHoldEnded("issuance", "expired")
	m.ConsensusHoldEnded("issuance", "expired")
	m.PromotionIssuanceHeld()
	m.PromotionIssuanceHeld()
	m.PromotionIssuanceHeld()
	if err := testutil.GatherAndCompare(m.registry, strings.NewReader(gauge("0", "0")), "arbiter_consensus_hold_active"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := testutil.ToFloat64(m.holdsEnded.WithLabelValues("drain", "committed")); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("drain/committed = %v", got)
	}
	if got := testutil.ToFloat64(m.holdsEnded.WithLabelValues("issuance", "expired")); got != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("issuance/expired = %v", got)
	}
	if got := testutil.ToFloat64(m.heldPromotions); got != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("held promotions = %v", got)
	}
}
```

```go
		Name: "arbiter_consensus_holds_total",
		Help: "Consensus holds this node ended, by mode (issuance, drain) and outcome (committed, refused, released, expired, leadership_lost).",
	}, []string{"mode", "outcome"})
	m.heldPromotions = prometheus.NewCounter(prometheus.CounterOpts{
		Name: "arbiter_consensus_hold_held_promotions_total",
		Help: "Promotion issuances this leader skipped because a consensus hold refused them; the orchestrator retries each on its next pass while the hold lasts.",
	})
	// Both mode series exist from the start, so an alert on the gauge never
	// reads an absent series as no hold.
	for _, mode := range []string{"issuance", "drain"} {
		m.holdActive.WithLabelValues(mode).Set(0)
	}
	m.registry.MustRegister(m.holdActive, m.holdsEnded, m.heldPromotions)
```

Create `cmd/arbiter-admin/consensus_hold_test.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/hashicorp/raft"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/authority"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/wire"
	pb "github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-proto/gen/pb"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/codes"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/metadata"
	"google.golang.org/grpc/status"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"
	"google.golang.org/protobuf/types/known/emptypb"

	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter/fsm"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter/server"
)

const (
	issuanceHold = pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_ISSUANCE
	drainHold    = pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_DRAIN
)

// fastHoldPolls shortens the CLI's hold polling for one test.
func fastHoldPolls(t *testing.T) {
	t.Helper()
	previous := holdPollInterval
	holdPollInterval = 5 * time.Millisecond
	t.Cleanup(func() { holdPollInterval = previous })
}

// holdUpdateArgs is updateArgs with --hold mode after its --hold none.
func holdUpdateArgs(addr, mode string, extra ...string) []string {
	return append(append(updateArgs(addr), "--hold", mode), extra...)
}

// requireSignedBy checks that req's token authorizes its update for signer.
func requireSignedBy(t *testing.T, signer *authority.Signer, req *pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd) {
	t.Helper()
	validator := authority.Validator{AllowedAddresses: map[string]bool{signer.Address(): true}, MaxTokenAge: time.Minute}
	if _, err := validator.AuthorizeConsensusParamsUpdate(wire.ConsensusParamsUpdateFromPB(req.GetUpdate()), req.GetAuthorityJws()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the submitted token does not authorize its update: %v", err)
	}
}

// holdLeader is a ConsensusAdmin leader that grants holds. state answers the
// n-th GetConsensusParams (from 1; nil: testConsensusState), prepare the n-th
// PrepareConsensusUpdate, poll the n-th GetConsensusHold (nil: NotFound);
// every request is recorded under mu.
type holdLeader struct {
	pb.UnimplementedConsensusAdminServer
	state   func(n int) *pb.ConsensusParamsState
	prepare func(n int, req *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error)
	poll    func(n int, ref *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error)

	mu        sync.Mutex
	reads     int
	polls     int
	prepared  []*pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest
	released  []string
	submitted []*pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd
	holdIDs   [][]string
}

// holdLeaderView is a copy of what a holdLeader recorded.
type holdLeaderView struct {
	reads, polls int
	prepared     []*pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest
	released     []string
	submitted    []*pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd
	holdIDs      [][]string
}

func (l *holdLeader) GetConsensusParams(context.Context, *emptypb.Empty) (*pb.ConsensusParamsState, error) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.reads++
	if l.state != nil {
		return l.state(l.reads), nil
	}
	return testConsensusState(), nil
}

func (l *holdLeader) PrepareConsensusUpdate(_ context.Context, req *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.prepared = append(l.prepared, req)
	return l.prepare(len(l.prepared), req)
}

func (l *holdLeader) GetConsensusHold(_ context.Context, ref *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.polls++
	if l.poll == nil {
		return nil, status.Error(codes.NotFound, "unknown consensus hold")
	}
	return l.poll(l.polls, ref)
}

func (l *holdLeader) ReleaseConsensusHold(_ context.Context, ref *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.Ack, error) {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.released = append(l.released, ref.GetHoldId())
	return &pb.Ack{}, nil
}

func (l *holdLeader) UpdateConsensusParams(ctx context.Context, req *pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd) (*pb.Ack, error) {
	md, _ := metadata.FromIncomingContext(ctx)
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	l.submitted = append(l.submitted, req)
	l.holdIDs = append(l.holdIDs, md.Get(consensusHoldMetadataKey))
	return &pb.Ack{}, nil
}

func (l *holdLeader) view() holdLeaderView {
	l.mu.Lock()
	defer l.mu.Unlock()
	return holdLeaderView{reads: l.reads, polls: l.polls, prepared: slices.Clone(l.prepared), released: slices.Clone(l.released),
		submitted: slices.Clone(l.submitted), holdIDs: slices.Clone(l.holdIDs)}
}

// TestConsensusUpdateTakesAnIssuanceHold: clarification K5. One signature:
// the draft the hold was taken with is the update submitted, under the hold
// id's metadata, with the requested timeout.
func TestConsensusUpdateTakesAnIssuanceHold(t *testing.T) {
	signer := adminKey(t)
	leader := &holdLeader{prepare: func(_ int, req *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
		return &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-1", Mode: req.GetMode(), PromotionSeq: req.GetDraft().GetUpdate().GetExpectedPromotionSeq(), Ready: true}, nil
	}}
	addr := serveAdminImpl(t, leader)
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := run(context.Background(), holdUpdateArgs(addr, "issuance", "--hold-timeout", "90s"), &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v := leader.view()
	if len(v.prepared) != 1 || v.prepared[0].GetMode() != issuanceHold || v.prepared[0].GetTimeoutMs() != 90_000 {
		t.Fatalf("prepare requests = %v", v.prepared)
	}
	if len(v.submitted) != 1 || !proto.Equal(v.submitted[0], v.prepared[0].GetDraft()) || v.submitted[0].GetUpdate().GetExpectedPromotionSeq() != 12 {
		t.Fatalf("submitted %v, want the draft %v", v.submitted, v.prepared[0].GetDraft())
	}
	if !slices.Equal(v.holdIDs[0], []string{"hold-1"}) || v.polls != 0 || len(v.released) != 0 || v.reads != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("hold metadata %v, polls %d, releases %v, reads %d", v.holdIDs, v.polls, v.released, v.reads)
	}
	requireSignedBy(t, signer, v.submitted[0])
	var result struct{ Status, Hold string }
	if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Bytes(), &result); err != nil || result.Status != "committed" || result.Hold != "issuance" {
		t.Fatalf("result %s, %v", &out, err)
	}
	// An issuance hold reports no drain state, so its progress is the drain
	// gate alone (K10: it is ready once the gate passes).
	if got := holdProgress(&pb.ConsensusHold{Mode: issuanceHold, DrainRefusal: "consensus update requires all cleanup commands to be acknowledged"}); got != "drain gate: consensus update requires all cleanup commands to be acknowledged" {
		t.Fatalf("issuance hold progress = %q", got)
	}
}

// TestConsensusUpdateDrainsThenSignsTheFrozenSeq: spec §10.2. The CLI polls
// until the drained leader reports ready, prints each change of progress,
// and only then signs the update with the frozen promotion_seq.
func TestConsensusUpdateDrainsThenSignsTheFrozenSeq(t *testing.T) {
	fastHoldPolls(t)
	signer := adminKey(t)
	warnings := captureStderr(t)
	leader := &holdLeader{
		state: func(n int) *pb.ConsensusParamsState {
			s := testConsensusState()
			if n > 1 {
				s.PromotionSeq = 14
			}
			return s
		},
		prepare: func(_ int, req *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
			return &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-2", Mode: req.GetMode(), PromotionSeq: 12, DrainRefusal: "consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged",
				Tracks: []*pb.TrackDrain{{IndexerId: 1, PrefixBlockSeq: 4, FrontierBlockSeq: 5, InFlightBlocks: []uint64{5}}}}, nil
		},
		poll: func(n int, _ *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
			if n < 3 {
				return &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-2", Mode: drainHold, PromotionSeq: 13, DrainRefusal: "consensus update requires all cleanup commands to be acknowledged",
					Tracks: []*pb.TrackDrain{{IndexerId: 1, PrefixBlockSeq: 5, FrontierBlockSeq: 5}}}, nil
			}
			return &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-2", Mode: drainHold, PromotionSeq: 14, Ready: true,
				Tracks: []*pb.TrackDrain{{IndexerId: 1, PrefixBlockSeq: 5, FrontierBlockSeq: 5}}}, nil
		},
	}
	addr := serveAdminImpl(t, leader)
	if err := run(context.Background(), holdUpdateArgs(addr, "drain"), &bytes.Buffer{}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v := leader.view()
	if len(v.prepared) != 1 || v.prepared[0].GetMode() != drainHold || v.prepared[0].GetTimeoutMs() != uint64((10*time.Minute)/time.Millisecond) ||
		v.prepared[0].GetDraft().GetUpdate().GetExpectedPromotionSeq() != 12 {
		t.Fatalf("prepare requests = %v", v.prepared)
	}
	if v.polls != 3 || v.reads != 2 || len(v.submitted) != 1 || len(v.released) != 0 || !slices.Equal(v.holdIDs[0], []string{"hold-2"}) {
		t.Fatalf("leader saw %+v", v)
	}
	final := v.submitted[0]
	if final.GetUpdate().GetExpectedPromotionSeq() != 14 || proto.Equal(final, v.prepared[0].GetDraft()) {
		t.Fatalf("final update = %v; want it signed afresh at promotion_seq 14", final)
	}
	requireSignedBy(t, signer, final)
	out := warnings.String()
	for _, want := range []string{
		"took a consensus hold of mode drain on the leader (hold id hold-2",
		"waiting for the leader's drain hold: drain gate: consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged; indexer 1 prefix 4 frontier 5 in flight [5]",
		"waiting for the leader's drain hold: drain gate: consensus update requires all cleanup commands to be acknowledged; indexer 1 prefix 5 frontier 5",
		"the leader drained at promotion_seq 14; signing the update",
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Fatalf("stderr lacks %q:\n%s", want, out)
		}
	}
	if strings.Count(out, "waiting for the leader's drain hold") != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("progress must be printed once per change:\n%s", out)
	}
}

// TestConsensusUpdateRetriesPrepareWhenAPromotionLandsFirst: a promotion that
// lands between the CLI's read and the leader's check is absorbed by
// re-signing the draft, a bounded number of times.
func TestConsensusUpdateRetriesPrepareWhenAPromotionLandsFirst(t *testing.T) {
	signer := adminKey(t)
	overtaken := status.Error(codes.FailedPrecondition, "consensus parameter update expected_promotion_seq 12 does not match the current promotion sequence 13")
	leader := &holdLeader{
		state: func(n int) *pb.ConsensusParamsState {
			s := testConsensusState()
			if n > 1 {
				s.PromotionSeq = 13
			}
			return s
		},
		prepare: func(n int, req *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
			if n == 1 {
				return nil, overtaken
			}
			return &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-3", Mode: req.GetMode(), PromotionSeq: 13, Ready: true}, nil
		},
	}
	addr := serveAdminImpl(t, leader)
	if err := run(context.Background(), holdUpdateArgs(addr, "issuance"), &bytes.Buffer{}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v := leader.view()
	if len(v.prepared) != 2 || v.reads != 2 || len(v.submitted) != 1 ||
		v.prepared[0].GetDraft().GetUpdate().GetExpectedPromotionSeq() != 12 || v.prepared[1].GetDraft().GetUpdate().GetExpectedPromotionSeq() != 13 ||
		!proto.Equal(v.submitted[0], v.prepared[1].GetDraft()) {
		t.Fatalf("leader saw %+v", v)
	}
	requireSignedBy(t, signer, v.submitted[0])

	restless := &holdLeader{prepare: func(int, *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) { return nil, overtaken }}
	err := run(context.Background(), holdUpdateArgs(serveAdminImpl(t, restless), "drain"), &bytes.Buffer{})
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "take consensus hold") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "does not match the current promotion sequence") {
		t.Fatalf("a leader that keeps moving = %v", err)
	}
	if v := restless.view(); len(v.prepared) != holdPrepareAttempts || len(v.submitted) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("restless leader saw %d prepares and %d updates", len(v.prepared), len(v.submitted))
	}
}

// TestConsensusUpdateReleasesTheHoldOnEveryEarlyExit: every exit between the
// hold and the submit releases the hold and submits nothing.
func TestConsensusUpdateReleasesTheHoldOnEveryEarlyExit(t *testing.T) {
	notReady := func(id string) *pb.ConsensusHold {
		return &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: id, Mode: drainHold, PromotionSeq: 12, DrainRefusal: "consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged"}
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name  string
		args  func(addr string) []string
		state func(n int) *pb.ConsensusParamsState
		hold  *pb.ConsensusHold
		poll  func(n int, ref *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error)
		want  string
	}{
		{name: "parameters changed while draining", args: func(addr string) []string { return holdUpdateArgs(addr, "drain") },
			state: func(n int) *pb.ConsensusParamsState {
				s := testConsensusState()
				if n > 1 {
					s.Epoch = 8
				}
				return s
			},
			hold: notReady("hold-4"),
			poll: func(int, *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
				return &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-4", Mode: drainHold, PromotionSeq: 12, Ready: true}, nil
			},
			want: "consensus parameters changed while the leader drained (epoch 7 -> 8)"},
		{name: "never ready", args: func(addr string) []string {
			return holdUpdateArgs(addr, "drain", "--timeout", "150ms", "--hold-timeout", "150ms")
		},
			hold: notReady("hold-5"),
			poll: func(int, *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) { return notReady("hold-5"), nil },
			want: "the consensus hold was not ready within --timeout plus --hold-timeout"},
		{name: "hold ended", args: func(addr string) []string { return holdUpdateArgs(addr, "drain") },
			hold: notReady("hold-6"),
			want: "the consensus hold ended before it was ready"},
		{name: "issuance hold froze another sequence", args: func(addr string) []string { return holdUpdateArgs(addr, "issuance") },
			hold: &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-7", Mode: issuanceHold, PromotionSeq: 11, Ready: true},
			want: "the issuance hold froze promotion_seq 11, not the 12 the update is signed with"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			fastHoldPolls(t)
			_ = adminKey(t)
			_ = captureStderr(t)
			hold := tc.hold
			leader := &holdLeader{state: tc.state, poll: tc.poll,
				prepare: func(int, *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) { return hold, nil }}
			err := run(context.Background(), tc.args(serveAdminImpl(t, leader)), &bytes.Buffer{})
			if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.want) {
				t.Fatalf("run = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
			if v := leader.view(); !slices.Equal(v.released, []string{hold.GetHoldId()}) || len(v.submitted) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("released %v, submitted %d", v.released, len(v.submitted))
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestConsensusUpdateHoldUnimplementedNamesHoldNone: a leader that predates

func TestConsensusUpdateHoldUnimplementedNamesHoldNone(t *testing.T) {

	for _, args := range [][]string{

// TestConsensusUpdateHoldNoneKeepsTodaysFlow: --hold none reads once,
// submits once, takes no hold and sends no hold metadata.
func TestConsensusUpdateHoldNoneKeepsTodaysFlow(t *testing.T) {
	_ = adminKey(t)
	leader := &holdLeader{prepare: func(int, *pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
		return nil, status.Error(codes.Internal, "no hold expected")
	}}
	addr := serveAdminImpl(t, leader)
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := run(context.Background(), updateArgs(addr), &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	v := leader.view()
	if len(v.prepared) != 0 || v.polls != 0 || v.reads != 1 || len(v.submitted) != 1 || len(v.holdIDs[0]) != 0 || len(v.released) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("leader saw %+v", v)
	}
	if strings.Contains(out.String(), `"hold"`) {
		t.Fatalf("an update without a hold reports one: %s", &out)
	}
}

func TestConsensusUpdateRejectsABadHoldFlag(t *testing.T) {
	_ = adminKey(t)
	impl := &adminTestServer{}
	addr := startAdminServer(t, impl)
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		args []string
		want string
	}{
		{holdUpdateArgs(addr, "sometimes"), "--hold must be none, issuance or drain"},
		{holdUpdateArgs(addr, "drain", "--hold-timeout", "0s"), "--hold-timeout must be positive"},
		{append(updateArgs(addr), "--hold-timeout", "1m"), "--hold-timeout is only used with --hold issuance or --hold drain"},
		{[]string{"consensus", "hold-status", "--address", addr}, "--hold-id is required"},
		{[]string{"consensus", "hold-release", "--address", addr}, "--hold-id is required"},
	} {
		if err := run(context.Background(), tc.args, &bytes.Buffer{}); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.want) {
			t.Fatalf("%v: %v, want %q", tc.args, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
	if impl.reads.Load() != 0 || impl.probes.Load() != 0 || impl.writes.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("flag validation contacted the node")
	}
}

func TestConsensusHoldMetadataKeyMatchesTheServer(t *testing.T) {
	if consensusHoldMetadataKey != server.ConsensusHoldMetadataKey {
		t.Fatalf("CLI key %q, server key %q", consensusHoldMetadataKey, server.ConsensusHoldMetadataKey)
	}
}

func TestHoldStatusAndHoldReleaseUseRealGRPC(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv(authorityPrivateKeyEnv, "")
	want := &pb.ConsensusHold{HoldId: "hold-9", Mode: drainHold, RaftTerm: 3, PromotionSeq: 21, ExpiresUnixMs: 1_800_000_000_000,
		DrainRefusal: "consensus update requires all promotions to be acknowledged",
		Tracks:       []*pb.TrackDrain{{IndexerId: 0, PrefixBlockSeq: 8, FrontierBlockSeq: 9, InFlightBlocks: []uint64{9}}}}
	leader := &holdLeader{poll: func(_ int, ref *pb.ConsensusHoldRef) (*pb.ConsensusHold, error) {
		if ref.GetHoldId() != "hold-9" {
			return nil, status.Error(codes.NotFound, "unknown consensus hold")
		}
		return want, nil
	}}
	addr := serveAdminImpl(t, leader)
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := run(context.Background(), []string{"consensus", "hold-status", "--address", addr, "--hold-id", "hold-9"}, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var got pb.ConsensusHold
	if err := protojson.Unmarshal(out.Bytes(), &got); err != nil || !proto.Equal(&got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("hold-status = %s, %v", &out, err)
	}
	if err := run(context.Background(), []string{"consensus", "hold-status", "--address", addr, "--hold-id", "other"}, &bytes.Buffer{}); status.Code(err) != codes.NotFound {
		t.Fatalf("an unknown hold = %v, want NotFound", err)
	}
	out.Reset()
	if err := run(context.Background(), []string{"consensus", "hold-release", "--address", addr, "--hold-id", "hold-9"}, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var released struct {
		HoldID string `json:"hold_id"`
		Status string `json:"status"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Bytes(), &released); err != nil || released.HoldID != "hold-9" || released.Status != "released" ||
		!slices.Equal(leader.view().released, []string{"hold-9"}) {
		t.Fatalf("hold-release = %s, %v; leader released %v", &out, err, leader.view().released)
	}
	old := startAdminServer(t, &adminTestServer{})
	for _, op := range []string{"hold-status", "hold-release"} {
		if err := run(context.Background(), []string{"consensus", op, "--address", old, "--hold-id", "hold-9"}, &bytes.Buffer{}); err == nil || err.Error() != consensusHoldsUnsupportedMessage {
			t.Fatalf("%s against an old leader = %v", op, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestCLIConsensusUpdateHoldsThroughServerAndFSM: the default drain hold
// against the production server and FSM. An idle network is drained at once:
// the CLI takes the hold, signs at the frozen sequence, submits under the
// hold, the commit ends it, and nothing but the update reaches the log.
func TestCLIConsensusUpdateHoldsThroughServerAndFSM(t *testing.T) {
	a := adminKey(t)
	params := fsm.Params{NetworkID: "cli-hold-network", SchemaSnapshotID: "cli-schema", ExecutorProfileID: "cli-profile",
		AuthorityAddresses: []string{a.Address()}, MaxWriters: 1}
	state, err := fsm.New(params)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	executor := payloadexec.New(params.NetworkID, payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.admin", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "value", Type: "UInt64"}}})
	genesis, err := executor.GenesisSnapshot(0, params.SchemaSnapshotID, params.ExecutorProfileID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := state.ConfigureGenesis(genesis); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	encodedGenesis, err := wire.Encode(wire.Command{PublishSafeSnapshot: &wire.PublishSafeSnapshot{Manifest: genesis}})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if result := state.Apply(&raft.Log{Index: 1, Term: 1, Type: raft.LogCommand, Data: encodedGenesis}); result != (fsm.Applied{}) {
		t.Fatalf("publish genesis: %v", result)
	}
	node := &integrationConsensusNode{state: state, index: 1}
	node.leader.Store(true)
	address, _ := startProductionAdminServer(t, node, server.Config{NodeID: "arbiter-under-test", ApplyTimeout: time.Second,
		ConsensusUpdatesEnabled: true, ConsensusAdminMaxTokenAge: 5 * time.Minute}, "")
	warnings := captureStderr(t)
	var out bytes.Buffer
	if err := run(context.Background(), []string{"consensus", "update", "--address", address, "--expected-epoch", "0",
		"--authority", a.Address(), "--max-writers", "3"}, &out); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if node.applies.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d entries applied, want the update alone", node.applies.Load())
	}
	view, err := state.ConsensusParamsView()
	if err != nil || view.Epoch != 1 || view.Current.MaxWriters != 3 || view.PromotionSeq != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("committed view = %+v, %v", view, err)
	}
	if text := warnings.String(); !strings.Contains(text, "took a consensus hold of mode drain") || strings.Contains(text, "waiting for") || strings.Contains(text, "released consensus hold") {
		t.Fatalf("stderr:\n%s", text)
	}
	var result struct{ Status, Hold string }
	if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Bytes(), &result); err != nil || result.Status != "committed" || result.Hold != "drain" {
		t.Fatalf("result %s, %v", &out, err)
	}
	client, closeAdmin, err := dialAdmin(address)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer closeAdmin()
	current, err := client.GetConsensusParams(t.Context(), &emptypb.Empty{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	next, err := authority.NormalizeConsensusParamsUpdate(arbiter.ConsensusParamsUpdate{NetworkID: current.GetNetworkId(), GenesisSnapshotID: current.GetGenesisSnapshotId(),
		ExpectedEpoch: 1, PreviousParamsDigest: current.GetParamsDigest(), ExpectedPromotionSeq: 0, AuthorityAddresses: []string{a.Address()}, MaxWriters: 4})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	token, err := a.SignConsensusParamsUpdate(next)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	hold, err := client.PrepareConsensusUpdate(t.Context(), &pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest{Mode: issuanceHold,
		Draft: &pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd{Update: wire.ConsensusParamsUpdateToPB(next), AuthorityJws: token}})
	if err != nil || !hold.GetReady() {
		t.Fatalf("the next hold = %v, %v; the first hold must have ended with its commit", hold, err)
	}
	if _, err := client.ReleaseConsensusHold(t.Context(), &pb.ConsensusHoldRef{HoldId: hold.GetHoldId()}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

```go
// parseHoldMode maps --hold to the RPC's mode; none is UNSPECIFIED.
func parseHoldMode(name string) (pb.ConsensusHoldMode, error) {
	switch name {
	case "none":
		return pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_UNSPECIFIED, nil
	case "issuance":
		return pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_ISSUANCE, nil
	case "drain":
		return pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_DRAIN, nil
	}
	return pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_UNSPECIFIED, errors.New("--hold must be none, issuance or drain")
}

// holdModeName is --hold's spelling of mode, "" for none.
func holdModeName(mode pb.ConsensusHoldMode) string {
	switch mode {
	case pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_ISSUANCE:
		return "issuance"
	case pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_DRAIN:
		return "drain"
	}
	return ""
}

// consensusHoldSession is the consensus hold one consensus update took.
type consensusHoldSession struct {
	client    pb.ConsensusAdminClient
	ctx       context.Context
	mode      pb.ConsensusHoldMode
	id        string
	hold      *pb.ConsensusHold
	state     *pb.ConsensusParamsState
	draft     *pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd
	sign      func(uint64) (*pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd, error)
	submitted bool
}

// takeConsensusHold asks the leader for a hold of mode authorized by draft.
// A promotion that lands between the CLI's read and the leader's check
// leaves the draft stale; the CLI then reads the parameters again, requires
// the same epoch and digest, signs the draft at the new sequence and asks
// again, at most holdPrepareAttempts times in all.
func takeConsensusHold(ctx context.Context, client pb.ConsensusAdminClient, address string, mode pb.ConsensusHoldMode, timeout time.Duration,
	state *pb.ConsensusParamsState, draft *pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd, sign func(uint64) (*pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd, error)) (*consensusHoldSession, error) {
	for attempt := 1; ; attempt++ {
		hold, err := client.PrepareConsensusUpdate(ctx, &pb.PrepareConsensusUpdateRequest{Mode: mode, Draft: draft, TimeoutMs: uint64(timeout / time.Millisecond)})
		if err == nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "took a consensus hold of mode %s on the leader (hold id %s, expires %s)\n", holdModeName(mode), hold.GetHoldId(),
				time.UnixMilli(int64(hold.GetExpiresUnixMs())).UTC().Format(time.RFC3339))
			return &consensusHoldSession{client: client, ctx: ctx, mode: mode, id: hold.GetHoldId(), hold: hold, state: state, draft: draft, sign: sign}, nil
		}
		if status.Code(err) == codes.Unimplemented {
			return nil, errors.New(consensusHoldsUnsupportedMessage)
		}
		if !promotionOvertookDraft(err) || attempt == holdPrepareAttempts {
			return nil, rpcError("take consensus hold", address, err)
		}
		current, readErr := client.GetConsensusParams(ctx, &emptypb.Empty{})
		if readErr != nil {
			return nil, rpcError("read consensus parameters", address, readErr)
		}
		if current.GetEpoch() != state.GetEpoch() || current.GetParamsDigest() != state.GetParamsDigest() {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("consensus parameters changed before the hold was taken (epoch %d -> %d); run consensus show and review them before retrying",
				state.GetEpoch(), current.GetEpoch())
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "a promotion moved promotion_seq to %d before the hold was taken; signing the draft again\n", current.GetPromotionSeq())
		if draft, err = sign(current.GetPromotionSeq()); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}
}

// promotionOvertookDraft reports the leader's refusal of a draft signed at a
// promotion sequence a promotion has since moved: its precondition check, or
// the issuance hold's own re-check under the lease.
func promotionOvertookDraft(err error) bool {
	message := status.Convert(err).Message()
	return status.Code(err) == codes.FailedPrecondition &&
		(strings.Contains(message, "does not match the current promotion sequence") || strings.Contains(message, "while the hold was taken"))
}

// await polls the hold until the leader reports it ready, printing each
// change of progress to stderr, and returns the update to submit: in
// issuance mode the draft the hold froze, in drain mode the update signed
// afresh with the drained leader's promotion_seq.
func (h *consensusHoldSession) await(ctx context.Context, address string) (*pb.UpdateConsensusParamsCmd, error) {
	last := ""
	for !h.hold.GetReady() {
		if progress := holdProgress(h.hold); progress != last {
			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "waiting for the leader's %s hold: %s\n", holdModeName(h.mode), progress)
			last = progress
		}
		select {
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("the consensus hold was not ready within --timeout plus --hold-timeout (%s)", last)
		case <-time.After(holdPollInterval):
		}
		hold, err := h.client.GetConsensusHold(ctx, &pb.ConsensusHoldRef{HoldId: h.id})
		switch {
		case status.Code(err) == codes.NotFound:
			return nil, errors.New("the consensus hold ended before it was ready: it expired at the leader's limit or leadership changed; run the update again")
		// gRPC propagates the deadline, so the leader can answer
		// DeadlineExceeded a moment before ctx.Err() is set here.
		case err != nil && (ctx.Err() != nil || status.Code(err) == codes.DeadlineExceeded):
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("the consensus hold was not ready within --timeout plus --hold-timeout (%s)", last)
		case err != nil:
			return nil, rpcError("read consensus hold", address, err)
		}
		h.hold = hold
	}
	frozen := h.hold.GetPromotionSeq()
	if h.mode == pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_ISSUANCE {
		if signed := h.draft.GetUpdate().GetExpectedPromotionSeq(); frozen != signed {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("the issuance hold froze promotion_seq %d, not the %d the update is signed with; run the update again", frozen, signed)
		}
		return h.draft, nil
	}
	current, err := h.client.GetConsensusParams(ctx, &emptypb.Empty{})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, rpcError("read consensus parameters", address, err)
	}
	switch {
	case current.GetEpoch() != h.state.GetEpoch() || current.GetParamsDigest() != h.state.GetParamsDigest():
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("consensus parameters changed while the leader drained (epoch %d -> %d); run consensus show and review them before retrying",
			h.state.GetEpoch(), current.GetEpoch())
	case current.GetPromotionSeq() != frozen:
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("promotion_seq is %d, not the %d the drained hold reported; run the update again", current.GetPromotionSeq(), frozen)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "the leader drained at promotion_seq %d; signing the update\n", frozen)
	return h.sign(frozen)
}

// releaseUnlessSubmitted releases the hold on an exit before the submit. It
// runs detached from the operation's context, which may already be over.
func (h *consensusHoldSession) releaseUnlessSubmitted() {
	if h == nil || h.submitted {
		return
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(h.ctx), holdReleaseTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	if _, err := h.client.ReleaseConsensusHold(ctx, &pb.ConsensusHoldRef{HoldId: h.id}); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "WARNING: releasing consensus hold %s failed: %v; it ends at the leader's limit, or run consensus hold-release\n", h.id, err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "released consensus hold %s\n", h.id)
}

// holdProgress summarizes a hold that is not ready: the drain gate's
// refusal, then for a drain hold per track (after the tracks activation) or
// globally its prefix, frontier and in-flight blocks. An issuance hold
// records no frontier and reports no drain state (consensus.proto), so the
// drain gate is all it waits for.
func holdProgress(hold *pb.ConsensusHold) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if refusal := hold.GetDrainRefusal(); refusal != "" {
		b.WriteString("drain gate: " + refusal)
	} else {
		b.WriteString("drain gate passes")
	}
	if hold.GetMode() == pb.ConsensusHoldMode_CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_ISSUANCE {
		return b.String()
	}
	if tracks := hold.GetTracks(); len(tracks) > 0 {
		for _, tr := range tracks {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; indexer %d prefix %d frontier %d", tr.GetIndexerId(), tr.GetPrefixBlockSeq(), tr.GetFrontierBlockSeq())
			if tr.GetQuarantined() {
				b.WriteString(" (quarantined)")
			}
			if blocks := tr.GetInFlightBlocks(); len(blocks) > 0 {
				fmt.Fprintf(&b, " in flight %v", blocks)
			}
		}
		return b.String()
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "; prefix %d frontier %d", hold.GetGlobalPrefixBlockSeq(), hold.GetGlobalFrontierBlockSeq())
	if blocks := hold.GetInFlightBlocks(); len(blocks) > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " in flight %v", blocks)
	}
	return b.String()
}

// holdRPCError is rpcError, naming an older leader's Unimplemented.
func holdRPCError(operation, address string, err error) error {
	if status.Code(err) == codes.Unimplemented {
		return errors.New(consensusHoldsUnsupportedMessage)
	}
	return rpcError(operation, address, err)
}
```

append to the section `## Stage-3 reads and consensus holds` (Task 7):

```markdown
**Consensus holds.** Every consensus update is bound to an exact `expected_promotion_seq`, and while promotions are issued an update signed a moment ago is refused (`consensus update expected_promotion_seq differs from current promotion sequence`). A consensus hold removes that race on the leader, outside consensus. `ConsensusAdmin.PrepareConsensusUpdate{mode, draft, timeout_ms}` takes one: the draft is an authority-signed `UpdateConsensusParamsCmd`, checked exactly as `UpdateConsensusParams` checks an update (token shape, authority, `max_token_age`, the epoch, digest and promotion-sequence preconditions) and never proposed. Refusals come first and cost nothing on the log: `consensus parameter updates are disabled; …` when `consensus_updates_enabled` is false, `consensus hold mode is required`, `consensus hold draft is required`, the update's own authorization refusals, and `a consensus hold is already active on this leader` (one hold at a time). The leader then waits for any promotion issuance in flight, crosses one read barrier and records the hold. The answer carries the hold id (random, 128 bits as 32 hex characters, a bearer capability: `GetConsensusHold{hold_id}` and `ReleaseConsensusHold{hold_id}` need only it), the Raft term, the expiry, `ready`, the drain gate's refusal (`drain_refusal`) and, for a drain hold, the drain state; an issuance hold records no frontier and leaves the `global_*` fields, `in_flight_blocks` and `tracks` empty. Both hold reads are leader-only: `GetConsensusHold` crosses one read barrier and answers `NotFound` (`unknown consensus hold`) for an id this leader does not hold, including one that has ended, and `ReleaseConsensusHold` answers `Ack` for such an id. An update is submitted under the hold by naming it in the gRPC metadata `arbiter-consensus-hold` (never in the command); a hold that is not this leader's live one is refused (`unknown consensus hold`). The hold ends when its update commits or is refused, on `ReleaseConsensusHold`, at its deadline (`timeout_ms`, capped by `consensus_admin.max_issuance_hold` or `max_drain_mode`; 0 takes the cap), and on a leadership change (a hold of an earlier Raft term is void); an update whose outcome is unknown leaves the hold to expire. In **issuance** mode (`CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_ISSUANCE`) the leader proposes no `RecordPromotionIssued` at all while acknowledgements, publications, cleanups and resends continue; the draft must be signed at the current `promotion_seq` (`promotion_seq moved to N while the hold was taken; sign the update again` otherwise), it is the update to submit, and the hold is ready once the stage-2 drain gate passes (no promotion is issued meanwhile, so the owed acknowledgements and cleanups finish; Plan S3-A clarification K10). Issuance alone can wait until it expires on a block that is half promoted across partitions, because that block's cleanup waits for a publication the hold prevents. In **drain** mode (`CONSENSUS_HOLD_MODE_DRAIN`) the leader records each non-quarantined track's promotion frontier block (before the tracks activation, the global one), keeps issuing every promotion and re-issue of blocks at or below it and refuses only promotions of later blocks; the hold is ready once the stage-2 drain gate passes and every recorded track's prefix reached its frontier, and from then on `promotion_seq` cannot move, so the update is signed with the `promotion_seq` the hold reports. A drain hold taken after the tracks activation reports one `tracks[]` entry per enrolled indexer with the frontier recorded at hold start (0 for a track quarantined then) and nothing global; one taken before it reports `global_prefix_block_seq` and `global_frontier_block_seq`. `tracks[].in_flight_blocks` (before the activation, `in_flight_blocks`) names the blocks still holding the drain. A stuck track with in-flight work never drains: quarantine it first. Holds exist only on a leader running this release; an older one answers `Unimplemented`.

**CLI.** `arbiter-admin consensus update` takes a hold by default (`--hold drain`): it signs the draft, takes the hold, polls it every second (progress and the hold id on stderr), re-reads the parameters, signs the final update with the frozen `promotion_seq`, re-runs its gates and submits under the hold. `--hold issuance` submits the draft instead; `--hold none` keeps the flow without a hold and is the only mode a leader older than this release supports (the CLI says so: `leader does not support consensus holds (arbiter older than this arbiter-admin); upgrade the leader or pass --hold none`; `hold-status` and `hold-release` answer the same). `--hold-timeout` (default `10m`) is requested as the hold's timeout and extends `--timeout` for the whole operation. A draft a promotion overtook before the leader checked it is signed again, at most five times. Any exit before the submit releases the hold. `arbiter-admin consensus hold-status --address LEADER --hold-id ID` prints a hold and `consensus hold-release --address LEADER --hold-id ID` releases one.
```

and in the Metrics section, after the `arbiter_stream_send_dropped_total` paragraph (`:417`), add:

```markdown
Consensus holds add `arbiter_consensus_hold_active{mode}` (`issuance`, `drain`; 0 or 1, both series exported from the start), `arbiter_consensus_holds_total{mode,outcome}` (`committed`, `refused`, `released`, `expired`, `leadership_lost`) and `arbiter_consensus_hold_held_promotions_total` (issuances a hold refused; the orchestrator retries each on every pass, so it counts attempts). All three are process-local and only a leader moves them. A hold that stays active well past the drain an operator expects is the signal to read `consensus hold-status` and quarantine a stuck track.
```

## Task 9: arbiter — consensus-state size and snapshot gauges (S3-A)

Spec §13.1 asks for gauges of the snapshot document size and of the in-memory state size, measured as the uncompacted canonical encoding length, per component, and of restore and snapshot-install time, with L = min(read cap, voter memory / 4, voter volume / 4) driving the alerts; clarification K8 rules out an RPC, so operators read gauges only (contract §4). Today nothing measures either: `writeSnapshot` (`fsm/snapshot.go:167-188`) has no size check, `readSnapshot` refuses a document above `maxSnapshotDocBytes = 1 << 30` (`:59`, `:282-284`) and then allocates it, and raft's own timings go to go-metrics' blackhole sink (`go.mod` carries `armon/go-metrics` and `hashicorp/go-metrics` as indirect dependencies only). This task adds three pieces that change no byte any replica writes: a node-local state-size sample taken by the FSM when a snapshot is persisted or restored, outside the FSM lock (`fsm/state_size.go`); a raftnode wrapper that times serialize, persist, restore and install from outside the FSM, which may not read the clock (`raftnode/snapshot_observer.go`); and the gauges, with `metrics.New` moved before Raft opens so the startup restore is observed.

Notes:
- **No consensus byte changes.** The sample lives in an `atomic.Pointer` field of `FSM`, like `registryWake` a node-local value that is never snapshotted; `Apply` never reads it; `writeSnapshot` and `snapshotDocument` are untouched, so every container stays byte-identical (the frozen `fsm/testdata` goldens, `TestPreActivationHistoryIsByteIdenticalAcrossSignedClaims`, `TestLegacyHistoryIsByteIdenticalAcrossTheLaneRelease` and the pre-tracks golden all run unchanged), and `fsm` still neither reads the clock nor imports `gen/pb` (CI red lines).
- **Where the work runs.** `FSM.Snapshot` serializes under the read lock on raft's FSM goroutine, so its time is an Apply stall; it does no measuring. `fsmSnapshot.Persist` measures after the sink took the bytes, on raft's snapshot goroutine and outside the lock. `Restore` splits the document inside the reader, while its bytes are live for decoding anyway and before the lock is taken, and stores the sample only after the restored state replaced the old one. The scan is one pass over the compact `encoding/json` output that allocates only its 31-entry result; a document it cannot split (the writer never produces one) only costs the sample, never a refused restore.
- **What the numbers mean.** `StateBytes` is the uncompacted canonical encoding length: the JSON document plus the spent-ids dump (in P0 the container minus its 13-byte envelope; after a v21 interned body the document shrinks while this stays the plain length). A component's bytes follow `CountSnapshotEncoding`'s `LifecycleFieldBytes` convention (quoted key, colon, value); the document's braces and commas belong to no component; an omitted member is 0. The component label set is `StateComponents()`: the 30 `snapshotDoc` members in declaration order plus `spent_ids`, pinned by test, so a new document member cannot ship without its label.
- **Not part of `MetricsSnapshot`.** `MetricsSnapshot` is the replicated inventory: replicas and a restored copy compare equal (`TestMetricsSnapshotInventoryAndRestore`, `TestChallengeCounterCoverageDependsOnReplayBoundary` compare whole values with `reflect.DeepEqual`). The sample is node-local and differs between a replica that persisted and one that restored, so the collector reads it through `(*FSM).StateSizeSample` instead, behind an optional interface of its source; the existing fakes do not implement it and keep emitting no size series.
- **Freshness.** The size gauges refresh at each snapshot the node persists (every `raft.snapshot_threshold` entries, checked every `raft.snapshot_interval`; production 8192 and 120 s) and at each restore; they are absent until the first, so an alert needs a `for:` window and never reads an absent series as an empty state. A periodic live walk is deliberately not offered: it would hold the read lock as long as a `json.Marshal`.
- **Timing lives in raftnode.** `observedFSM` embeds `raft.FSM`, so it exposes exactly `Apply`, `Snapshot` and `Restore`; `*fsm.FSM` implements neither `raft.BatchingFSM` nor `raft.ConfigurationStore` (pinned by test), so raft's optional-interface checks see the same FSM. A restore is an install when a sink that the FSM's own `Persist` did not write closed successfully since the last restore; raft's user `Restore` would count as one too, and arbiter never calls it. `metrics.New` only builds a registry, so it moves before `openRaftRuntime`: the startup restore runs inside `raft.NewRaft`, and without the move the most important observation is lost.
- **Failures.** `arbiter_snapshot_failures_total{operation}` is pre-created at 0 for `serialize`, `persist`, `restore` and `install`, so the first failure is an `increase()`. A refused FSM restore, the read cap included, counts under `restore`; when the leader sent that snapshot it also counts under `install`. The timing gauges keep the newest successful value.
- **What the failure counter cannot see.** The `/metrics` listener starts only after Raft is open (Step 12), and the startup restore runs inside `raft.NewRaft`. A startup restore that refuses every local snapshot makes `NewRaft` fail, so `run` returns and the process exits before anything can scrape it: that voter shows as a crash loop with the restore error in its log, never as `arbiter_snapshot_failures_total{operation="restore"}`. A refused newest snapshot that raft survives by restoring an older one is counted before the first scrape, so the series first appears at 1 and `increase()` misses it too. The counter therefore alerts on refused installs and later restores; a voter that can no longer restart is caught before it happens by `ArbiterSnapshotDocNearReadCap` and the state-size alerts, and afterwards by the pod's restart count (README, Step 13).
- **The cap and the writer stay as they are.** `SnapshotDocReadCapBytes` (1 GiB) is exported for the gauge and pinned by test; the writer still never refuses for size (spec §13.1 "it alarms"). Raising the cap is a later, reviewed edit that must reach every voter and rollback image before any document crosses the old cap.
- **Checked while drafting.** Every code block of this task, applied to a `git archive` export of `fb42260` (no worktree), compiles; `go vet ./...` is clean; `go test -race` passes for `fsm` (frozen goldens included), `raftnode`, `metrics`, `cmd/...` and `integration` (2026-10-14). Step 11's expected failure was reproduced against the unwired `cmd/arbiter`.
- **On top of Task 8.** Task 8 (committed before this task) already changed two of the functions this task edits, anchored on the base: `metrics.New` gained, after its single `m.registry.MustRegister(...)` call (`:86`), the three hold collectors, the two zeroed `arbiter_consensus_hold_active{mode}` series and a second `MustRegister` for them, and the `Metrics` struct the three hold fields after `admissionRejects`; `cmd/arbiter/app.go` `run` gained `var holdMetrics server.ConsensusHoldMetrics`, a six-way metrics assignment and `holdMetrics: holdMetrics,` in the `serviceRuntime` literal. This task replaces only the first `MustRegister` call (Step 9) and moves `metrics.New` before `openRaftRuntime` (Step 12), carrying Task 8's lines over unchanged; after both tasks `New` registers its collectors in two calls, this task's extended one first.
- **Raft storage.** `WatchRaftStorage` reads `raft.db` (bolt never shrinks it, so it is the high-water mark the volume holds) and every file under `snapshots/` at scrape time, the inputs of the spec's "document plus trailing log" volume alert.

```go
// contract §4): every snapshot document member in declaration order, then

// label set and the README change with the document, never silently.
func TestStateComponentsListEverySnapshotDocMember(t *testing.T) {
	want := []string{
		"challenge_counters", "next_statement_seq", "next_l3_block_seq", "open_block", "blocks", "statements",
		"pending_rc", "verifications", "promotion_seq", "pending_promotions", "pending_cleanups", "partitions",
		"safe_watermark", "manifests", "safe_parts", "promoted_unsafe", "nodes", "params", "bootstrap_params",
		"consensus_epoch", "consensus_updates", "cleanup_audits", "legacy_promotion_seq", "legacy_promotion_proofs",
		"legacy_cleanup_proofs", "artifact_disposition", "table_registry", "lane_counts", "registration_seqs", "tracks",
		"spent_ids",
	}
	got := StateComponents()
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("StateComponents() = %q\nwant %q", got, want)
	}
	if n := reflect.TypeFor[snapshotDoc]().NumField(); n+1 != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("snapshotDoc has %d members, the label set %d document components", n, len(want)-1)
	}
	got[0] = "mutated"

		t.Fatal("StateComponents must return a copy")
	}
}

// TestSnapshotDocComponentsSplitTheDocument: each member's size is its quoted
// key, colon and value exactly as the writer emitted them (the
// LifecycleFieldBytes convention), an omitted member is 0, and the members
// plus the braces and separating commas are the whole document. Strings that
// carry braces, brackets, commas, colons, quotes, backslashes and the
// characters encoding/json escapes must not split a member.
func TestSnapshotDocComponentsSplitTheDocument(t *testing.T) {
	plain := newTestFSM(t)
	registerActive(t, plain, "s1", arbiter.NodeRoleSNode)
	escaped := newTestFSM(t)
	escaped.st.Params.NetworkID = "net\"},{[]\\,:\u2028<&>"
	for name, f := range map[string]*FSM{"plain": plain, "escaped": escaped, "tracks": newTrackManifestFixture(t).f} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			doc := snapshotJSONDocument(t, f)
			components, err := snapshotDocComponents(doc)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("snapshotDocComponents: %v", err)
			}
			var fields map[string]json.RawMessage
			if err := json.Unmarshal(doc, &fields); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			var sum uint64
			for _, c := range components[:len(components)-1] {
				want := uint64(0)
				if raw, present := fields[c.Component]; present {
					want = uint64(len(`"`+c.Component+`":`) + len(raw))
				}
				if c.Bytes != want {
					t.Errorf("%s = %d bytes, want %d", c.Component, c.Bytes, want)
				}
				sum += c.Bytes
			}
			if last := components[len(components)-1]; last != (StateComponentSize{Component: StateComponentSpentIDs}) {
				t.Errorf("the document scan sized %+v; spent_ids is not a document member", last)
			}
			if want := uint64(len(doc)) - 2 - uint64(len(fields)-1); sum != want {
				t.Fatalf("members sum to %d bytes, want %d of a %d-byte document with %d members", sum, want, len(doc), len(fields))
			}
			switch name {
			case "escaped":
				if !bytes.Contains(doc, []byte(`\u2028`)) || !bytes.Contains(doc, []byte(`\u003c`)) {
					t.Fatal("the fixture string was not escaped by the writer")
				}
			case "tracks":
				if components[slices.Index(StateComponents(), "tracks")].Bytes == 0 {
					t.Fatal("the tracks fixture has no tracks component")
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestSnapshotDocComponentsRefusesMalformedDocuments: the scan refuses what
// it cannot split exactly, never estimates; an empty object is all zeros.
func TestSnapshotDocComponentsRefusesMalformedDocuments(t *testing.T) {
	empty, err := snapshotDocComponents([]byte("{}"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("an empty document: %v", err)
	}
	for _, c := range empty {
		if c.Bytes != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("an empty document sized %s at %d bytes", c.Component, c.Bytes)
		}
	}
	for name, doc := range map[string]string{
		"empty input":        ``,
		"not an object":      `[]`,
		"unterminated":       `{"promotion_seq":1`,
		"unknown member":     `{"nope":1}`,
		"repeated member":    `{"promotion_seq":1,"promotion_seq":2}`,
		"trailing comma":     `{"promotion_seq":1,}`,
		"missing value":      `{"promotion_seq":}`,
		"missing colon":      `{"promotion_seq"}`,
		"unterminated text":  `{"params":"x}`,
		"unbalanced":         `{"params":[1}`,
		"unquoted key":       `{promotion_seq:1}`,
		"the tail as member": `{"spent_ids":1}`,
	} {
		if _, err := snapshotDocComponents([]byte(doc)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: %s was split", name, doc)
		}
	}
}

// TestSnapshotRecordsAStateSizeSample: a persisted snapshot records the
// container it wrote: the document length the read cap governs, the
// spent-ids tail, the whole container, and their sum as the state size.
func TestSnapshotRecordsAStateSizeSample(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTestFSM(t)
	registerActive(t, f, "s1", arbiter.NodeRoleSNode)
	if _, ok := f.StateSizeSample(); ok {
		t.Fatal("a fresh FSM has a state-size sample before any snapshot or restore")
	}
	data := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	got, ok := f.StateSizeSample()
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("a persisted snapshot recorded no state-size sample")
	}
	n := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[5:13])
	tail := uint64(len(data)) - 13 - n
	if got.Source != StateSizeSourceSnapshot || got.DocBytes != n || got.SpentIDsBytes != tail ||
		got.ContainerBytes != uint64(len(data)) || got.StateBytes != n+tail {
		t.Fatalf("sample = %+v for a %d-byte container with a %d-byte document", got, len(data), n)
	}
	if !slices.EqualFunc(got.Components, StateComponents(), func(c StateComponentSize, name string) bool { return c.Component == name }) {
		t.Fatalf("components %+v are not StateComponents() in order", got.Components)
	}
	if last := got.Components[len(got.Components)-1]; last.Bytes != tail {
		t.Fatalf("spent_ids = %d bytes, want the %d-byte tail", last.Bytes, tail)
	}
}

// stateSizeSink is a snapshot sink whose Write or Close fails.
type stateSizeSink struct {
	memSink
	writeErr, closeErr error
}

func (s *stateSizeSink) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
	if s.writeErr != nil {
		return 0, s.writeErr
	}
	return s.memSink.Write(p)
}

func (s *stateSizeSink) Close() error { return s.closeErr }

// TestSnapshotRecordsNothingUntilTheSinkHoldsIt: Snapshot, which stalls
// Apply, measures nothing; a snapshot the sink did not keep records nothing.
func TestSnapshotRecordsNothingUntilTheSinkHoldsIt(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTestFSM(t)
	snap, err := f.Snapshot()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := f.StateSizeSample(); ok {
		t.Fatal("Snapshot alone recorded a sample")
	}
	writeFails := &stateSizeSink{writeErr: errors.New("disk full")}
	if err := snap.Persist(writeFails); err == nil || !writeFails.canceled {
		t.Fatalf("Persist into a failing sink = %v, canceled %v", err, writeFails.canceled)
	}
	if err := snap.Persist(&stateSizeSink{closeErr: errors.New("rename failed")}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("Persist ignored a failed Close")
	}
	if _, ok := f.StateSizeSample(); ok {
		t.Fatal("a snapshot the sink did not keep recorded a sample")
	}
	if err := snap.Persist(&memSink{}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, ok := f.StateSizeSample(); !ok {
		t.Fatal("a persisted snapshot recorded no sample")
	}
}

// TestRestoreRecordsAStateSizeSample: a restore records the container it
// read, with the same numbers the writer's sample had.
func TestRestoreRecordsAStateSizeSample(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTestFSM(t)
	registerActive(t, f, "s1", arbiter.NodeRoleSNode)
	data := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	written, _ := f.StateSizeSample()
	g := restoreInto(t, data)
	got, ok := g.StateSizeSample()
	if !ok || got.Source != StateSizeSourceRestore {
		t.Fatalf("restore sample = %+v, %v", got, ok)
	}
	written.Source = StateSizeSourceRestore
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, written) {
		t.Fatalf("restore sample = %+v\nwant the writer's %+v", got, written)
	}
}

// TestFailedRestoreKeepsThePreviousSample: a refused container, the read cap
// included, leaves the previous sample, and so does one that decodes (and is
// measured) but fails validateRestoredState: the sample is stored only once
// the restored state replaced the old one.
func TestFailedRestoreKeepsThePreviousSample(t *testing.T) {
	data := snapshotBytes(t, newTestFSM(t))
	g := restoreInto(t, data)
	before, ok := g.StateSizeSample()
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("the first restore recorded no sample")
	}
	// TestRestoreRejectsUnpinnedBlocksWithoutConfiguredGenesis's container:
	// readSnapshot accepts it, validateRestoredState refuses it.
	unpinned, _ := recoveryLatchedBlock(t)
	unpinned.st.Blocks[0].PrevSafeSnapshotID = ""
	for name, bad := range map[string][]byte{
		"truncated spent-ids":   data[:len(data)-1],
		"bad magic":             append([]byte("XXXX"), data[4:]...),
		"above the read cap":    {'A', 'F', 'S', 'M', snapshotVersion, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF},
		"refused by validation": snapshotBytes(t, unpinned),
	} {
		if err := g.Restore(io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(bad))); err == nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the container was restored", name)
		}
		if after, _ := g.StateSizeSample(); !reflect.DeepEqual(after, before) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: sample %+v replaced %+v", name, after, before)
		}
	}
}

// TestStateSizeSamplingNeverChangesSnapshotBytes: taking and holding a sample
// changes no snapshot byte, and a restored state writes the same container.
func TestStateSizeSamplingNeverChangesSnapshotBytes(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTestFSM(t)
	registerActive(t, f, "s1", arbiter.NodeRoleSNode)
	first := snapshotBytes(t, f)
	if second := snapshotBytes(t, f); !bytes.Equal(first, second) {
		t.Fatal("a held sample changed the next snapshot")
	}
	if again := snapshotBytes(t, restoreInto(t, first)); !bytes.Equal(again, first) {
		t.Fatal("a restored state with a restore sample wrote different bytes")
	}
}

// TestStateSizeSampleIsRaceFreeAgainstReads: Persist stores samples on raft's
// snapshot goroutine while scrapes read them; run under -race in CI.
func TestStateSizeSampleIsRaceFreeAgainstReads(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTestFSM(t)
	snap, err := f.Snapshot()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		for range 50 {
			_ = snap.Persist(&memSink{})
		}
	}()
	for range 50 {
		_, _ = f.StateSizeSample()
	}
	<-done
}

// TestStateSizeSampleIsDetached: a caller may keep or change the copy it got
// without touching the FSM's sample, and the replicated MetricsSnapshot does
// not carry it (a persisting and a restoring replica must stay equal there).
func TestStateSizeSampleIsDetached(t *testing.T) {
	f := newTestFSM(t)
	before := f.MetricsSnapshot()
	snapshotBytes(t, f)
	got, ok := f.StateSizeSample()
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("a persisted snapshot recorded no sample")
	}
	got.Components[0].Bytes = 0
	if again, _ := f.StateSizeSample(); again.Components[0].Bytes == 0 {
		t.Fatal("StateSizeSample handed out the FSM's own components")
	}
	if after := f.MetricsSnapshot(); !reflect.DeepEqual(after, before) {
		t.Fatalf("a snapshot changed the replicated metrics inventory: %+v, was %+v", after, before)
	}
}

// reviewed change (it must reach every voter and rollback image first), so
```

```go
package fsm

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
)

// Sources of a StateSizeSample.
const (
	// StateSizeSourceSnapshot is a snapshot this process wrote and persisted.
	StateSizeSourceSnapshot = "snapshot"
	// StateSizeSourceRestore is a snapshot this process restored, at startup
	// or from an install.
	StateSizeSourceRestore = "restore"
)

// StateComponentSpentIDs is the component of the spent-ids dump the container
// carries after the JSON document.
const StateComponentSpentIDs = "spent_ids"

// SnapshotDocReadCapBytes is the largest snapshot JSON document Restore
// accepts. The writer never refuses a larger one, so a voter whose state
// outgrows it can no longer restart or install a snapshot; the state-size
// gauges alarm long before (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §13.1). Raising it is a
// reviewed change of maxSnapshotDocBytes that must reach every voter and
// every rollback image before any document crosses the old value.
const SnapshotDocReadCapBytes uint64 = maxSnapshotDocBytes

// StateComponentSize is one component's bytes in a state-size sample.
type StateComponentSize struct {
	Component string
	Bytes     uint64
}

// StateSizeSample measures one snapshot container this process persisted or
// restored (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §13.1). It is node-local: it is never
// part of State or of the snapshot document, Apply never reads it, and taking
// it changes no byte any replica writes. A member's size follows
// CountSnapshotEncoding's LifecycleFieldBytes convention: its quoted key,
// colon and value; the document's braces and separating commas belong to no
// component.
type StateSizeSample struct {
	Source string
	// StateBytes is the uncompacted canonical encoding length of the state:
	// DocBytes plus SpentIDsBytes.
	StateBytes uint64
	// DocBytes is the JSON document's length, which Restore refuses above
	// SnapshotDocReadCapBytes.
	DocBytes uint64
	// SpentIDsBytes is the spent-ids dump's length.
	SpentIDsBytes uint64
	// ContainerBytes is the whole container (a Raft snapshot's state.bin):
	// the 13-byte envelope, the document and the dump.
	ContainerBytes uint64
	// Components lists every StateComponents value in that order; a member
	// the document omits has 0 bytes.
	Components []StateComponentSize
}

var (
	stateComponentNames = snapshotDocMemberNames()
	stateComponentIndex = indexComponents(stateComponentNames)
)

// snapshotDocMemberNames is every snapshotDoc JSON member name in declaration
// order, then StateComponentSpentIDs.
func snapshotDocMemberNames() []string {
	doc := reflect.TypeFor[snapshotDoc]()
	names := make([]string, 0, doc.NumField()+1)
	for i := 0; i < doc.NumField(); i++ {
		field := doc.Field(i)
		if field.PkgPath != "" {
			continue
		}
		if name, _, skip := snapshotJSONField(field); !skip {
			names = append(names, name)
		}
	}
	return append(names, StateComponentSpentIDs)
}

func indexComponents(names []string) map[string]int {
	index := make(map[string]int, len(names))
	for i, name := range names {
		index[name] = i
	}
	return index
}

// StateComponents is the component label set of the state-size gauges: the
// snapshot document's members in declaration order, then spent_ids. It is a
// fixed enum that changes only with the snapshot document itself.
func StateComponents() []string {
	return slices.Clone(stateComponentNames)
}

// StateSizeSample returns the newest state-size sample: of the snapshot this
// process last persisted or restored, whichever came last. ok is false until
// the first. The copy is detached from the FSM.
func (f *FSM) StateSizeSample() (StateSizeSample, bool) {
	s := f.stateSize.Load()
	if s == nil {
		return StateSizeSample{}, false
	}
	out := *s
	out.Components = slices.Clone(s.Components)
	return out, true
}

// containerStateSize measures a container writeSnapshot wrote.
func containerStateSize(data []byte) (StateSizeSample, error) {
	if len(data) < snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes {
		return StateSizeSample{}, fmt.Errorf("state size: container shorter than its %d-byte envelope", snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes)
	}
	n := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(data[5:snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes])
	if n > uint64(len(data)-snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes) {
		return StateSizeSample{}, fmt.Errorf("state size: document length %d exceeds the container", n)
	}
	components, err := snapshotDocComponents(data[snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes : snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes+n])
	if err != nil {
		return StateSizeSample{}, err
	}
	return stateSizeSample(StateSizeSourceSnapshot, n, uint64(len(data))-snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes-n, components), nil
}

// stateSizeSample assembles a sample from a document's member sizes and the
// dump's length.
func stateSizeSample(source string, docBytes, spentIDsBytes uint64, components []StateComponentSize) StateSizeSample {
	components[len(components)-1].Bytes = spentIDsBytes
	return StateSizeSample{
		Source:         source,
		StateBytes:     docBytes + spentIDsBytes,
		DocBytes:       docBytes,
		SpentIDsBytes:  spentIDsBytes,
		ContainerBytes: snapshotEnvelopePrefixBytes + docBytes + spentIDsBytes,
		Components:     components,
	}
}

// snapshotDocComponents splits a snapshot document, the compact encoding/json
// output of snapshotDoc, at its top-level members and sizes each one. It is
// one pass over doc and allocates only the result. A document that is not a
// flat object of known, distinct members is refused, never estimated. The
// spent_ids entry stays 0: the dump is not a document member.
func snapshotDocComponents(doc []byte) ([]StateComponentSize, error) {
	sizes := make([]StateComponentSize, len(stateComponentNames))
	for i, name := range stateComponentNames {
		sizes[i].Component = name
	}
	if len(doc) < 2 || doc[0] != '{' || doc[len(doc)-1] != '}' {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc is not a JSON object")
	}
	end := len(doc) - 1
	for i := 1; i < end; {
		start := i
		if doc[i] != '"' {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc member at byte %d does not start with a key", i)
		}
		closing := bytes.IndexByte(doc[i+1:end], '"')
		if closing < 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc key at byte %d is unterminated", i)
		}
		key := doc[i+1 : i+1+closing]
		i += closing + 2
		if i >= end || doc[i] != ':' {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc key %q has no value", key)
		}
		valueEnd, err := snapshotDocValueEnd(doc, i+1, end)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc member %q: %w", key, err)
		}
		j, known := stateComponentIndex[string(key)]
		if !known || j == len(sizes)-1 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc has unknown member %q", key)
		}
		if sizes[j].Bytes != 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc repeats member %q", key)
		}
		sizes[j].Bytes = uint64(valueEnd - start)
		i = valueEnd
		if i < end {
			// valueEnd stopped at a separating comma.
			i++
			if i == end {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("state size: snapshot doc ends with a comma")
			}
		}
	}
	return sizes, nil
}

// snapshotDocValueEnd returns the index just past the JSON value that starts
// at doc[from], scanning no further than end: the first comma outside every
// string, object and array, or end itself.
func snapshotDocValueEnd(doc []byte, from, end int) (int, error) {
	depth, inString, escaped := 0, false, false
	i := from
	for ; i < end; i++ {
		c := doc[i]
		if inString {
			switch {
			case escaped:
				escaped = false
			case c == '\\':
				escaped = true
			case c == '"':
				inString = false
			}
			continue
		}
		switch c {
		case '"':
			inString = true
		case '{', '[':
			depth++
		case '}', ']':
			if depth == 0 {
				return 0, fmt.Errorf("unbalanced %q at byte %d", c, i)
			}
			depth--
		case ',':
			if depth == 0 {
				if i == from {
					return 0, fmt.Errorf("empty value at byte %d", i)
				}
				return i, nil
			}
		}
	}
	if inString || depth != 0 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("value at byte %d is unterminated", from)
	}
	if i == from {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("empty value at byte %d", from)
	}
	return i, nil
}

// countingReader counts the bytes the spent-ids restore consumes.
type countingReader struct {
	r io.Reader
	n uint64
}

func (c *countingReader) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
	n, err := c.r.Read(p)
	c.n += uint64(n)
	return n, err
}
```
